  • Sharing: Viewer, Commenter, Editor roles. Link-sharing settings aur specific emails.
  • Protected ranges: Data > Protect sheets and ranges. Kuch cells sirf kuch users edit kar sakte hain.
  • Version history: File > Version history. Purane version restore kar sakte ho.
  • Apps Script: Extensions > Apps Script. JavaScript me. Custom menu, triggers (time-driven) aur email automation.
  • Common functions: FILTER, UNIQUE, SORT, SPLIT, XLOOKUP aur VLOOKUP chalte hain.

Example

text
Data: A=country, B=game, C=rake   (A1:C100 with header)
=QUERY(A1:C100, "select A, sum(C) where B='Cash' group by A order by sum(C) desc label sum(C) 'Cash Rake'", 1)
=IMPORTRANGE("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/FILE_ID", "Data!A1:C100")
=ARRAYFORMULA(IF(A2:A="", "", C2:C*0.82))
=GOOGLEFINANCE("CURRENCY:USDINR")

QUERY me last argument 1 ka matlab data me ek header row hai.

javascript
function onOpen() {
  SpreadsheetApp.getUi().createMenu('Report')
    .addItem('Stamp date', 'stampDate').addToUi();
}
function stampDate() {
  SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSheet().getRange('B1').setValue(new Date());
}

Ye sheet khulte hi "Report" menu add karta hai.

Common mistakes

  • QUERY me text criteria ko single quotes me na likhna, aur date ko date '2026-01-01' format me na dena.
  • IMPORTRANGE ko access na dena, #REF! aata hai.
  • Link sharing "Anyone with the link: Editor" chhod dena. Sensitive data leak ho sakta hai.
  • ARRAYFORMULA me blank rows handle na karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. QUERY aur FILTER me kya fark?
    A. QUERY me SQL jaisa select, group by, order by milta hai. FILTER sirf rows filter karta hai.
  • Q. Do Sheets files ko kaise jodoge?
    A. IMPORTRANGE se. Ek baar access allow karna hota hai.

Yaad rakho

Sheets me QUERY aur ARRAYFORMULA sabse bade hathiyar hain. Sharing permissions soch ke do.

SQL 37 topics

SQL-01Relational database basicsBasicMust Know

Data tables me rows aur columns me store hota hai, aur keys se tables aapas me jude hote hain.

Simple me samjho

Relational database ek Excel workbook jaisa hai, lekin strict rules ke saath. Har sheet ek table hai, aur sheets ko ID se link kiya jaata hai. Isse same data baar baar copy nahi karna padta.

Key points

  • Table: Ek entity ka data, jaise players, transactions, tables.
  • Row (record): Ek single item, jaise ek player ya ek deposit.
  • Column (field): Ek attribute with fixed data type, jaise country, balance.
  • Primary key (PK): Har row ko unique pehchaan deta hai. NULL ya duplicate nahi ho sakta.
  • Foreign key (FK): Ek table ka column jo doosre table ke PK ko point karta hai. Isse integrity milti hai, jaise transactions.player_id -> players.id.
  • Relationships: One-to-many (ek player, kai deposits), many-to-many (players aur tournaments, beech me bridge table).
  • Schema: Tables ka logical group ya blueprint. PostgreSQL me public.players jaisa schema.table use hota hai.
  • ER diagram: Tables aur unke relationships ka picture. Boxes = tables, lines = FK links.
  • OLTP: Live app ka database. Chhoti fast reads/writes, normalized tables, jaise game ke transactions.
  • OLAP: Analytics warehouse. Badi scans aur aggregations, denormalized (star schema), jaise BigQuery, Redshift.

Example

sql
CREATE TABLE players (
  id      INT PRIMARY KEY,
  name    TEXT NOT NULL,
  country TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE deposits (
  id        INT PRIMARY KEY,
  player_id INT REFERENCES players(id),  -- foreign key
  amount    NUMERIC(12,2)
);
text
players            deposits
id | name | country    id | player_id | amount
1  | Amit | IN         10 | 1         | 100.00
2  | Sara | US         11 | 1         | 50.00

Ek player (id 1) ke 2 deposits hain: yeh one-to-many hai. player_id = 99 insert karoge to FK error aayega.

Common mistakes

  • Analytics queries seedha OLTP production DB par chalana. Heavy query live game slow kar sakti hai; replica ya warehouse use karo.
  • FK constraint ko hamesha enforced maan lena. Warehouses me aksar FK enforce nahi hota, orphan rows ho sakti hain.
  • Natural key (email) ko PK bana dena. Email change hota hai; surrogate id safer hai.
  • Table ka grain (ek row = kya?) samjhe bina query likhna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Primary key aur unique key me kya farak hai?
    A. PK table me sirf ek hota hai aur NULL nahi hota. Unique key kai ho sakti hain aur (usually) NULL allow hoti hai.
  • Q. OLTP vs OLAP?
    A. OLTP = daily transactions, fast small writes, normalized. OLAP = reporting aur analysis, large reads, denormalized.

Yaad rakho

PK = row ki pehchaan, FK = doosre table ka rasta, aur hamesha pehle table ka grain pata karo.

SQL-02SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMITBasicMust Know

SELECT se columns chunte hain, WHERE se rows filter karte hain, ORDER BY se sort aur LIMIT se top rows lete hain.

Simple me samjho

Table ek badi list hai. SELECT batata hai kaunse columns chahiye. WHERE batata hai kaunsi rows chahiye, ORDER BY sort karta hai, LIMIT sirf pehli kuch rows deta hai.

Key points

  • SELECT: Columns choose karo. SELECT * exploration ke liye theek, production queries me columns likho.
  • WHERE: Row-level filter. Operators: =, <> (ya !=), <, >, <=, >=, AND, OR, NOT.
  • BETWEEN: x BETWEEN 100 AND 1000 dono ends inclusive hai.
  • IN: country IN ('IN','US') kai OR ka short form.
  • LIKE: Pattern match. % = kuch bhi (0 ya zyada chars), _ = exactly ek char. 'Am%' = Am se shuru.
  • DISTINCT: Duplicate rows hatata hai. SELECT DISTINCT country unique countries deta hai.
  • Alias: balance AS chips column ko naam deta hai. Table alias: FROM players p.
  • ORDER BY: Default ASC. DESC ulta. Kai columns: ORDER BY country, balance DESC.
  • LIMIT: PostgreSQL/MySQL me LIMIT n. SQL Server me TOP n. Oracle me FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY.
  • Precedence: AND pehle chalta hai OR se. Mix karo to brackets lagao.

Example

sql
SELECT name, balance AS chips
FROM players
WHERE country IN ('IN','US')
  AND balance BETWEEN 100 AND 1000
ORDER BY balance DESC
LIMIT 2;
text
name | chips
Amar | 750
Amit | 500

Sara (1200) BETWEEN se bahar hai, Ravi (0) bhi, Anna country DE hai. Sirf Amar aur Amit bache.

Common mistakes

  • LIMIT ko ORDER BY ke bina use karna. Bina order ke kaunsi rows aayengi, guaranteed nahi.
  • a = 1 OR b = 2 AND c = 3 me brackets na lagana, aur galat result aana.
  • LIKE '%abc%' badi tables par slow hota hai (index use nahi hota).
  • WHERE me column alias use karna (WHERE chips > 100). Yeh nahi chalta, kyunki WHERE SELECT se pehle chalta hai.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. BETWEEN inclusive hai ya exclusive?
    A. Inclusive, dono boundaries shamil. Timestamps par dhyan rakho: BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-01-31' 31 Jan ke din ka data chhod dega.
  • Q. DISTINCT aur GROUP BY me farak?
    A. Dono unique rows de sakte hain. GROUP BY aggregation bhi karta hai, DISTINCT sirf duplicates hatata hai.

Yaad rakho

Pehle filter (WHERE), phir sort (ORDER BY), phir cut (LIMIT), aur LIMIT ke saath ORDER BY zaroor lagao.

SQL-03NULL handlingBasicMust Know

NULL ka matlab "value maloom nahi" hai, zero ya khaali string nahi. Iske saath comparison aur aggregation alag behave karte hain.

Simple me samjho

NULL ek khaali dabba hai jisme kuch likha hi nahi gaya. Isliye "NULL barabar NULL" bhi pakka nahi hota. SQL me teen results hote hain: TRUE, FALSE, aur UNKNOWN.

Key points

  • IS NULL / IS NOT NULL: NULL check karne ka sahi tareeka. = NULL kabhi kaam nahi karta.
  • Three-valued logic: NULL = 1, NULL = NULL, NULL <> 1 sab UNKNOWN hote hain. WHERE sirf TRUE rows rakhta hai.
  • AND/OR with NULL: FALSE AND NULL = FALSE, TRUE OR NULL = TRUE, baaki UNKNOWN.
  • COALESCE(a, b, ...): Pehli non-NULL value deta hai. COALESCE(bonus, 0).
  • NULLIF(a, b): a = b ho to NULL deta hai, warna a. Divide-by-zero se bachne me kaam aata hai: x / NULLIF(y, 0).
  • Aggregates: SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, COUNT(col) NULL ko ignore karte hain.
  • COUNT(*): NULL wali rows bhi gino. COUNT(col) sirf non-NULL ginta hai.
  • NOT IN trap: Agar list me ek bhi NULL ho to NOT IN kuch return nahi karta. NOT EXISTS use karo.
  • Sorting: PostgreSQL me ASC me NULL last aata hai. MySQL aur SQL Server me NULL pehle aata hai.
  • Safe compare: PostgreSQL me IS DISTINCT FROM NULL-safe hai.

Example

sql
-- bonus: 50, NULL, 0
SELECT id,
       COALESCE(bonus, 0) AS bonus_safe,
       NULLIF(bonus, 0)   AS bonus_nz
FROM t;

SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_all, COUNT(bonus) AS n_bonus, AVG(bonus) AS avg_bonus FROM t;
text
id | bonus_safe | bonus_nz
1  | 50         | 50
2  | 0          | NULL
3  | 0          | NULL

n_all | n_bonus | avg_bonus
3     | 2       | 25.0

AVG(bonus) = (50+0)/2 = 25, kyunki NULL row count hi nahi hui. Agar NULL ko 0 maanna hai to AVG(COALESCE(bonus,0)) = 16.67.

Common mistakes

  • WHERE bonus <> 0 likhna aur NULL rows ka gayab ho jaana.
  • Blindly COALESCE(x, 0) lagana jab NULL ka matlab "unknown" ho, "zero" nahi. Average badal jaata hai.
  • COUNT(col) aur COUNT(*) ko same samajhna.
  • LEFT JOIN ke baad NULL ko missing data samajh lena, jabki woh "no match" bhi ho sakta hai.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. WHERE x = NULL kyun fail hota hai?
    A. Kyunki comparison UNKNOWN deta hai, TRUE nahi. IS NULL use karte hain.
  • Q. AVG NULL ko kaise handle karta hai?
    A. Ignore karta hai. Denominator sirf non-NULL rows ka hota hai.

Yaad rakho

NULL se compare = UNKNOWN. IS NULL likho, aur aggregates NULL skip karte hain.

SQL-04Aggregations and GROUP BYBasicMust Know

Aggregate functions bahut rows ko ek value me badalte hain, aur GROUP BY har group ke liye alag value deta hai.

Simple me samjho

Poore table ka total nikalna ho to sirf aggregate lagao. Game-wise total chahiye to GROUP BY lagao. Har group ek chhoti table ki tarah treat hota hai, aur uske ek row nikalti hai.

Key points

  • COUNT(*): Rows ginta hai, NULL ke saath bhi.
  • COUNT(col): Sirf non-NULL values ginta hai.
  • COUNT(DISTINCT col): Unique non-NULL values. Unique players nikalne me kaam aata hai.
  • SUM, AVG: Numeric columns par. NULL ignore hota hai.
  • MIN, MAX: Numbers, dates, text sab par chalta hai.
  • GROUP BY: Jo columns SELECT me hain aur aggregate nahi hain, woh GROUP BY me hone chahiye.
  • Multiple columns: GROUP BY game, country har (game, country) combination ke liye ek row deti hai.
  • Position: GROUP BY 1, 2 select list ki position se group karta hai. Chhoti queries me theek, long queries me risky.
  • No GROUP BY: Poori table ek hi group maani jaati hai, to ek row aati hai.
  • Empty table: COUNT 0 deta hai, lekin SUM NULL deta hai.

Example

sql
-- bets: (user_id, game, amount)
-- (1,holdem,100) (1,holdem,50) (1,omaha,200) (2,holdem,70) (2,holdem,70)
SELECT game,
       COUNT(*)                  AS bets,
       COUNT(DISTINCT user_id)   AS users,
       SUM(amount)               AS total,
       ROUND(AVG(amount), 2)     AS avg_amt,
       MIN(amount)               AS min_amt,
       MAX(amount)               AS max_amt
FROM bets
GROUP BY game
ORDER BY game;
text
game   | bets | users | total | avg_amt | min_amt | max_amt
holdem | 4    | 2     | 290   | 72.50   | 50      | 100
omaha  | 1    | 1     | 200   | 200.00  | 200     | 200

bets 4 hai lekin users 2, kyunki ek user ne kai bets lagayi. Isliye COUNT(*) aur COUNT(DISTINCT ...) alag hote hain.

Common mistakes

  • SELECT me non-aggregated column daalna jo GROUP BY me nahi hai (PostgreSQL error deta hai; purane MySQL me chup-chaap galat value deta tha).
  • Users count karna COUNT(*) se jab rows events hain. COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) chahiye.
  • AVG of ratios nikalna. Average of averages galat hota hai; SUM(a)/SUM(b) use karo.
  • AVG ke decimals ko round kiye bina report karna. ROUND(AVG(x), 2) use karo.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. COUNT(*), COUNT(1), COUNT(col) me farak?
    A. COUNT(*) aur COUNT(1) same hain (sab rows). COUNT(col) NULL skip karta hai.
  • Q. Kya GROUP BY ke bina aggregate chal sakta hai?
    A. Haan, to poori table ek group hoti hai aur 1 row aati hai.

Yaad rakho

Grain badlo to GROUP BY badlo: jo columns group nahi hain, unhe aggregate karna hi padega.

SQL-05WHERE vs HAVING and execution orderBasicMust Know

WHERE rows ko grouping se pehle filter karta hai, HAVING groups ko aggregate ke baad. SQL ka logical order likhne ke order se alag hai.

Simple me samjho

Pehle table se rows chuno, phir unhe group karo, phir groups ko check karo. Aap SELECT pehle likhte ho, lekin database use baad me chalata hai.

Key points

  • Logical order: FROM (aur JOIN) -> WHERE -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> SELECT -> DISTINCT -> ORDER BY -> LIMIT.
  • Window functions: HAVING ke baad, SELECT ke time evaluate hote hain. Isliye WHERE me window function nahi chalta.
  • WHERE: Individual rows filter karta hai. Aggregate (SUM, COUNT) yahan allowed nahi.
  • HAVING: Groups filter karta hai. Aggregate use kar sakte ho: HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2.
  • Performance: Jo condition WHERE me ho sakti hai, use WHERE me hi rakho. Pehle rows kam hongi to GROUP BY tez chalega.
  • Alias: WHERE me SELECT alias nahi chalta. ORDER BY me chalta hai.
  • GROUP BY alias: PostgreSQL aur MySQL me alias allow hai, SQL Server me nahi.
  • LIMIT: Sabse last me lagta hai, sort ke baad.
  • Why it matters: "Rows kaun si count hongi" aur "groups kaun se bachenge" yeh order se decide hota hai.

Example

sql
SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS players
FROM players
WHERE balance > 0
GROUP BY country
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
ORDER BY players DESC
LIMIT 5;
text
country | players
IN      | 2

Pehle balance > 0 se Ravi (0) nikla. Phir country ke group bane: IN=2, US=1, DE=1. HAVING ne sirf IN rakha.

Common mistakes

  • WHERE COUNT(*) > 1 likhna. Error aayega, aggregate ke liye HAVING chahiye.
  • Normal condition (country = 'IN') ko HAVING me rakhna. Chalta hai lekin slow aur confusing.
  • WHERE rank = 1 jab rank window function ka alias ho. CTE ya subquery me wrap karo.
  • Maan lena ki SELECT ke alias har jagah chalte hain.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. WHERE aur HAVING me kya farak hai?
    A. WHERE grouping se pehle rows filter karta hai, HAVING grouping ke baad groups filter karta hai, aggregate ke saath.
  • Q. SQL ka execution order batao.
    A. FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY, LIMIT.

Yaad rakho

WHERE = row filter, HAVING = group filter. Order yaad rakho: F-W-G-H-S-O-L.

SQL-06JoinsBasicMust Know

Join do ya zyada tables ko ek key par jodta hai. Sahi join type chunna result decide karta hai.

Simple me samjho

Ek table me players, doosre me deposits. Join dono ko player ID se milata hai. Question yeh hota hai: jo match nahi hua, uska kya karein?

Key points

  • INNER JOIN: Sirf matching rows, dono taraf.
  • LEFT JOIN: Left table ki saari rows, right me match na ho to NULL.
  • RIGHT JOIN: Left join ka mirror. Practice me aksar LEFT hi use hota hai, table order badal ke.
  • FULL (OUTER) JOIN: Dono taraf ki saari rows. MySQL me nahi hai (UNION se banate hain).
  • CROSS JOIN: Har row x har row (cartesian). Date x game combinations banane me kaam aata hai.
  • SELF JOIN: Table ko khud se join karna, alias ke saath. Jaise employee -> manager, ya player -> referrer.
  • Join key: ON a.id = b.player_id. Same data type honi chahiye, aur ideally indexed.
  • USING (id): Dono side same naam ke column ho to shortcut.
  • Choose karo: "Sab left rows chahiye" = LEFT. "Sirf common" = INNER. "Mismatch dhoondhna hai" = FULL ya anti-join.
  • Multiple joins: Ek ke baad ek, left se right padhte hue.

Example

sql
-- players: (1,Amit) (2,Sara) (3,Ravi)
-- deposits: (player_id,amount) (1,100) (1,50) (2,200) (4,75)
SELECT p.name, SUM(d.amount) AS deposited
FROM players p
LEFT JOIN deposits d ON d.player_id = p.id
GROUP BY p.name
ORDER BY p.name;
text
name | deposited
Amit | 150
Ravi | NULL
Sara | 200

Ravi ka koi deposit nahi, phir bhi row aayi (NULL). INNER JOIN me Ravi gayab ho jata. player_id = 4 ka deposit kisi player se match nahi hua, to drop ho gaya; FULL JOIN me dikhta.

Self join ka chhota udaharan:

sql
SELECT e.name AS player, r.name AS referrer
FROM players e
JOIN players r ON r.id = e.referred_by;

Common mistakes

  • Jab "saare users chahiye" tab INNER JOIN use karna, aur inactive users ka silently gayab ho jaana.
  • Join key galat ya incomplete dena, to cartesian explosion ho jaata hai.
  • Alag data types ki keys join karna (int vs text); cast karo.
  • SELECT * joins me, aur duplicate column names ka confusion.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. INNER aur LEFT JOIN me farak?
    A. INNER sirf matched rows deta hai. LEFT left table ki sab rows rakhta hai, unmatched par right columns NULL.
  • Q. Self join kab use hota hai?
    A. Jab table me hi hierarchy ya comparison ho, jaise employee-manager, ya consecutive records compare karna.

Yaad rakho

Pehle decide karo kaunsi table ki saari rows chahiye. Wahi LEFT side, aur wahi grain.

SQL-07Join pitfallsIntermediateMust Know

Joins me rows chupchaap duplicate ho sakti hain aur totals galat aate hain. Row counts check karna aur ON vs WHERE samajhna zaroori hai.

Simple me samjho

Join ke baad rows ginti badal sakti hai. Agar ek player ke 2 deposits aur 2 sessions hain, to join me 2 x 2 = 4 rows banti hain. Phir SUM double-triple count karta hai.

Key points

  • Fan-out (one-to-many): Parent ko child se join karne par parent ki value child rows ke barabar repeat hoti hai. Parent ka SUM badh jaata hai.
  • Many-to-many duplicates: Dono taraf duplicates ho to rows multiply hoti hain (m x n).
  • Fix: Pehle har table ko join key ke level par aggregate karo (CTE/subquery), phir join karo.
  • Filter in ON vs WHERE (LEFT JOIN): Right table ki condition ON me ho to left rows bachti hain. WHERE me ho to NULL rows hat jaati hain aur LEFT JOIN INNER ban jaata hai.
  • INNER JOIN me: ON ya WHERE, result same hota hai.
  • Anti-join: "Jinka match nahi hai". LEFT JOIN ... WHERE b.key IS NULL ya NOT EXISTS.
  • Semi-join: "Jinka match hai, lekin duplicate nahi chahiye". EXISTS ya IN. Right table ki columns nahi aati.
  • Row count check: Join se pehle aur baad COUNT(*) aur COUNT(DISTINCT key) compare karo.
  • Uniqueness check: GROUP BY key HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 se pata chalta hai key unique hai ya nahi.

Example

sql
-- Amit: deposits 100, 50 ; sessions s1, s2
SELECT SUM(d.amount) AS wrong_total
FROM players p
JOIN deposits d ON d.player_id = p.id
JOIN sessions s ON s.player_id = p.id
WHERE p.id = 1;

-- Fix: aggregate pehle
SELECT SUM(d.total) AS right_total
FROM players p
JOIN (SELECT player_id, SUM(amount) AS total
      FROM deposits GROUP BY player_id) d ON d.player_id = p.id
WHERE p.id = 1;
text
wrong_total        right_total
300                150

Amit ke 2 deposits x 2 sessions = 4 rows bani, har deposit 2 baar gina gaya. 150 ka double 300 aaya. Anti-join ke liye (jinhone kabhi deposit nahi kiya):

sql
SELECT p.id FROM players p
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM deposits d WHERE d.player_id = p.id);

Common mistakes

  • Join ke baad SUM dekhna aur row count na check karna.
  • LEFT JOIN ke right-table filter ko WHERE me daalna (WHERE d.status = 'ok'), jisse non-matching players hat jaate hain.
  • NOT IN (subquery) use karna jab subquery me NULL ho sakta hai.
  • Dimension table me duplicate keys hona (jaise ek country ke 2 rows) aur fact rows double hona.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Join ke baad revenue double kyun aa raha hai?
    A. Fan-out. One-to-many join se parent value repeat hui. Pehle aggregate karo ya COUNT(DISTINCT) / unique key check lagao.
  • Q. LEFT JOIN me filter ON me ya WHERE me?
    A. Right table ka filter ON me, taaki unmatched left rows bachi rahein. WHERE me daalne par woh INNER ban jaata hai.

Yaad rakho

Join se pehle grain check karo, join ke baad row count check karo.

SQL-08Set operationsBasicGood to Have

UNION, INTERSECT aur EXCEPT do query results ko rows ke level par combine ya compare karte hain.

Simple me samjho

Join columns jodta hai (side by side). Set operations rows jodte hain (upar-neeche). Do lists hain, aur aap union, common, ya difference nikalte ho.

Key points

  • UNION ALL: Dono results ki saari rows, duplicates ke saath. Fast, kyunki sort/dedupe nahi karta.
  • UNION: Combine karke duplicates hata deta hai. Slow, kyunki dedupe karta hai.
  • INTERSECT: Sirf woh rows jo dono me hain.
  • EXCEPT: Pehle result me hain, doosre me nahi. Oracle me isi ko MINUS kehte hain.
  • Rules: Columns ki ginti same, aur types compatible. Column names pehli query se aate hain.
  • Order: ORDER BY sirf aakhir me lagta hai, poore combined result par.
  • NULLs: Set operations me NULL ko equal maana jaata hai (dedupe me), join se alag.
  • Kab kya: Logs ya monthly tables jodni hain to UNION ALL. Unique list chahiye to UNION.
  • Dialect: MySQL me INTERSECT/EXCEPT 8.0.31 se aaye. MINUS nahi hai. BigQuery me UNION DISTINCT, INTERSECT DISTINCT, EXCEPT DISTINCT likhna padta hai.

Example

sql
-- cash_players: 1,2,3   tourney_players: 2,3,4
SELECT id FROM cash_players
UNION ALL SELECT id FROM tourney_players;   -- 1,2,3,2,3,4

SELECT id FROM cash_players
UNION SELECT id FROM tourney_players;       -- 1,2,3,4

SELECT id FROM cash_players
INTERSECT SELECT id FROM tourney_players;   -- 2,3

SELECT id FROM cash_players
EXCEPT SELECT id FROM tourney_players;      -- 1
text
UNION ALL | UNION | INTERSECT | EXCEPT
1,2,3,2,3,4 | 1,2,3,4 | 2,3 | 1

EXCEPT ka matlab: sirf cash khelne wale, tournament nahi. Dono players (2,3) dono me hain.

Common mistakes

  • Default me UNION use karna jab UNION ALL kaafi ho. Extra sort cost aur kabhi kabhi rows ka galat hat jaana.
  • Column order alag hona. Position se match hota hai, naam se nahi.
  • EXCEPT ka order ulta kar dena. A EXCEPT B aur B EXCEPT A alag hain.
  • Alag data types union karna (text vs int), jisse error ya implicit cast hota hai.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. UNION vs UNION ALL?
    A. UNION duplicates hatata hai, UNION ALL nahi. UNION ALL tez hai; duplicates na hone ka pata ho to wahi use karo.
  • Q. INTERSECT ko join se kaise likhoge?
    A. INNER JOIN ya WHERE EXISTS se, key columns par.

Yaad rakho

Rows upar-neeche jodni hain to set operations. Default UNION ALL, dedupe sochke hi UNION.

SQL-09SubqueriesIntermediateMust Know

Subquery ek query ke andar doosri query hoti hai. Scalar, correlated, IN/EXISTS aur derived table iske main roop hain.

Simple me samjho

Pehle ek chhota sawaal solve karo, phir uska jawab bade sawaal me use karo. Jaise "average balance kya hai?", phir "kaun usse upar hai?".

Key points

  • Scalar subquery: Ek value deta hai (1 row, 1 column). WHERE balance > (SELECT AVG(balance) FROM players).
  • Derived table: FROM (SELECT ...) AS t. Alias zaroori hai. Pehle aggregate, phir join ke liye useful.
  • IN: WHERE id IN (SELECT player_id FROM deposits). Values ki list se match.
  • EXISTS: Sirf yeh check karta hai ki row mili ya nahi. Aksar IN se safe aur fast.
  • NOT EXISTS: Anti-join. NULL ki problem nahi aati.
  • NOT IN trap: Subquery me ek NULL aaya to result khaali. NOT EXISTS prefer karo.
  • Correlated subquery: Outer query ki column use karta hai, to har outer row ke liye chalta hai. Slow ho sakta hai.
  • Column subquery: SELECT list me subquery. Ek value per row, chhote data par ok.
  • CTE vs subquery: Same kaam, CTE zyada readable (SQL-10).
  • Window alternative: Correlated subquery ki jagah aksar window function tez hoti hai.

Example

sql
-- players: Amit 500, Sara 1200, Ravi 0, Anna 300, Amar 750 (avg = 550)
SELECT name, balance
FROM players
WHERE balance > (SELECT AVG(balance) FROM players);
text
name | balance
Sara | 1200
Amar | 750

Correlated + EXISTS ka example, jisme deposit kar chuke players milte hain:

sql
SELECT p.name
FROM players p
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM deposits d WHERE d.player_id = p.id);

Yahan inner query outer p.id use karti hai, isliye correlated hai.

Common mistakes

  • Scalar subquery se 2 rows aa jana. Error aata hai (more than one row returned).
  • NOT IN me NULL wali list ke saath use karna.
  • Badi table par correlated subquery chalana aur query slow hona.
  • Derived table ko alias na dena (MySQL aur PostgreSQL 15 tak me error).

Interview Q&A

  • Q. IN vs EXISTS?
    A. IN values ki list match karta hai. EXISTS sirf row ki maujoodgi check karta hai aur NULL se safe hai. Optimizer aksar dono ko same plan me badal deta hai.
  • Q. Correlated subquery kya hai?
    A. Jo outer query ki column par depend karti hai, to logically har outer row ke liye ek baar chalti hai.

Yaad rakho

Value chahiye to scalar, existence chahiye to EXISTS, aur NULL ho sakta ho to NOT EXISTS.

SQL-10CTEsIntermediateMust Know

WITH clause se query ko naam wale steps me tod ke likhte hain. Padhna aasan hota hai, aur recursion bhi possible hai.

Simple me samjho

CTE ek temporary naam wala result hai jo sirf us query ke liye hota hai. Bade sawaal ko chhote steps me likho, jaise pipeline: step 1, step 2, final.

Key points

  • WITH: WITH name AS (SELECT ...) SELECT ... FROM name.
  • Chained CTEs: Comma se kai CTEs. Baad wala CTE pehle wale ko use kar sakta hai.
  • Readability: Nested subqueries ki jagah top-to-bottom flow. Debug karna aasan, har step alag select karke dekho.
  • Reuse: Ek CTE ko query me kai baar reference kar sakte ho.
  • Scope: CTE sirf ek statement tak rehta hai, table ya view nahi banta.
  • Recursive CTE: WITH RECURSIVE, anchor member + UNION ALL + recursive member. Hierarchy, date series ke liye.
  • Termination: Recursive me stop condition (WHERE) zaroori, warna infinite loop.
  • Dialect: SQL Server me RECURSIVE keyword nahi likhte, sirf WITH. PostgreSQL 12+ me simple CTE inline hota hai; MATERIALIZED se force kar sakte ho.
  • Performance: CTE magic se tez nahi karta. Plan dekhna zaroori hai.

Example

sql
-- deposits: (1,100) (1,50) (2,200) (4,75)
WITH totals AS (
  SELECT player_id, SUM(amount) AS total
  FROM deposits
  GROUP BY player_id
),
big AS (
  SELECT * FROM totals WHERE total >= 100
)
SELECT * FROM big ORDER BY player_id;
text
player_id | total
1         | 150
2         | 200

Step 1 me totals bane (1:150, 2:200, 4:75), step 2 me total >= 100 filter hua, to player 4 hat gaya.

Recursive CTE (1 se 5 tak):

sql
WITH RECURSIVE n AS (
  SELECT 1 AS d
  UNION ALL
  SELECT d + 1 FROM n WHERE d < 5
)
SELECT d FROM n;   -- 1,2,3,4,5

Common mistakes

  • Recursive CTE me stop condition bhool jana, jisse query atak jaati hai.
  • Maan lena ki CTE ek temp table hai jo ek baar compute hoke store hota hai (hamesha nahi).
  • Bahut zyada CTEs jinme koi aggregate ya filter nahi, bas naam badalne ke liye.
  • Recursive me anchor aur recursive part ke column types match na karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. CTE vs subquery?
    A. Result same hota hai. CTE readable hai aur kai baar reuse ho sakta hai. Performance engine ke optimizer par depend karti hai.
  • Q. Recursive CTE kab use karoge?
    A. Org hierarchy, referral chain, ya date series banane ke liye.

Yaad rakho

CTE = naam wala step. Pipeline likho, aur recursion me hamesha stop condition do.

SQL-11CASE WHENBasicMust Know

CASE WHEN SQL ka if-else hai. Bucketing, pivot aur conditional aggregation me sabse zyada use hota hai.

Simple me samjho

Har row ke liye condition check hoti hai, aur pehli sahi condition ki value milti hai. Jaise balance dekh ke player ko low, mid ya high tier dena.

Key points

  • Syntax: CASE WHEN cond THEN val ... ELSE val END. Conditions upar se neeche check hoti hain.
  • First match wins: Pehli TRUE condition par ruk jaata hai. Order matter karta hai.
  • ELSE: Na likho to unmatched rows ko NULL milta hai.
  • Simple CASE: CASE country WHEN 'IN' THEN 'India' ... END (equality ke liye).
  • Bucketing: Numbers ko ranges me baantna (age group, balance tier).
  • Conditional aggregation: SUM(CASE WHEN cond THEN x ELSE 0 END). Ek query me kai filtered totals.
  • CASE-based pivot: Rows ko columns me badalna. Har column ke liye ek CASE.
  • FILTER: PostgreSQL me COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cond) short form hai.
  • Type rule: Saare THEN/ELSE ke types compatible hone chahiye.
  • Kahin bhi: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, GROUP BY, aur aggregate ke andar bhi chalta hai.

Example

sql
-- players: Amit IN 500, Sara US 1200, Ravi IN 0, Anna DE 300, Amar IN 750
SELECT CASE WHEN balance < 100  THEN 'low'
            WHEN balance < 1000 THEN 'mid'
            ELSE 'high' END AS tier,
       COUNT(*) AS players
FROM players
GROUP BY 1;
text
tier | players
low  | 1
mid  | 3
high | 1

Conditional aggregation (country-wise balance ek row me):

sql
SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN country = 'IN' THEN balance ELSE 0 END) AS in_bal,
       SUM(CASE WHEN country = 'US' THEN balance ELSE 0 END) AS us_bal
FROM players;

Result: in_bal = 1250 (500+0+750), us_bal = 1200.

Common mistakes

  • Conditions ka order galat rakhna (< 1000 pehle likh diya, to < 100 kabhi nahi chalega).
  • ELSE bhool jaana aur result me NULL aana, jo SUM/AVG ko badal deta hai.
  • COUNT(CASE WHEN x THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) likhna. Yeh 0 ko bhi ginta hai; ELSE hatao ya SUM use karo.
  • Boundary values (< vs <=) par bucket galat hona.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Conditional aggregation kya hai?
    A. Aggregate ke andar CASE lagana, taaki ek hi query me alag-alag conditions ke totals mil jayein.
  • Q. CASE me ELSE nahi diya to?
    A. Koi bhi condition match na hui to NULL milta hai.

Yaad rakho

CASE upar se neeche, pehla match jeetta hai. Aggregate ke andar CASE = pivot ka base.

SQL-12String functionsBasicMust Know

Text ko saaf karne, todne aur search karne ke functions. Dirty data (email, names) clean karne me roz kaam aate hain.

Simple me samjho

Raw data me spaces, capital-small ka mix aur extra characters hote hain. String functions unhe analysis ke layak saaf banate hain.

Key points

  • CONCAT / ||: Strings jodna. CONCAT NULL ko khaali maanta hai; || PostgreSQL me NULL ke saath NULL deta hai.
  • SUBSTRING: SUBSTRING(s, start, length). Position 1 se shuru hoti hai. LEFT(s, n) aur RIGHT(s, n) bhi hain.
  • TRIM: Dono taraf ke spaces hatata hai. LTRIM/RTRIM ek taraf ke.
  • REPLACE: REPLACE(s, 'old', 'new') har occurrence badalta hai.
  • UPPER / LOWER / LENGTH: Case badalna aur length. Matching se pehle LOWER lagana achhi aadat hai.
  • SPLIT_PART: SPLIT_PART(s, '@', 2) delimiter se todke n-th hissa deta hai (PostgreSQL). MySQL me SUBSTRING_INDEX, BigQuery me SPLIT(s, '@')[OFFSET(1)].
  • LIKE: Case-sensitive in PostgreSQL. ILIKE: Case-insensitive (sirf PostgreSQL). MySQL me LIKE collation ke hisaab se aksar case-insensitive hota hai.
  • REGEXP: PostgreSQL me ~ aur REGEXP_REPLACE, MySQL me REGEXP, BigQuery me REGEXP_CONTAINS. Complex patterns ke liye.
  • Escape: Literal % ya _ dhoondhne ke liye ESCAPE use karo.
  • Performance: Column par function lagane se (LOWER(email) = ...) normal index kaam nahi karta.

Example

sql
-- users: (1, ' Amit.Sharma@Gmail.com ') (2, 'sara@yahoo.com')
SELECT id,
       LOWER(TRIM(email))                       AS email_clean,
       SPLIT_PART(LOWER(TRIM(email)), '@', 2)   AS domain
FROM users;
text
id | email_clean            | domain
1  | amit.sharma@gmail.com  | gmail.com
2  | sara@yahoo.com         | yahoo.com

Pehle TRIM spaces hataya, phir LOWER, phir SPLIT_PART se @ ke baad ka hissa nikala. Domain-wise players ginne ke liye yahi pattern use hota hai.

Common mistakes

  • Clean kiye bina join ya group karna ('Amit ' aur 'amit' alag count hote hain).
  • SUBSTRING ki position 0 se socha. SQL me 1 se hoti hai.
  • LIKE ko case-insensitive maan lena (PostgreSQL me nahi hota).
  • CONCAT ya || me NULL ke effect ko ignore karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Email se domain kaise nikaloge?
    A. PostgreSQL me SPLIT_PART(email, '@', 2). MySQL me SUBSTRING_INDEX(email, '@', -1).
  • Q. LIKE vs ILIKE?
    A. ILIKE case-insensitive hai aur sirf PostgreSQL me hota hai. Baaki me LOWER(col) LIKE ... use karo.

Yaad rakho

Pehle TRIM + LOWER karke clean karo, phir match ya split karo. Dialect function names alag hote hain.

SQL-13Date and time functionsIntermediateMust Know

Dates truncate karna, parts nikalna, difference lena aur time zone sambhalna. Daily, weekly aur monthly reports ka base.

Simple me samjho

Timestamp me din, mahina, ghanta sab hota hai. Report ke liye usse sahi bucket me daalna padta hai. Time zone galat ho to raat ke events agle din me chale jaate hain.

Key points

  • DATE_TRUNC('month', ts): Timestamp ko month/week/day ki shuruaat par kaat deta hai (PostgreSQL). MySQL me DATE_FORMAT ya DATE_SUB; BigQuery me DATE_TRUNC(d, MONTH); SQL Server me DATETRUNC (2022+).
  • EXTRACT: EXTRACT(YEAR FROM ts), HOUR, ISODOW. PostgreSQL me DOW me Sunday = 0, ISODOW me Monday = 1.
  • Week boundary: PostgreSQL me DATE_TRUNC('week', ...) Monday se shuru. Dusre tools me Sunday default ho sakta hai, check karo.
  • Date difference: PostgreSQL me date1 - date2 = days. MySQL DATEDIFF(a, b), SQL Server DATEDIFF(day, a, b), BigQuery DATE_DIFF(a, b, DAY).
  • Date add: PostgreSQL d + INTERVAL '7 days'. MySQL aur BigQuery DATE_ADD(d, INTERVAL 7 DAY).
  • Intervals: INTERVAL '1 month', INTERVAL '30 minutes' jodne-ghatane ke liye.
  • Month end: DATE_TRUNC('month', d) + INTERVAL '1 month' - INTERVAL '1 day'.
  • Time zone: ts AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata' (PostgreSQL). Store UTC me karo, report local zone me.
  • timestamp vs timestamptz: timestamptz absolute moment hai. timestamp me zone info nahi hoti.
  • Date range filter: ts >= '2026-03-01' AND ts < '2026-04-01' (half-open), BETWEEN se bacho.

Example

sql
-- ts (UTC): 2026-03-15 22:30:00+00   (Sunday)
SELECT ts AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata'                          AS ist_ts,
       DATE_TRUNC('week',  ts AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')     AS ist_week,
       DATE_TRUNC('month', ts AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')     AS ist_month
FROM events;
text
ist_ts              | ist_week            | ist_month
2026-03-16 04:00:00 | 2026-03-16 00:00:00 | 2026-03-01 00:00:00

UTC me yeh Sunday raat hai, lekin IST me Monday subah 4 baje. Isliye week bhi agla ban gaya. Time zone nahi dekhoge to daily/weekly numbers shift ho jayenge.

Common mistakes

  • Time zone ka dhyan na rakhna, aur raat ke events galat din me girna.
  • BETWEEN se month filter karna aur last din ka time-portion chhoot jaana.
  • Week start (Monday/Sunday) assume karna.
  • DATE_TRUNC ko text me format karke group karna (slow aur sort galat).

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Monthly active users kaise nikaloge?
    A. DATE_TRUNC('month', event_ts) se group karke COUNT(DISTINCT user_id), sahi time zone ke saath.
  • Q. Do dates ka difference kaise nikalte ho?
    A. Dialect par depend karta hai: PostgreSQL me subtract (d2 - d1), MySQL me DATEDIFF, SQL Server me DATEDIFF(day, ...).

Yaad rakho

UTC me store, local me report. Date range hamesha >= start AND < next_start.

SQL-14Type casting and numeric gotchasIntermediateMust Know

Data type conversion aur number ke chhote jaal: integer division, rounding, float ki galtiyan, aur implicit conversion.

Simple me samjho

SQL har value ka ek type maanta hai, aur calculation us type ke rules se hoti hai. Do integers ko divide karoge to kuch dialects me answer bhi integer aata hai.

Key points

  • CAST: CAST(x AS type) standard hai, sab jagah chalta hai.
  • :: operator: x::numeric PostgreSQL ka shortcut hai.
  • Integer division: PostgreSQL aur SQL Server me 7/2 = 3. MySQL aur BigQuery me 7/2 = 3.5.
  • Fix: Ek side ko decimal banao: 7/2.0, 7::numeric/2, ya 1.0 * a / b.
  • ROUND(x, n): n decimals tak round. PostgreSQL me ROUND(x, 2) ke liye x numeric hona chahiye, float par error aata hai.
  • Float vs decimal: FLOAT/DOUBLE approximate hote hain. NUMERIC/DECIMAL exact hote hain. Paise ke liye NUMERIC(12,2).
  • Float equality: 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.3 float me FALSE ho sakta hai. Equality se bacho.
  • Implicit conversion: Engine khud type badal deta hai ('10' = 10). MySQL me '10abc' ko 10 maan leta hai. Indexed column par cast se index bekaar ho sakta hai.
  • Division by zero: x / NULLIF(y, 0) se NULL milta hai.
  • Text to date: CAST('2026-01-05' AS date). Galat format par error aata hai.

Example

sql
SELECT 7/2                         AS int_div,
       7/2.0                       AS dec_div,
       ROUND(10 * 1.0 / 3, 2)      AS rounded,
       (0.1::float8 + 0.2::float8) = 0.3   AS float_eq,
       (0.1::numeric + 0.2::numeric) = 0.3 AS num_eq;
text
int_div | dec_div            | rounded | float_eq | num_eq
3       | 3.5000000000000000 | 3.33    | f        | t

PostgreSQL me 7/2 = 3, kyunki dono integer hain. float_eq FALSE aaya kyunki 0.1 + 0.2 float me 0.30000000000000004 hota hai. numeric me exact 0.3 milta hai.

Conversion rate ka sahi formula:

sql
SELECT 100.0 * SUM(converted) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS conv_pct FROM signups;

Common mistakes

  • Percentage nikalte time count_a / count_b karna aur 0 aana (integer division).
  • Money ko FLOAT me store karna.
  • ROUND ko report ke beech me lagana aur phir sum karna. Round aakhir me karo.
  • Text column ko number se compare karna (WHERE id = '5') aur surprise conversions ya slow query.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. 5/2 ka result kya hoga?
    A. Dialect par depend: PostgreSQL aur SQL Server me 2, MySQL aur BigQuery me 2.5. Safe tareeka decimal me cast karna.
  • Q. Float aur decimal me kya farak?
    A. Float binary approximate hota hai, rounding errors aate hain. Decimal exact hota hai, isliye money ke liye wahi use hota hai.

Yaad rakho

Divide karne se pehle ek side ko decimal banao, aur paise hamesha NUMERIC me rakho.

SQL-15Window functions: rankingIntermediateMust Know

ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK aur NTILE rows ko group ke andar rank karte hain, bina rows ghataye.

Simple me samjho

GROUP BY rows ko ek me sameet deta hai. Window function rows ko rakhte hue unke saath ek extra calculated column deta hai. Ranking ke liye har group ke andar sort karke number lagate hain.

Key points

  • Syntax: fn() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY x DESC).
  • PARTITION BY: Group banata hai. Na do to poori table ek group.
  • ROW_NUMBER: 1, 2, 3, 4, bina repeat. Ties me order arbitrary, isliye extra tie-breaker do.
  • RANK: Ties ko same rank, phir gap. 1, 1, 3.
  • DENSE_RANK: Ties ko same rank, bina gap. 1, 1, 2.
  • NTILE(n): Rows ko n barabar buckets me baantta hai. Quartile ya decile ke liye (NTILE(4)).
  • Top-N per group: Rank nikalo CTE/subquery me, phir bahar WHERE rn <= N.
  • Why wrap: WHERE window function se pehle chalta hai (SQL-05), isliye seedha filter nahi hota. MySQL 8+ aur PostgreSQL me chalta hai; SQL Server me bhi.
  • QUALIFY: BigQuery/Snowflake me window result par seedha filter. PostgreSQL me nahi hai.
  • Choose: Exactly ek row chahiye to ROW_NUMBER. Ties dono chahiye to RANK/DENSE_RANK.

Example

sql
-- winnings: (A,holdem,500) (B,holdem,500) (C,holdem,300) (D,omaha,900) (E,omaha,100)
SELECT game, player, winnings,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY game ORDER BY winnings DESC, player) AS rn,
       RANK()       OVER (PARTITION BY game ORDER BY winnings DESC)         AS rnk,
       DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY game ORDER BY winnings DESC)         AS drnk
FROM winnings
ORDER BY game, rn;
text
game   | player | winnings | rn | rnk | drnk
holdem | A      | 500      | 1  | 1   | 1
holdem | B      | 500      | 2  | 1   | 1
holdem | C      | 300      | 3  | 3   | 2
omaha  | D      | 900      | 1  | 1   | 1
omaha  | E      | 100      | 2  | 2   | 2

A aur B ka tie hai: RANK dono ko 1 deta hai aur C ko 3 (gap). DENSE_RANK C ko 2 deta hai.

Top-2 per game:

sql
WITH r AS (
  SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY game ORDER BY winnings DESC, player) AS rn
  FROM winnings)
SELECT * FROM r WHERE rn <= 2;

Common mistakes

  • Tie-breaker bina ROW_NUMBER use karna, aur har run me alag rows aana.
  • WHERE rn <= 3 ko seedha same SELECT me likhna.
  • PARTITION BY bhool jaana, to poori table ki ranking ho jaati hai.
  • RANK aur DENSE_RANK ko mix karna jab "top 3 distinct values" chahiye.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. RANK, DENSE_RANK, ROW_NUMBER me farak?
    A. ROW_NUMBER unique 1,2,3. RANK ties par same, phir gap (1,1,3). DENSE_RANK ties par same, bina gap (1,1,2).
  • Q. Har group ke top 3 kaise nikaloge?
    A. CTE me ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY x DESC) lagao, phir WHERE rn <= 3.

Yaad rakho

Window = rows rakho, calculation add karo. Top-N ke liye rank pehle, filter baad me.

SQL-16Window functions: LAG and LEADIntermediateMust Know

LAG pichli row ki value aur LEAD agli row ki value current row ke saath laate hain. Change aur gap nikalne ke liye best.

Simple me samjho

Aapko ek row me kal ki value chahiye taaki aaj se compare kar sako. LAG peeche dekhta hai, LEAD aage dekhta hai.

Key points

  • Syntax: LAG(col, n, default) OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY t). n default 1 hai.
  • LAG: n rows pehle ki value. Pehli row par NULL.
  • LEAD: n rows baad ki value. Aakhri row par NULL.
  • Default value: Teesra argument NULL ki jagah value deta hai, LAG(rev, 1, 0).
  • ORDER BY zaroori: Bina order ke previous ka matlab nahi hota.
  • PARTITION BY: Har user ya game ke liye alag chalta hai, to user A ki last row user B ko nahi milti.
  • Period-over-period change: rev - LAG(rev) OVER (ORDER BY day).
  • Percent change: 100.0 * (rev - prev) / NULLIF(prev, 0).
  • Time between events: ts - LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts). Sessions ya inactivity gap ke liye.
  • Row-based: LAG row ke hisaab se chalta hai, date ke hisaab se nahi. Dates missing hon to calendar table se join karo.

Example

sql
-- daily_rev: (2026-03-01,100) (2026-03-02,120) (2026-03-03,90)
SELECT day, revenue,
       LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY day) AS prev_rev,
       ROUND(100.0 * (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY day))
             / NULLIF(LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY day), 0), 1) AS pct_change
FROM daily_rev
ORDER BY day;
text
day        | revenue | prev_rev | pct_change
2026-03-01 | 100     | NULL     | NULL
2026-03-02 | 120     | 100      | 20.0
2026-03-03 | 90      | 120      | -25.0

Pehle din ka pichla din nahi hai, to NULL. Dusre din (120-100)/100 = 20%. Teesre din (90-120)/120 = -25%.

Time between events:

sql
SELECT user_id, ts,
       ts - LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts) AS gap
FROM logins;

Common mistakes

  • PARTITION BY na lagana, aur ek user ki row ko doosre user se compare karna.
  • Pehli row ke NULL ko handle na karna.
  • Maan lena ki LAG(1) ka matlab "kal" hai, jabki data me din missing ho sakte hain.
  • ORDER BY galat column par lagana (ts ki jagah id).

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Month-over-month growth kaise nikaloge?
    A. Monthly aggregate CTE me banao, phir LAG(value) OVER (ORDER BY month) se (curr - prev) / prev.
  • Q. LAG aur LEAD me kya farak?
    A. LAG pichli row dekhta hai, LEAD agli row. Dono ka syntax same hai.

Yaad rakho

LAG = peeche, LEAD = aage. Hamesha PARTITION aur ORDER sochke lagao.

SQL-17Window functions: running totals and moving averagesIntermediateMust Know

Frame (ROWS/RANGE BETWEEN) decide karta hai window kitni rows dekhegi. Isse cumulative sum aur moving average milte hain.

Simple me samjho

Running total me har row tak ka jod milta hai. Moving average me sirf pichle kuch din ka average hota hai. Frame batata hai "kitni rows peeche tak dekhna hai".

Key points

  • Running total: SUM(x) OVER (ORDER BY day). Default frame pehli row se current row tak.
  • Frame syntax: ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW.
  • 7-day moving average: AVG(x) OVER (ORDER BY day ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW).
  • ROWS: Physical rows ginta hai.
  • RANGE: Value ke hisaab se range lagata hai, aur ties (same ORDER BY value) saath me shamil hoti hain. PostgreSQL 11+ me date interval se bhi: RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL '6 days' PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW.
  • Default frame trap: ORDER BY ke saath default RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING TO CURRENT ROW hota hai. Ties wale running total me same value dikhti hai. ROWS likhna safe hai.
  • PARTITION BY: Running total har user ya game ke liye restart hota hai.
  • FIRST_VALUE: Frame ki pehli value. LAST_VALUE: Frame ki aakhri value.
  • LAST_VALUE trap: Default frame current row par rukta hai, to LAST_VALUE current row ki hi value deta hai. Frame ko UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING tak badhao.
  • Missing dates: Din gayab hon to 7 rows != 7 din. Calendar se pehle fill karo.

Example

sql
-- daily_dep: day1..day5 = 10, 20, 30, 40, 50
SELECT day, amount,
       SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY day)                                   AS running,
       ROUND(AVG(amount) OVER (ORDER BY day
             ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 1)               AS ma3,
       FIRST_VALUE(amount) OVER (ORDER BY day)                           AS first_amt
FROM daily_dep;
text
day  | amount | running | ma3  | first_amt
1    | 10     | 10      | 10.0 | 10
2    | 20     | 30      | 15.0 | 10
3    | 30     | 60      | 20.0 | 10
4    | 40     | 100     | 30.0 | 10
5    | 50     | 150     | 40.0 | 10

Day 3 ka ma3 = (10+20+30)/3 = 20. Pehli 2 rows me poori 3 rows nahi hain, to partial average aata hai.

Common mistakes

  • Pehli 6 din ka partial average report karna jab "full 7-day average" chahiye.
  • LAST_VALUE ko bina frame badle use karna.
  • Duplicate dates par RANGE default se running total me ek saath jump aana.
  • Missing dates ke saath ROWS ko calendar days samajhna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. ROWS aur RANGE me farak?
    A. ROWS physical row count se frame banata hai. RANGE ORDER BY value se banata hai aur same value wali (tie) rows ko saath me leta hai.
  • Q. 7-day moving average ka SQL?
    A. AVG(x) OVER (ORDER BY day ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW).

Yaad rakho

Frame likh ke hi window chalao: ROWS BETWEEN n PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW. LAST_VALUE me UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING yaad rakho.

SQL-18DeduplicationIntermediateMust Know

Duplicate rows hatana ya har user ka latest record nikalna. Raw data me yeh sabse common cleaning step hai.

Simple me samjho

Raw tables me same user kai baar aa sakta hai (retries, updates, double loads). Aapko decide karna hai kaunsi row rakhni hai, aur aksar woh latest hoti hai.

Key points

  • Exact duplicates: Poori row same ho to SELECT DISTINCT * kaafi hai.
  • Key duplicates: Same id, alag values ho to decide karo kaunsi rakhni hai (latest, first, non-NULL).
  • ROW_NUMBER dedupe: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY updated_at DESC), phir rn = 1.
  • Tie-breaker: updated_at same ho to doosra column (ingested_at, id) ORDER BY me jodo.
  • Latest record per user: Wahi pattern. Earliest chahiye to ASC.
  • DISTINCT ON: PostgreSQL ka shortcut. SELECT DISTINCT ON (id) * FROM t ORDER BY id, updated_at DESC.
  • QUALIFY: BigQuery/Snowflake me QUALIFY rn = 1 seedha filter.
  • Detect first: GROUP BY id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 se duplicates ginti dekho.
  • Source dhoondho: Duplicate kyun aaye? Retry, join fan-out, ya double ingestion. Sirf dedupe karke chhod dena theek nahi.
  • Delete safety: Table se delete karne se pehle SELECT se verify karo. Production me approval lo; naya cleaned table banana safe hai.

Example

sql
-- users_raw: (1,a@x.com,2026-01-01) (1,a@x.com,2026-02-01) (2,b@x.com,2026-01-15)
WITH ranked AS (
  SELECT *,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY updated_at DESC) AS rn
  FROM users_raw
)
SELECT id, email, updated_at
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY id;
text
id | email   | updated_at
1  | a@x.com | 2026-02-01
2  | b@x.com | 2026-01-15

User 1 ki 2 rows thi, latest updated_at wali rakhi. PostgreSQL me same kaam: SELECT DISTINCT ON (id) * FROM users_raw ORDER BY id, updated_at DESC.

Common mistakes

  • DISTINCT lagana jab sirf kuch columns alag hon, to duplicates bach jaate hain.
  • Tie-breaker na dena, aur har run me alag row bachna.
  • DISTINCT se join fan-out chhupana, jabki asli problem join key ki hai.
  • Pehle ki duplicates dekhe bina seedha DELETE chalana.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Har user ka latest record kaise nikaloge?
    A. ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC) lagao, phir rn = 1 filter karo.
  • Q. DISTINCT ON kya hai?
    A. PostgreSQL feature jo har key ki pehli row rakhta hai, ORDER BY ke hisaab se.

Yaad rakho

PARTITION BY key, ORDER BY latest DESC, rn = 1. Pehle duplicates ka kaaran dhoondho.

SQL-19Pivot and unpivotIntermediateGood to Have

Pivot rows ko columns me badalta hai, unpivot columns ko rows me. CASE se har dialect me kar sakte hain.

Simple me samjho

Long table me har (month, game) ki ek row hoti hai. Pivot me game ke columns ban jaate hain, jaise Excel pivot. Unpivot iska ulta hai: wide table se wapas long.

Key points

  • CASE-based pivot: SUM(CASE WHEN game = 'holdem' THEN amount END) per column, GROUP BY row key. Har dialect me chalta hai.
  • Limitation: Column names pehle se maloom hone chahiye. Dynamic columns ke liye dynamic SQL chahiye.
  • PIVOT: SQL Server, Oracle aur BigQuery me built-in PIVOT (SUM(x) FOR col IN (...)).
  • UNPIVOT: SQL Server, Oracle, BigQuery me built-in. Wide columns ko rows me badalta hai.
  • PostgreSQL / MySQL: Built-in PIVOT nahi hai. PostgreSQL me crosstab (tablefunc extension) ya CASE use karo.
  • Unpivot in PostgreSQL: CROSS JOIN LATERAL (VALUES (...), (...)) se.
  • UNNEST: Array ko rows me todta hai. PostgreSQL aur BigQuery me UNNEST(tags).
  • Lateral flatten: Snowflake me LATERAL FLATTEN array ya JSON ko rows me badalta hai. MySQL 8 me JSON_TABLE.
  • Kab pivot: Report ya BI ke liye wide format. Analysis aur charts ke liye long format aksar behtar hai.
  • NULL: CASE pivot me match na ho to NULL aata hai. Zaroorat ho to COALESCE(..., 0).

Example

sql
-- sales: (2026-01-01,holdem,100) (2026-01-01,omaha,50)
--        (2026-02-01,holdem,80)  (2026-02-01,omaha,70)
SELECT month,
       SUM(CASE WHEN game = 'holdem' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS holdem,
       SUM(CASE WHEN game = 'omaha'  THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS omaha
FROM sales
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month;
text
month      | holdem | omaha
2026-01-01 | 100    | 50
2026-02-01 | 80     | 70

Rows ke game values ab columns ban gaye. Ulta (unpivot) PostgreSQL me:

sql
SELECT p.month, v.game, v.amount
FROM pivoted p
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (VALUES ('holdem', p.holdem), ('omaha', p.omaha)) AS v(game, amount);

Array ke liye: SELECT id, UNNEST(tags) AS tag FROM players; har tag ek row deta hai.

Common mistakes

  • Naye game add hone par pivot columns update karna bhool jaana.
  • Pivot ke baad us par aur aggregation lagana jab long data se seedha ho sakta tha.
  • ELSE 0 aur NULL ka fark na samajhna (average me farak aata hai).
  • UNNEST karne par row count badhna aur phir SUM double ginna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. PostgreSQL me pivot kaise karoge?
    A. SUM(CASE WHEN ... THEN x END) ... GROUP BY, ya crosstab function. Built-in PIVOT keyword nahi hai.
  • Q. UNNEST kab use karte hain?
    A. Jab column me array ho (tags, items) aur har element ko alag row me chahiye, jaise tag-wise count.

Yaad rakho

Pivot = GROUP BY + CASE. Unpivot = rows me wapas (UNION ALL, LATERAL VALUES, ya UNPIVOT).

SQL-20Date series and gap fillingIntermediateMust Know

Missing dates ko zero ke saath dikhane ke liye date spine banao aur data ko usme LEFT JOIN karo.

Simple me samjho

Agar kisi din koi deposit nahi hua, to GROUP BY wo din dikhata hi nahi. Chart me gap aa jaata hai. Pehle poore dates ki list (spine) banao. Phir data ko us par chipkao.

Key points

  • Problem: GROUP BY sirf wahi dates deta hai jo table me hain. Missing din ki row exist hi nahi karti.
  • Date spine: Ek list jisme har din ki ek row ho. Isko LEFT JOIN me left side rakho.
  • generate_series: PostgreSQL me generate_series(start, stop, step). Date dene par timestamp milta hai, isliye ::date cast karo.
  • Left join to spine: FROM spine LEFT JOIN data. Spine ke saare din rahenge, data na ho to NULL.
  • Zero fill: COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0) use karo. COUNT(t.id) NULL ko ignore karke 0 deta hai.
  • Filter ki jagah: Data table ke conditions ON me likho, WHERE me nahi. Warna LEFT JOIN INNER JOIN ban jaata hai.
  • Calendar table: Permanent dim_date table (date, week, month, is_weekend, holiday flag). Warehouse me yahi reuse hota hai.
  • MySQL / SQL Server: Recursive CTE se dates banao (MySQL 8+).
  • BigQuery / Snowflake: BigQuery me UNNEST(GENERATE_DATE_ARRAY(a, b)). Snowflake me TABLE(GENERATOR(ROWCOUNT => n)) ke saath ROW_NUMBER().
  • Redshift: generate_series limited hai, calendar table safe option hai.

Example

sql
SELECT s.day::date AS day,
       COUNT(t.id)  AS deposits,
       COALESCE(SUM(t.amount), 0) AS total_amount
FROM generate_series('2024-05-01'::date, '2024-05-05'::date, '1 day') AS s(day)
LEFT JOIN transactions t
       ON t.type = 'deposit'
      AND t.created_at >= s.day
      AND t.created_at <  s.day + INTERVAL '1 day'
GROUP BY s.day
ORDER BY s.day;
text
day         | deposits | total_amount
2024-05-01  | 3        | 1500
2024-05-02  | 0        | 0
2024-05-03  | 2        | 900

2 May ko koi row nahi thi, phir bhi spine ki wajah se 0 aaya.

Common mistakes

  • type = 'deposit' ko WHERE me daalna. Isse zero wale din gayab ho jaate hain.
  • COUNT(*) use karna. Ye NULL-extended row ko bhi 1 gin leta hai. COUNT(t.id) use karo.
  • Spine ki range hard-code karna. MIN/MAX date se ya parameter se lo.
  • created_at::date = s.day likhna. Index kaam nahi karta, range condition better hai.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Daily active users chart me missing days kaise fill karoge?
    A. Date spine banake LEFT JOIN karunga aur COALESCE(..., 0) lagaunga.
  • Q. Calendar table kab generate_series se better hai?
    A. Jab holiday, week number jaise attributes chahiye ya engine me generate_series na ho.

Yaad rakho

Spine left me, data right me, filter ON me, aur NULL ko COALESCE se zero.

SQL-21Cohort and retention queriesIntermediateMust Know

Users ko unki pehli activity ke mahine se group karo aur dekho baad me kitne wapas aaye.

Simple me samjho

Cohort matlab ek hi time pe join hue users ka group. Jaise May me register hue sab log "May cohort". Retention batata hai ki us group ke kitne log din 1, din 7 ya mahine 2 me wapas aaye.

Key points

  • First activity date: MIN(activity_date) per user. Ye har user ka cohort-start hai.
  • Cohort month: DATE_TRUNC('month', first_date). Isse user ek cohort me jaata hai.
  • Day-N retention: Activity date minus first date = day_n. Day 7 retention = day 7 pe active users / cohort size.
  • Cohort size: Day 0 pe COUNT(DISTINCT user_id). Yahi denominator hai.
  • Retention matrix: Rows = cohort month, columns = month index (0, 1, 2...). Month index = months between activity month aur cohort month.
  • Percentage: ROUND(100.0 * d7 / cohort_size, 1). Integer division se bachne ke liye 100.0 likho.
  • Unmatured cohorts: Agar cohort abhi 7 din ka hua hi nahi, to d7 ko NULL ya exclude karo. Warna retention kam dikhega.
  • Day-N vs rolling: Exact day N (strict) ya "N ke baad kabhi bhi" (rolling). Definition pehle fix karo.
  • Dialect: PostgreSQL me date - date integer deta hai. MySQL DATEDIFF(a, b), SQL Server DATEDIFF(day, b, a).

Example

sql
WITH first_act AS (
  SELECT user_id, MIN(activity_date) AS first_date
  FROM activity GROUP BY user_id
),
cohort AS (
  SELECT f.user_id,
         DATE_TRUNC('month', f.first_date)::date AS cohort_month,
         a.activity_date - f.first_date AS day_n
  FROM first_act f
  JOIN activity a ON a.user_id = f.user_id
)
SELECT cohort_month,
       COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FILTER (WHERE day_n = 0) AS cohort_size,
       COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FILTER (WHERE day_n = 1) AS d1,
       COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FILTER (WHERE day_n = 7) AS d7
FROM cohort
GROUP BY cohort_month
ORDER BY cohort_month;
text
cohort_month | cohort_size | d1 | d7
2024-04-01   | 200         | 80 | 40
2024-05-01   | 250         | 95 | 60

Pehle cohort ka D7 retention = 40/200 = 20%. (Numbers sample hain.)

Common mistakes

  • Cohort ko registration date se banana jab definition "first game played" hai.
  • COUNT(*) use karna. Ek user ki multiple rows hoti hain, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) lo.
  • Incomplete recent cohort ko bhi compare karna.
  • Timezone ignore karna. Din ki boundary UTC vs IST me badal jaati hai.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. D7 retention kaise nikaalte ho?
    A. First date nikaalo, activity ke saath join karke day_n = 7 wale distinct users ko cohort size se divide karo.
  • Q. Retention matrix ka denominator kya hota hai?
    A. Cohort size, yaani us cohort ke day 0 users.

Yaad rakho

First date, cohort, day_n, distinct users. Denominator hamesha cohort size.

SQL-22Funnel queriesIntermediateMust Know

Step by step conversion nikaalo, jaise signup se deposit se first game, aur dekho kahan users drop hue.

Simple me samjho

Funnel ek pipe jaisa hai. Signup ke baad kitne deposit tak pahunche, deposit ke baad kitne game tak. Har step pe users kam hote hain. Kahan sabse zyada gire, wahi drop-off hai.

Key points

  • Steps define karo: Event names fix karo, jaise signup, deposit, first_game.
  • Conditional aggregation: Per user MIN(event_time) FILTER (WHERE event_name = ...) se har step ka pehla time lo.
  • Ordered events: Step 2 ka time step 1 ke baad hona chahiye (t_deposit >= t_signup). Warna galat order bhi gin jaata hai.
  • Step conversion: Step n users / step n-1 users.
  • Overall conversion: Last step users / first step users.
  • Drop-off: 1 - step conversion, ya previous minus current.
  • CTE approach: Har step ka alag CTE, previous CTE se join. Padhne me saaf, par zyada code.
  • Time window: "7 din ke andar deposit" jaisi condition add karo.
  • Dialect: FILTER PostgreSQL feature hai. MySQL / SQL Server / BigQuery me MIN(CASE WHEN ... THEN event_time END).

Example

sql
WITH u AS (
  SELECT user_id,
    MIN(event_time) FILTER (WHERE event_name = 'signup')     AS t_signup,
    MIN(event_time) FILTER (WHERE event_name = 'deposit')    AS t_deposit,
    MIN(event_time) FILTER (WHERE event_name = 'first_game') AS t_game
  FROM events
  GROUP BY user_id
)
SELECT COUNT(t_signup) AS signup,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t_deposit >= t_signup) AS deposited,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE t_game >= t_deposit
                          AND t_deposit >= t_signup) AS played
FROM u;
text
signup | deposited | played
1000   | 400       | 300

Signup se deposit 40%, deposit se game 75%, overall 30%. Biggest drop-off signup se deposit me hai.

Common mistakes

  • Order check na karna. Game pehle aur deposit baad me ho to bhi user gin jaata hai.
  • Users ki jagah events gin lena. Hamesha distinct users per step.
  • Alag-alag date ranges har step pe lagana.
  • Step 3 ko step 1 se compare karna jab step 2 skip hua ho. Funnel strict hai ya loose, decide karo.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Funnel me ordered events kaise enforce karte ho?
    A. Per user har step ka MIN time lo aur next step ka time previous se bada ya barabar check karo.
  • Q. Conditional aggregation vs CTE?
    A. Conditional aggregation ek scan me hota hai, tez hai. CTE zyada readable hai jab logic complex ho.

Yaad rakho

Per user step ka first time, order check, phir distinct users gino.

SQL-23SessionizationAdvancedGood to Have

Events ko 30 minute inactivity rule se sessions me todo, phir session duration aur count nikaalo.

Simple me samjho

Raw events me session ka column nahi hota. Hum rule lagate hain: do events ke beech 30 minute se zyada gap ho to naya session. LAG se pichla event dekho, gap check karo, aur running sum se session id banao.

Key points

  • LAG with timeout: LAG(event_time) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_time) pichla event time deta hai.
  • New session flag: Agar prev_time IS NULL ya gap > timeout, to flag 1, warna 0.
  • Session id: Flag ka running SUM(...) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_time). Har naye flag pe id badhti hai.
  • Session duration: Session ke andar MAX(event_time) - MIN(event_time).
  • Session count: Per user distinct session ids ya MAX(session_id).
  • Single event session: Duration 0 aayegi. Ye normal hai, par report me note karo.
  • Timeout choice: 30 minute web analytics ka common default hai. Poker app me game ki nature dekh ke badlo.
  • Three steps: LAG, flag, running sum. Teen CTE me likho.
  • Dialect: Interval syntax alag hai. PostgreSQL INTERVAL '30 minutes', SQL Server DATEDIFF(minute, prev, curr) > 30.

Example

sql
WITH e AS (
  SELECT user_id, event_time,
         LAG(event_time) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_time) AS prev_time
  FROM events
),
f AS (
  SELECT *,
         CASE WHEN prev_time IS NULL
                OR event_time - prev_time > INTERVAL '30 minutes'
              THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_new
  FROM e
),
s AS (
  SELECT *, SUM(is_new) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_time) AS session_id
  FROM f
)
SELECT user_id, session_id,
       MIN(event_time) AS started_at,
       MAX(event_time) - MIN(event_time) AS duration,
       COUNT(*) AS events
FROM s
GROUP BY user_id, session_id;
text
user_id | session_id | started_at | duration | events
7       | 1          | 10:00      | 00:20:00 | 5
7       | 2          | 14:05      | 00:03:00 | 2

Common mistakes

  • PARTITION BY user_id bhool jaana. Sessions users ke beech mix ho jaate hain.
  • Running sum me ORDER BY na dena.
  • Same timestamp ke duplicate events pe tie-break na rakhna.
  • Sessions ko global unique maan lena. Id sirf user ke andar unique hai.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Session id SQL me kaise banate ho?
    A. LAG se gap nikaalo, gap > timeout pe flag 1, phir flag ka running sum.
  • Q. Session count per user kaise?
    A. Session id pe group karke COUNT(DISTINCT session_id) per user.

Yaad rakho

LAG, flag, running SUM. Teen kadam, session id ready.

SQL-24Percentiles and medianIntermediateGood to Have

Median aur percentiles outliers se bachte hain. PERCENTILE_CONT se nikaalo aur IQR se outliers pakdo.

Simple me samjho

Average ek bade deposit se bigad jaata hai. Median beech ki value hai, to wo stable rehta hai. Percentile batata hai ki kitne percent values us number se neeche hain.

Key points

  • PERCENTILE_CONT: PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY col). Interpolate karke value deta hai.
  • PERCENTILE_DISC: Actual existing value deta hai, interpolate nahi karta.
  • Median: 0.5 percentile. Even rows me CONT beech ki do values ka average deta hai.
  • Per group: Aggregate ki tarah GROUP BY ke saath chalta hai (PostgreSQL, Snowflake).
  • SQL Server: PERCENTILE_CONT sirf window function hai, OVER (PARTITION BY ...) ke saath. MySQL me built-in nahi, ROW_NUMBER se workaround.
  • Approximate median: Bade data pe tez. BigQuery APPROX_QUANTILES(x, 100)[OFFSET(50)], Snowflake APPROX_PERCENTILE, MEDIAN bhi hai (Snowflake, Redshift).
  • Outlier by IQR: Q1 - 1.5*IQR se neeche ya Q3 + 1.5*IQR se upar outlier hai. IQR = Q3 - Q1.
  • NULLs: Percentile functions NULL ignore karte hain.
  • Use: Deposit amount, session length, query latency jaise skewed data pe median/p95 report karo.

Example

sql
WITH q AS (
  SELECT PERCENTILE_CONT(0.25) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY amount) AS q1,
         PERCENTILE_CONT(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY amount) AS median,
         PERCENTILE_CONT(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY amount) AS q3
  FROM deposits
)
SELECT d.*
FROM deposits d CROSS JOIN q
WHERE d.amount > q.q3 + 1.5 * (q.q3 - q.q1)
   OR d.amount < q.q1 - 1.5 * (q.q3 - q.q1);

Amounts 10, 20, 30, 1000 ho to median 25 hai, average 265. Median zyada sahi "typical" value batata hai. 1000 outlier me pakda jaayega.

Common mistakes

  • Skewed data pe sirf AVG report karna.
  • CONT aur DISC ko same samajhna. Even count pe answer alag aata hai.
  • Outlier ko seedha delete kar dena. Pehle check karo ki wo fraud hai, bug hai ya real high roller.
  • Approximate function ko exact bata dena.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Median SQL me kaise nikaalte ho?
    A. PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY col). MySQL me row number se.
  • Q. Outlier SQL me kaise detect karoge?
    A. IQR rule ya z-score. Q1, Q3 nikaal ke fences ke bahar wali rows filter karo.

Yaad rakho

Skewed data me median aur p95, average nahi. Outlier pehle samjho, phir hatao.

SQL-25Views, materialized views, temp tablesIntermediateGood to Have

View saved query hai, materialized view stored result hai, temp table session ka scratch space hai.

Simple me samjho

View ek shortcut hai jo har baar query chalata hai. Materialized view result ko save karke rakhta hai. Temp table kaam khatam hote hi gayab ho jaata hai.

Key points

  • View: CREATE VIEW v_x AS SELECT .... Data store nahi hota, har baar query chalti hai. Logic reuse aur access control ke liye.
  • Materialized view: Result physically store hota hai. Padhna tez, par data purana ho sakta hai jab tak refresh na ho.
  • Refresh cost: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW mv_x poori query dobara chalata hai. PostgreSQL me CONCURRENTLY ke liye unique index chahiye.
  • Temp table: CREATE TEMP TABLE tmp_x AS .... Session khatam to drop. Bade intermediate result ya multi-step kaam me kaam aata hai.
  • CTE vs temp: CTE sirf ek query ke liye. Temp table me index laga sakte ho aur baar-baar use kar sakte ho.
  • Kab kya: Halka aur hamesha fresh data chahiye to view. Bhaari aggregation aur daily refresh chalega to materialized view. Ek hi session ka kaam to temp table.
  • Naming: v_ view, mv_ materialized view, tmp_ temp. Team convention follow karo.
  • Clean up: DROP VIEW IF EXISTS, DROP TABLE IF EXISTS. Shared schema me tmp tables chhodna galat hai.
  • Dialect: MySQL me materialized view nahi hai. SQL Server me indexed views. BigQuery aur Snowflake me materialized views ki limitations hoti hain.

Example

sql
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW mv_daily_deposits AS
SELECT created_at::date AS day, SUM(amount) AS total
FROM transactions
WHERE type = 'deposit'
GROUP BY 1;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON mv_daily_deposits (day);
REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY mv_daily_deposits;

Dashboard ab pre-computed table padhta hai. Refresh ke time par hi heavy query chalti hai.

Common mistakes

  • Materialized view refresh schedule na karna, aur purana data report karna.
  • Views ke upar views ke upar views banana. Debug aur performance dono kharab.
  • Temp tables ko drop na karna.
  • View ko "fast" samajhna. View sirf saved query hai, speed nahi badhata.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. View aur materialized view me fark?
    A. View query save karta hai, materialized view result save karta hai aur refresh maangta hai.
  • Q. Temp table kab use karoge?
    A. Jab bada intermediate result baar-baar use karna ho ya us par index chahiye.

Yaad rakho

View = fresh, MV = fast but stale, temp = scratch. Kaam ke baad safai.

SQL-26DDL and DMLBasicMust Know

DDL table ka structure badalta hai, DML data badalta hai. Production par WHERE aur backup ke bina kuch mat chalao.

Simple me samjho

DDL matlab table banana ya todna. DML matlab rows daalna, badalna, hatana. Galat UPDATE ya DELETE ek second me poora data bigaad sakta hai, isliye bahut dhyan se.

Key points

  • CREATE: CREATE TABLE players (id int, name text). Naya object banata hai.
  • ALTER: ALTER TABLE players ADD COLUMN country text. Structure badalta hai. Bade table pe lock lag sakta hai.
  • DROP: DROP TABLE players. Table aur data dono chale jaate hain. Pehle backup lo.
  • INSERT: INSERT INTO players (id, name) VALUES (1, 'Ravi').
  • UPDATE: UPDATE players SET country = 'IN' WHERE id = 1. WHERE bhoole to saari rows badal jaati hain.
  • DELETE: Rows hatata hai, WHERE ke saath. Transaction me rollback ho sakta hai.
  • TRUNCATE: Saari rows ek saath hatata hai, tez. PostgreSQL me transaction me rollback hota hai, MySQL me nahi.
  • UPSERT: PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE. MySQL ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE.
  • MERGE: SQL Server, Snowflake, BigQuery me MERGE. PostgreSQL 15+ me bhi hai.
  • Analyst ka rule: Production me aksar read-only access hota hai. Write karna pade to approval aur backup ke baad.

Example

sql
-- 1. Pehle SELECT se rows gino
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE status = 'pending' AND created_at < '2024-01-01';

-- 2. Transaction me chalao
BEGIN;
UPDATE users SET status = 'inactive'
WHERE status = 'pending' AND created_at < '2024-01-01';
-- output "UPDATE n" check karo, n step 1 ke barabar hona chahiye
COMMIT;   -- ya galat lage to ROLLBACK;

-- Upsert (PostgreSQL, user_id pe UNIQUE chahiye)
INSERT INTO player_stats (user_id, hands) VALUES (7, 10)
ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO UPDATE SET hands = player_stats.hands + EXCLUDED.hands;

Count match nahi kare to ROLLBACK karo aur condition dobara dekho.

Common mistakes

  • UPDATE / DELETE bina WHERE.
  • Production aur dev database ka connection confuse karna. Chalane se pehle database name dekho.
  • DROP ya TRUNCATE chalane se pehle backup na lena.
  • ON CONFLICT bina unique constraint ke likhna. Error aayega.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. DELETE, TRUNCATE aur DROP me fark?
    A. DELETE selected rows hatata hai. TRUNCATE saari rows hatata hai, table rehta hai. DROP table hi hata deta hai.
  • Q. Upsert kya hai?
    A. Row na ho to insert, ho to update. PostgreSQL me ON CONFLICT, MySQL me ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE.

Yaad rakho

Pehle SELECT, phir BEGIN, phir WHERE ke saath change. Production pe approval pehle.

SQL-27Constraints and keysBasicGood to Have

Constraints database ko galat data lene se rokte hain. PK, FK, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, CHECK aur DEFAULT.

Simple me samjho

Constraint ek gate-keeper hai. Galat row aayi to database use andar hi nahi aane deta. Isse data quality table level pe hi bani rehti hai.

Key points

  • PRIMARY KEY: Har row ki unique pehchaan. NULL nahi ho sakta, ek table me ek hi PK.
  • FOREIGN KEY: Doosre table ke key ko refer karta hai. Orphan rows rokta hai.
  • UNIQUE: Duplicate values nahi. PK ke ulta, ek se zyada UNIQUE constraints ho sakte hain.
  • NOT NULL: Column khaali nahi reh sakta.
  • CHECK: Custom rule, jaise CHECK (chips >= 0).
  • DEFAULT: Value na di jaaye to default lagti hai, jaise DEFAULT now().
  • Referential integrity: Child me wahi value jo parent me hai. ON DELETE CASCADE child ko bhi hata deta hai, RESTRICT delete rok deta hai.
  • Index: PK aur UNIQUE par index apne aap banta hai. PostgreSQL me FK par nahi banta.
  • Warehouses: BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift me PK/FK sirf informational hote hain, enforce nahi hote (Snowflake NOT NULL enforce karta hai). Duplicates khud check karo.
  • MySQL: CHECK 8.0.16 se enforce hota hai.

Example

sql
CREATE TABLE users (
  user_id    bigint PRIMARY KEY,
  email      text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  country    text DEFAULT 'IN',
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE wallets (
  wallet_id bigint PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id   bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES users (user_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  chips     numeric NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (chips >= 0)
);

Negative chips ya missing user ke liye wallet insert karne par database error dega.

Common mistakes

  • Warehouse me PK dekh ke maan lena ki duplicates nahi honge.
  • FK column par index na banana. Join aur delete slow hote hain.
  • Business rule ko sirf app me rakhna aur DB me CHECK na lagana.
  • CASCADE bina soche lagana. Ek delete se bahut kuch hat sakta hai.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. PK aur UNIQUE me fark?
    A. PK NULL nahi leta aur table me ek hi hota hai. UNIQUE multiple ho sakte hain.
  • Q. Referential integrity kya hai?
    A. FK ki value hamesha parent table me maujood honi chahiye, orphan row nahi.

Yaad rakho

PK pehchaan, FK rishta, UNIQUE no-duplicate, CHECK rule. Warehouse me enforce nahi hota.

SQL-28IndexesIntermediateGood to Have

Index ek sorted shortcut hai jo lookups tez karta hai, par writes ko slow karta hai.

Simple me samjho

Kitaab ke peeche ka index dekho. Poori kitaab padhne ki jagah seedha page number milta hai. Database me bhi index se poora table scan nahi karna padta.

Key points

  • Kaise tez karta hai: Zyadatar B-tree sorted structure. Seq scan ki jagah seedha matching rows tak pahunchta hai.
  • Create: CREATE INDEX idx_name ON table (col).
  • Composite index: (user_id, created_at). Order matter karta hai.
  • Leftmost prefix: Index (a, b) filter a ya a AND b me kaam karega. Sirf b pe nahi.
  • Kab help nahi karta: Low selectivity column (jaise boolean), chhota table, LIKE '%abc', column pe function (DATE(col)), type mismatch.
  • Write cost: Har INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE par index bhi update hota hai. Zyada index to writes slow.
  • Space: Index disk leta hai.
  • PostgreSQL extras: Partial index (WHERE status = 'open') aur covering index (INCLUDE).
  • Analyst ke liye: Slow query ho to check karo ki filter/join columns par index hai ya nahi, aur DBA se request karo.
  • Warehouses: BigQuery/Snowflake me traditional index nahi hote. Partition aur clustering use hota hai.

Example

sql
CREATE INDEX idx_tx_user_created ON transactions (user_id, created_at);

-- Index use hoga
WHERE user_id = 7 AND created_at >= '2024-05-01'
WHERE user_id = 7

-- Index use nahi hoga (leading column nahi)
WHERE created_at >= '2024-05-01'

-- Index use nahi hoga (function)
WHERE DATE(created_at) = '2024-05-01'

Last wale ko created_at >= '2024-05-01' AND created_at < '2024-05-02' likho to index chalega.

Common mistakes

  • Har column pe index laga dena. Writes slow ho jaate hain.
  • Composite index ka order galat rakhna.
  • Index bana ke verify na karna ki plan me use hua ya nahi.
  • Low cardinality column (status with 2 values) pe akela index banana.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Index query tez kyun karta hai?
    A. Sorted structure se matching rows seedha mil jaati hain, poora table scan nahi hota.
  • Q. Index ke nuksan?
    A. Write slow hota hai aur extra storage lagti hai.

Yaad rakho

Index reads ko tez, writes ko slow karta hai. Leftmost column aur plain filter yaad rakho.

SQL-29Execution plans (EXPLAIN)IntermediateGood to Have

EXPLAIN batata hai database query ko kaise chalayega. Scan type, join type aur cost yahin dikhta hai.

Simple me samjho

Plan ek route map hai. Database batata hai kaunsa raasta chuna aur kitna time lagega. Slow query ko fix karne se pehle plan padho.

Key points

  • EXPLAIN: Sirf plan dikhata hai, query nahi chalata.
  • EXPLAIN ANALYZE: PostgreSQL me query asli me chalata hai aur actual time dikhata hai. UPDATE/DELETE par savdhan, wo bhi chal jaayega.
  • Seq Scan: Poora table padhta hai. Bade table pe filter ke saath ho to red flag.
  • Index Scan: Index se rows dhoondhta hai. Chhote result ke liye achha.
  • Join strategy: Nested Loop (chhote set), Hash Join (bade unsorted), Merge Join (sorted inputs).
  • Cost: cost=startup..total relative unit hai, seconds nahi. Plans compare karne ke liye.
  • Rows estimate vs actual: Bada fark ho to statistics purani hain. ANALYZE table_name chalao.
  • Plan ko neeche se upar padho: Sabse andar wala node pehle chalta hai.
  • Other tools: MySQL EXPLAIN (8.0.18+ me EXPLAIN ANALYZE), SQL Server actual execution plan, BigQuery execution graph, Snowflake Query Profile.

Example

sql
EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT * FROM transactions WHERE user_id = 7;
text
Index Scan using idx_tx_user_created on transactions
  (cost=0.43..8.45 rows=3 width=40) (actual time=0.03..0.04 rows=3 loops=1)
  Index Cond: (user_id = 7)
Planning Time: 0.1 ms
Execution Time: 0.06 ms

Index nahi hota to yahan Seq Scan aur Filter: (user_id = 7) dikhta, aur time kaafi zyada hota.

Common mistakes

  • Cost ko seconds samajhna.
  • EXPLAIN ANALYZE ko production me bhaari DML par chalana.
  • Chhote table par Seq Scan dekh ke panic karna. Wo sahi choice ho sakta hai.
  • Sirf plan dekhna, estimated vs actual rows compare na karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. EXPLAIN aur EXPLAIN ANALYZE me fark?
    A. EXPLAIN estimate dikhata hai. ANALYZE query chalake actual time aur rows dikhata hai.
  • Q. Seq Scan hamesha bura hai?
    A. Nahi. Chhote table ya bade result ke liye wahi best hota hai.

Yaad rakho

Plan padho, guess mat karo. Scan type, join type, estimate vs actual dekho.

SQL-30Query optimisationAdvancedMust Know

Kam data padho, jaldi filter karo, aur indexes/partitions ka fayda uthao. Ye sabse practical SQL skill hai.

Simple me samjho

Query slow hoti hai jab zyada data padha jaata hai. Goal hai database ko kam se kam rows aur columns chhuane dena. Chhote chhote habits se query 10x tez ho sakti hai.

Key points

  • Needed columns hi: Sirf zaroori columns select karo. Columnar warehouse me isse seedha cost kam hota hai.
  • SELECT * avoid: Extra data, extra network, aur schema badle to query tootti hai.
  • Filter early: WHERE aur date range jaldi lagao. Join se pehle subquery/CTE me data chhota karo.
  • Partition pruning: Partition column (jaise date) pe seedha filter lagao. Tabhi baaki partitions skip hote hain.
  • No function on indexed column: WHERE DATE(created_at) = ... ki jagah range likho.
  • Cross join explosion: Many-to-many join se rows multiply hoti hain. Join se pehle key uniqueness check karo.
  • Sampling: Exploration ke liye sample lo. PostgreSQL TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM (1), Snowflake SAMPLE (1), BigQuery TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM (1 PERCENT).
  • LIMIT sirf print kam karta hai: BigQuery me LIMIT se scanned bytes (cost) kam nahi hote.
  • EXISTS vs IN: Bade subquery pe EXISTS aksar safe hai. Plan se verify karo.
  • Pehle measure karo: EXPLAIN dekho, phir optimise karo.

Example

sql
-- Slow
SELECT *
FROM events
WHERE DATE(event_time) = '2024-05-01';

-- Fast
SELECT user_id, event_name, event_time
FROM events
WHERE event_time >= '2024-05-01'
  AND event_time <  '2024-05-02';

Dusri query index aur partition pruning dono use kar sakti hai, aur sirf 3 columns padhti hai.

Common mistakes

  • Pehle poora join karke baad me filter karna.
  • Many-to-many join me row count check na karna. Totals phool jaate hain.
  • Partition column pe cast ya function laga dena. Pruning band ho jaati hai.
  • Bina sample ke bade table pe baar-baar test query chalana.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Slow query ko kaise optimise karoge?
    A. EXPLAIN dekhunga, columns aur rows kam karunga, filter early lagaunga, index/partition ka use sunishchit karunga.
  • Q. Index column pe function kyun bura hai?
    A. Index raw value par bana hota hai. Function lagane par database index use nahi kar paata.

Yaad rakho

Kam columns, kam rows, plain filter, partition pe date. Pehle EXPLAIN.

SQL-31Transactions and ACIDIntermediateGood to Have

Transaction ek saath poora hota hai ya bilkul nahi. ACID, isolation levels aur locks data ko sahi rakhte hain.

Simple me samjho

Bank transfer socho: ek account se paisa kata, doosre me nahi gaya to gadbad. Transaction dono steps ko ek unit banata hai. Ya dono hon, ya koi nahi.

Key points

  • BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK: BEGIN shuru, COMMIT save, ROLLBACK sab undo.
  • Atomicity: Saare steps ya to poore hote hain ya koi nahi.
  • Consistency: Transaction ke baad constraints sahi rehte hain.
  • Isolation: Parallel transactions ek doosre ko disturb na karein.
  • Durability: COMMIT ke baad data crash me bhi safe.
  • Isolation levels: Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable. PostgreSQL ka default Read Committed hai. MySQL InnoDB ka default Repeatable Read.
  • Dirty / non-repeatable / phantom read: Strong level pe ye problems kam hoti hain, par performance cost badhta hai.
  • Locks: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE row lock karta hai. Doosra transaction wait karta hai.
  • Deadlock: Do transactions ek doosre ka lock maang rahe hain. Database ek ko rok deta hai (error).
  • Analyst warning: Khula transaction (COMMIT bhoolna) doosron ko block kar sakta hai.

Example

sql
BEGIN;
UPDATE wallets SET chips = chips - 500 WHERE user_id = 1 AND chips >= 500;
-- "UPDATE 0" aaye to ROLLBACK; (balance kam tha)
UPDATE wallets SET chips = chips + 500 WHERE user_id = 2;
COMMIT;

Dono updates ek saath save hote hain. Beech me error aaye to ROLLBACK se dono wapas.

Common mistakes

  • BEGIN ke baad COMMIT/ROLLBACK bhool jaana. Locks atke rehte hain.
  • Balance guard (chips >= 500) na lagana aur negative balance bana dena.
  • Lambi transaction rakhna. Doosre queries wait karte hain.
  • Isolation level badalne ke side effects na samajhna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. ACID kya hai?
    A. Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability. Transaction ki reliability ke chaar guarantees.
  • Q. Deadlock kya hota hai?
    A. Do transactions ek doosre ka lock maangte hain aur atak jaate hain. DB ek ko abort kar deta hai.

Yaad rakho

Paisa jaise kaam ek transaction me. COMMIT ya ROLLBACK, kabhi adhoora nahi.

SQL-32Stored procedures, functions, triggersAdvancedBonus

Database ke andar saved logic. Analyst ko mostly padhna padta hai, kabhi kabhi chhota function likhna padta hai.
