# test_utils.py
import pytest
from utils import rake_amount

def test_rake_basic():
    assert rake_amount(1000) == 50

def test_rake_negative():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        rake_amount(-1)
text
$ pytest
test_utils.py ..                                    [100%]
2 passed

Ek function, uska docstring aur type hints, aur 2 tests (normal aur error case).

Common mistakes

  • 300 line ka ek script, koi function nahi.
  • Tests na likhna, ya sirf happy path test karna.
  • Type hints ko runtime guarantee samajhna.
  • Vague naam (df2, temp, x).
  • Bina formatter ke style inconsistent chhodna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Type hints ka fayda?
    A. Code padhne me aasan, editor autocomplete aur static checkers (jaise mypy) bugs pakadte hain. Runtime pe enforce nahi hote.
  • Q. pytest me test kaise likhte hain?
    A. test_ se shuru hone wale functions me plain assert; exceptions ke liye pytest.raises.

Yaad rakho

Chhote named functions, type hints + docstring, aur pytest me kam se kam ek test.

PY-26DebuggingBasicMust Know

Error aaye to ghabrao mat: stack trace padho, print debugging, pdb aur minimal reproducible example se bug pakdo.

Simple me samjho

Bug dhundhna detective ka kaam hai. Traceback batata hai kahan toota, tumhe sochna hai kyun. Systematic raho: reproduce, isolate, fix, verify.

Key points

  • Traceback padhna: neeche se upar padho. Last line = error type aur message. Uske upar = kis file/line pe, aur call chain.
  • Common errors: KeyError (key nahi), AttributeError (object pe wo method nahi), TypeError, ValueError, IndexError, NameError.
  • Print debugging: print(type(x), x.shape, x.head()) se actual values dekho, anumaan nahi.
  • f-string debug: print(f"{len(df)=}").
  • pdb: breakpoint() likho, script wahan ruk jaati hai. Commands: n next line, s step into, c continue, p var print, l list code, q quit.
  • Post-mortem: Jupyter me %debug fail hone ke baad chalao.
  • Minimal reproducible example: chhota data (3-5 rows) aur kam code jo wahi bug dikhaye. Aksar banate hue hi cause mil jata hai.
  • Binary search: code ko beech se do hisso me baanto aur check karo bug kis hisse me hai.
  • Check assumptions: dtypes, nulls, index alignment, duplicates.
  • Pandas warnings: SettingWithCopyWarning ko ignore mat karo.
  • Ek baar me ek change: ek time pe ek cheez badlo, phir test karo.

Example

python
bets = {"a": 100, "b": "x"}
total = sum(bets.values())
text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "report.py", line 2, in <module>
    total = sum(bets.values())
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'int' and 'str'

Last line batati hai ki int aur str ko jodne ki koshish hui. Line 2 pe bets.values() me ek value string hai. Debug ke liye print(bets) ya breakpoint() lagao, phir "x" ko clean karo (pandas me pd.to_numeric(s, errors="coerce")).

Common mistakes

  • Traceback ki last line padhe bina code badalna shuru kar dena.
  • Ek saath kai changes karke fix test karna.
  • Bade data pe debug karna; chhota sample banao.
  • Debug print ya breakpoint() production code me chhod dena.
  • Error message Google/AI se paste karna bina apne code ka context samjhe.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Stack trace kaise padhte ho?
    A. Neeche se: pehle error type aur message, phir upar jaake apni file ki line dhundho jahan error trigger hua.
  • Q. Minimal reproducible example kyun?
    A. Bug ko chhote self-contained case me isolate karta hai. Cause jaldi milta hai aur dusron se madad maangna aasan hota hai.

Yaad rakho

Last line se shuru, values print karo, chhota example banao, ek baar me ek change.

PY-27OOP basicsIntermediateBonus

Classes aur methods ka basic idea. Analysts ko kam hi zaroorat padti hai, par libraries samajhne aur reusable tools banane me kaam aata hai.

Simple me samjho

Class ek blueprint hai, object uska actual instance. Isme data (attributes) aur kaam (methods) saath rehte hain. pandas ka DataFrame bhi ek class hai: df.head() us class ka method hai.

Key points

  • class: class Player: se blueprint banta hai.
  • __init__: constructor, object banate waqt attributes set karta hai.
  • self: object khud. Har instance method ka pehla parameter.
  • Attributes: self.name = name, object ka data.
  • Methods: class ke andar functions, obj.method() se call.
  • Object banana: p = Player("Aman", 500).
  • __repr__: object print karne par kya dikhe.
  • dataclass: @dataclass simple data holder ke liye boilerplate kam karta hai.
  • Inheritance: class VipPlayer(Player): parent ka behaviour reuse. Analyst code me kam use hota hai.
  • Analysts ko kab chahiye: reusable report builder, API/DB client wrapper, ya library ke custom objects. Zyada tar kaam functions se chal jata hai.
  • Library se samajh: pd.read_csv function hai, uska result DataFrame object hai jiske methods hote hain.

Example

python
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass
class Player:
    name: str
    chips: int

    def add_chips(self, amount: int) -> None:
        self.chips += amount

class ReportBuilder:
    def __init__(self, title):
        self.title = title
        self.lines = []

    def add(self, text):
        self.lines.append(text)
        return self

    def render(self):
        return "\n".join([self.title, *self.lines])

p = Player("Aman", 500)
p.add_chips(250)
print(p)
print(ReportBuilder("Daily").add("rev: 1200").add("users: 40").render())
text
Player(name='Aman', chips=750)
Daily
rev: 1200
users: 40

dataclass ne __init__ aur repr khud bana diye. ReportBuilder me state (lines) object ke andar rehti hai.

Common mistakes

  • Har chhoti cheez ke liye class banana jab function kaafi hai.
  • self bhool jana, TypeError.
  • Class-level mutable attribute (lines = []) jo sab objects share karte hain.
  • Deep inheritance; composition ya simple functions behtar.
  • __init__ me heavy kaam (DB query) kar dena.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Class aur object me farq?
    A. Class blueprint hai, object us blueprint se bana instance, jiska apna data hota hai.
  • Q. Analyst ko OOP kab chahiye?
    A. Jab state ke saath reusable tool banana ho (report builder, API client) ya library ke objects samajhne hon. Warna functions kaafi hain.

Yaad rakho

Class = data + methods ek saath; pehle function try karo, zaroorat pade to class.

PY-28Streamlit and Python dashboardsIntermediateBonus

Streamlit se chand lines me interactive internal app ya demo ban jata hai: filters, charts aur tables. Frontend ki zaroorat nahi.

Simple me samjho

Streamlit ek Python script ko web app bana deta hai. Tum widgets (slider, dropdown) aur charts Python me likhte ho. Team ke liye quick dashboard ya demo ke liye perfect hai.

Key points

  • Install/run: pip install streamlit, streamlit run app.py.
  • Display: st.title(), st.write(), st.dataframe(df), st.metric("Revenue", 1200).
  • Widgets: st.selectbox, st.multiselect, st.slider, st.date_input, st.sidebar.
  • Charts: st.line_chart(df), st.bar_chart(df), ya st.pyplot(fig), st.plotly_chart(fig).
  • Rerun model: widget badalte hi poora script upar se dobara chalta hai.
  • Caching: @st.cache_data data load function pe lagao, baar-baar DB query nahi hoti.
  • Layout: st.columns(3), st.tabs([...]).
  • Secrets: DB credentials env variables ya Streamlit ke secrets se, code me nahi.
  • Sharing: internal server/container pe deploy; access control socho kyunki data sensitive ho sakta hai.
  • Other options: Plotly Dash, Panel, ya BI tools (Power BI/Tableau) production dashboards ke liye.
  • Limits: quick tool ke liye theek, bade multi-user production dashboards ke liye BI tool ya proper app.

Example

python
# app.py  ->  streamlit run app.py
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

@st.cache_data
def load():
    return pd.DataFrame({
        "game": ["NLH", "PLO", "NLH", "PLO"],
        "day": [1, 1, 2, 2],
        "revenue": [100, 60, 120, 80],
    })

df = load()
st.title("Revenue dashboard")
games = st.sidebar.multiselect("Game", df["game"].unique(),
                               default=list(df["game"].unique()))
view = df[df["game"].isin(games)]
st.metric("Total revenue", int(view["revenue"].sum()))
st.line_chart(view.pivot(index="day", columns="game", values="revenue"))
st.dataframe(view)
text
Browser opens at http://localhost:8501 with a sidebar filter, a metric, a line chart and a table.

Sidebar se game chunte hi script dobara chalta hai aur metric, chart aur table update ho jaate hain.

Common mistakes

  • Cache na lagana, har interaction pe DB query.
  • Sensitive data ko bina access control ke share karna.
  • Credentials app code me hardcode karna.
  • Rerun model na samajhna; widget badalne pe saara code dobara chalta hai.
  • Streamlit ko full production BI replacement samajhna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Streamlit kaise kaam karta hai?
    A. Python script upar se neeche chalti hai, har widget interaction pe poori script dobara run hoti hai. st.* calls UI banate hain.
  • Q. Streamlit vs Power BI?
    A. Streamlit code-first, custom aur quick Python demos ke liye. Power BI business users ke self-service aur governed dashboards ke liye.

Yaad rakho

Script hi app hai; cache lagao, secrets env me rakho, aur isse quick internal tool samjho.

Statistics 24 topics

ST-01Types of dataBasicMust Know

Data ke types samajhna zaroori hai kyunki type decide karta hai ki kaunsa chart, kaunsi statistic aur kaunsa test lagega.

Simple me samjho

Data ek tarah ka measurement hota hai. Kabhi label hota hai (country), kabhi order (VIP level), kabhi exact number (chips). Jaise school me: roll number sirf naam hai, rank order hai, marks gin sakte ho. Har ek ke saath alag math chalta hai.

Key points

  • Categorical: values groups hote hain (country, game_type, device). Average meaningless hota hai.
  • Numerical: values numbers hain jin par math ho sakta hai (chips, session_minutes).
  • Nominal: categorical, koi order nahi. Example: game_type = Holdem, Omaha, Rummy.
  • Ordinal: categorical, par order hai aur gap equal nahi. Example: VIP level Bronze < Silver < Gold.
  • Interval: numeric, difference meaningful hai par true zero nahi. Example: temperature in Celsius, calendar year. Ratio (2x) ka matlab nahi banta.
  • Ratio: numeric, true zero hai, so ratios valid hain. Example: chips balance, hands_played, revenue. 0 matlab "kuch nahi".
  • Discrete: gine jaane wale integers (hands played, logins). Gap ke beech values nahi.
  • Continuous: measure hone wale, decimals possible (session duration, latency in ms).
  • Trap: user_id, pin code, phone number numbers dikhte hain par nominal hain. Inka sum/mean nahi nikalte.

Example

python
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "user_id": [101, 102, 103],
    "vip": pd.Categorical(["Gold", "Bronze", "Silver"],
                          categories=["Bronze", "Silver", "Gold"], ordered=True),
    "hands_played": [250, 40, 900],
    "avg_session_min": [42.5, 10.2, 95.0],
})
print(df.dtypes)
print(df["vip"] > "Bronze")   # ordinal compare works

user_id ko int se str/category me convert karo. vip ordered category hai, isliye comparison chalta hai. hands_played discrete ratio hai, avg_session_min continuous ratio.

Common mistakes

  • ID columns ka mean ya correlation nikalna.
  • Ordinal (1-5 rating) ko interval maan kar mean lena bina soche. Gaps equal nahi hote.
  • Discrete data ko continuous jaisa histogram me bin karna bina bin width check kiye.
  • Celsius me ratio bolna ("40 degree is twice 20"). Ye interval hai.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Nominal aur ordinal me kya fark hai?
    A. Dono categorical hain. Ordinal me natural order hota hai (Low < Medium < High), nominal me nahi (country).
  • Q. Interval aur ratio me fark?
    A. Ratio me true zero hota hai, to "double" bolna valid hai (chips). Interval me nahi (Celsius).
  • Q. Rating 1 to 5 kaunsa type hai?
    A. Ordinal. Practice me mean lete hain par gaps equal hone ki assumption hoti hai.

Yaad rakho

Type pehle pehchano: label ya number, order hai ya nahi, true zero hai ya nahi, phir stat chuno.

ST-02Descriptive statisticsBasicMust Know

Data ko ek-do numbers me summarize karna: center (mean/median/mode) aur spread (variance, SD, IQR). Skewed data me mean dhoka deta hai.

Simple me samjho

Descriptive stats ek lambi list ka "chhota sa chehra" hain. Center batata hai data kahan baitha hai, spread batata hai kitna failla hai. Jaise ek tournament ke 7 players ka buy-in: ek whale poore average ko kheench leta hai.

Key points

  • Mean: sum / n. Har value use karta hai, isliye outlier se hil jata hai.
  • Median: sorted data ki beech wali value. Outlier-resistant.
  • Mode: sabse zyada aane wali value. Categorical data ke liye bhi chalta hai.
  • Range: max - min. Sirf 2 values par depend, kaafi unstable.
  • Variance: average squared distance from mean. Sample ke liye n-1 se divide (ddof=1).
  • Standard deviation (SD): sqrt(variance). Original unit me hota hai, isliye samajhna aasan.
  • IQR: Q3 - Q1, beech ke 50% data ka spread. Outlier se safe.
  • Formula: variance = sum((x - mean)^2) / (n - 1). SD = sqrt(variance).
  • Mean kab misleads: right-skewed data (spend, deposits, rake), outliers, bimodal data. Wahan median + percentiles report karo.

Example

python
import numpy as np
x = np.array([10, 20, 20, 30, 40, 50, 500])   # buy-ins
print(x.mean(), np.median(x))                 # 95.71  30.0
print(x.std(ddof=1))                          # 178.78
q1, q3 = np.percentile(x, [25, 75])           # 20, 45
print(q3 - q1, x.max() - x.min())             # IQR 25, range 490

Mode 20 hai. Mean 95.71 hai par 7 me se 6 players isse kam hain, kyunki 500 ne kheench diya. Median 30 zyada sahi "typical" hai. 500 hata do to mean 28.33 ho jata hai. SD 178.78 bhi usi outlier se bada hai, IQR 25 stable hai.

Common mistakes

  • Skewed money data par sirf mean report karna.
  • Population (ddof=0) aur sample (ddof=1) SD mix karna. pandas .std() default ddof=1, numpy np.std default ddof=0.
  • SD ko bina mean ke samajhna. SD 10 chhota hai ya bada, mean par depend karta hai.
  • Mode ko bhool jana jab data bimodal ho (casual aur grinder players).

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Mean aur median me kab farak aata hai?
    A. Jab data skewed ya outlier wala ho. Right skew me mean > median.
  • Q. Sample variance me n-1 kyun?
    A. Sample mean ke around spread kam dikhta hai, isliye n-1 (Bessel correction) se unbiased estimate milta hai.
  • Q. Spread ke liye SD ya IQR?
    A. Normal-ish data me SD, skewed ya outlier wale data me IQR.

Yaad rakho

Skewed ho to mean ke saath median aur IQR bhi dikhao.

ST-03DistributionsBasicMust Know

Distribution batata hai values kitni baar aur kahan aati hain. Sahi shape pehchano to sahi model aur test chuno.

Simple me samjho

Distribution ek "map" hai ki kaunsi value kitni likely hai. Bell curve me beech me bheed hoti hai, long-tail me chhote log bahut aur kuch log gigantic. Poker spend aksar second type ka hota hai.

Key points

  • Normal: bell shape, mean = median, symmetric. Heights, averages of many things.
  • Skewed: ek taraf lambi tail. Right-skew me mean > median (spend, session length).
  • Uniform: har value equally likely (fair die, random hash bucket).
  • Binomial: n independent trials, p success. P(X=k) = C(n,k) * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k). Example: 5 hands me kitne jeete.
  • Poisson: fixed time me events ki count, rate lambda. P(X=k) = e^-lambda * lambda^k / k!. Example: logins per hour.
  • Exponential: do events ke beech ka waiting time. P(T > t) = e^(-t/mean). Poisson ka "partner".
  • Long-tail business data: top 1-5% users 50%+ revenue deta hai (Pareto jaisa). Log transform ya median/percentile use karo.
  • Mean-vs-SD ke bharose normal assume mat karo; histogram aur QQ plot dekho.

Example

python
from scipy import stats
# Binomial: 5 hands, p(win)=0.3
print(stats.binom.pmf(2, 5, 0.3))        # 0.3087  exactly 2 wins
print(1 - stats.binom.cdf(1, 5, 0.3))    # 0.4718  at least 2 wins
# Poisson: avg 3 logins/hour
print(stats.poisson.pmf(0, 3))           # 0.0498  no login in an hour
# Exponential: mean wait 5 min
print(stats.expon.sf(10, scale=5))       # 0.1353  wait > 10 min

Exactly 2 wins ki chance 30.87%, kam se kam 2 ki 47.18%. Ek ghante me 0 login ki chance ~5%. 5 min average wait me 10 min se zyada wait e^-2 = 13.5%.

Common mistakes

  • Revenue ko normal maan kar mean +- 2 SD lagana.
  • Poisson use karna jab events independent na hon (bonus campaign ke time spikes).
  • Binomial me trials independent na hone par bhi use karna.
  • Long-tail data ka average dekh kar "typical user" bolna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Binomial vs Poisson?
    A. Binomial me fixed n trials aur success count. Poisson me fixed time window me events ki count, koi upper limit nahi.
  • Q. Spend data kaisa distribution hota hai?
    A. Right-skewed, long-tail. Isliye median, percentiles ya log scale use karte hain.
  • Q. Exponential ka memoryless matlab?
    A. Ab tak kitna wait kiya ye aage ke wait ko affect nahi karta.

Yaad rakho

Pehle histogram dekho, phir model chuno. Money data = long-tail.

ST-04Percentiles and quartilesBasicMust Know

Percentile batata hai ki kitne percent data us value se neeche hai. Latency aur spend ke liye mean se behtar report.

Simple me samjho

P90 = 870 ka matlab 90% requests 870 ms ya usse tez hain. Baaki 10% slow hain. Mean "average user" batata hai, percentile "bad experience wale users" batata hai.

Key points

  • Percentile: P50 = median, P90 = 90% neeche, P99 = 99% neeche.
  • Quartiles: Q1 = P25, Q2 = P50, Q3 = P75. IQR = Q3 - Q1.
  • Box plot: box = Q1 se Q3, line = median, whiskers = normally 1.5 * IQR tak, uske bahar dots = outliers.
  • Latency reporting: P50 (typical), P95/P99 (tail). SLA aksar P95 ya P99 par bante hain.
  • Spend reporting: "top 10% players = P90 se upar" jaisa segmentation. Median spend + P90 spend dikhao.
  • Interpolation: numpy default linear interpolation karta hai, isliye P90 data me na hone wali value bhi ho sakti hai.
  • Percentiles ko average nahi karte: do servers ke P99 ka average = overall P99 nahi. Raw data ya histogram se nikalo.
  • Percentile rank: ek value ka rank kitna percent. "Ye player spend me P95 par hai."

Example

python
import numpy as np
lat = np.array([80,85,90,95,100,105,110,120,130,140,
                150,160,180,200,250,300,400,800,1500,3000])  # ms
print(lat.mean())                              # 399.75
print(np.percentile(lat, [50, 90, 95, 99]))    # 145, 870, 1575, 2715
print(np.percentile(lat, [25, 75]))            # 103.75, 262.5

Mean 399.75 ms dikhata hai par median sirf 145 ms. Tail (P99 = 2715 ms) me asli dard hai. Is liye report: "P50 145 ms, P95 1575 ms, P99 2715 ms".

Common mistakes

  • Sirf average latency report karna, jisse tail problems chhup jati hain.
  • Pre-aggregated P99 ko average karna.
  • Chhote sample (20 points) par P99 bharosemand maan lena.
  • Pandas quantile(0.9) aur SQL percentile_cont(0.9) ko same assume karna jab method alag ho.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. P99 kyun important hai?
    A. Chhote % users ka worst experience dikhata hai, jo mean me dab jata hai.
  • Q. Box plot kya dikhata hai?
    A. Median, Q1, Q3, whiskers aur outliers, yani spread aur skew ek hi chart me.
  • Q. Do groups ke P90 spend ko merge kaise karein?
    A. Raw rows combine karke dobara P90 nikalo, average mat lo.

Yaad rakho

Latency aur spend: mean nahi, P50 + P90/P99 dikhao.

ST-05OutliersIntermediateMust Know

Outlier wo value hai jo baaki data se bahut alag ho. Pehchano, samjho kyun hai, phir remove ya keep ka sochke decide karo.

Simple me samjho

Outlier ya to error hota hai (bot, test account, bug) ya real extreme (whale player). Dono ka treatment alag hai. Pehle "kyun" poocho, phir "kya karein".

Key points

  • Z-score: z = (x - mean) / SD. Aam rule: |z| > 3 outlier. Normal-ish data me kaam karta hai.
  • Z-score ki limit: outlier khud mean aur SD ko bada kar deta hai, isliye khud ko mask karta hai. Chhote n me max z = (n-1)/sqrt(n) se zyada ho hi nahi sakta.
  • IQR rule: Q1 - 1.5*IQR se neeche ya Q3 + 1.5*IQR se upar. Robust hai, skewed data me bhi theek.
  • Winsorising: extreme values ko cap karna (jaise P1 aur P99 par), rows delete nahi hote.
  • Remove: sirf tab jab confirmed error ho (negative chips, duplicate bug).
  • Keep: real whales ko hatana revenue ka sach badal deta hai. Keep karo, alag segment ya median use karo.
  • Test accounts and bots: internal QA IDs aur bot accounts filter karo. Ye outlier nahi, "galat population" hai.
  • Hamesha document karo: kitni rows hatayi aur kis rule se.

Example

python
import numpy as np
d = np.array([10, 12, 11, 13, 12, 11, 14, 12, 200])
z = (d - d.mean()) / d.std(ddof=1)
print(z.max())                       # 2.67  -> |z| > 3 se miss!
q1, q3 = np.percentile(d, [25, 75])  # 11, 13
iqr = q3 - q1                        # 2
print(q1 - 1.5*iqr, q3 + 1.5*iqr)    # 8.0, 16.0 -> 200 flagged

Mean 32.78 aur SD 62.72 ho gaye, isliye 200 ka z sirf 2.67 aaya aur z-score rule ne use miss kar diya. IQR rule ne fence 8 se 16 diya aur 200 pakad liya.

Common mistakes

  • Har outlier ko blindly delete karna.
  • Outlier hatane se pehle mean/SD par z-score use karna.
  • Bots/test accounts ko filter na karna aur metrics inflate hona.
  • Winsorise karke batana bhool jana, jisse numbers reproduce nahi hote.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Outlier ko remove kab karte hain?
    A. Jab wo data error ya non-target population ho (bot, test account). Real extreme values ko keep karte hain.
  • Q. Z-score vs IQR?
    A. Z-score normal data me, par outlier se khud affect hota hai. IQR robust hai.
  • Q. Winsorising kya hai?
    A. Extremes ko percentile cap par replace karna, rows bachi rehti hain.

Yaad rakho

Pehle pucho "ye kyun hai", phir remove, cap ya keep decide karo.

ST-06Correlation vs causationBasicMust Know

Correlation batata hai do cheezein saath move karti hain. Causation batata hai ek doosre ko karti hai. Dono alag hain.

Simple me samjho

Garmi me ice cream aur drowning dono badhte hain. Ice cream drowning nahi karata, garmi (confounder) dono ko badhati hai. Data me jo saath dikhe, wo hamesha cause nahi hota.

Key points

  • Pearson r: linear relationship ka strength, -1 se +1. r = covariance(x, y) / (SD_x * SD_y).
  • Pearson ki limit: outliers se hil jata hai, sirf linear pattern pakadta hai.
  • Spearman: ranks par Pearson. Monotonic relation pakadta hai, outlier-robust.
  • Reading r: 0 = koi linear relation nahi, +-1 = perfect. r squared = variance explained.
  • Spurious correlation: coincidence ya trend ki wajah se correlation (do upward trending series).
  • Confounder: teesri variable jo x aur y dono ko affect kare. Example: tournament size dono, buy-in aur rake ko.
  • Causation kaise: randomized experiment (A/B test). Observational data me sirf association.
  • Reverse causality: shayad y, x ko cause kar raha ho (zyada khelne wale zyada bonus pate hain).

Example

python
from scipy import stats
x = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]; y = [2, 4, 5, 4, 5]
print(stats.pearsonr(x, y)[0])    # 0.7746
print(stats.spearmanr(x, y)[0])   # 0.7379

x2 = [1, 2, 3, 4, 100]; y2 = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
print(stats.pearsonr(x2, y2)[0])  # 0.725
print(stats.spearmanr(x2, y2)[0]) # 1.0

Pehle set me dono strong positive hain. Doosre set me ek outlier (100) Pearson ko 0.725 par le aata hai, par order perfect hai, isliye Spearman 1.0 deta hai.

Common mistakes

  • "Correlated hai to cause hai" bolna.
  • Sirf r number dekhna, scatter plot nahi dekhna (curved relation me r ~ 0 aa sakta hai).
  • Time trend wale series ka correlation nikal kar conclusion banana.
  • Confounder ko control kiye bina feature ko "driver" kehna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Pearson vs Spearman?
    A. Pearson linear, Spearman rank/monotonic aur outlier-robust.
  • Q. Correlation se causation kaise establish karein?
    A. Randomized experiment, ya observational me confounders control karke aur careful causal methods se.
  • Q. Confounder example do.
    A. Gold VIP players zyada bonus bhi lete hain aur zyada khelte bhi hain. VIP level dono ko drive karta hai.

Yaad rakho

Correlation sirf sawal uthata hai, jawab experiment deta hai.

ST-07Probability basicsBasicMust Know

Probability 0 se 1 ke beech ek event ke hone ki chance hai. Conditional probability aur Bayes batate hain naya evidence belief kaise badalta hai.

Simple me samjho

Probability = favourable outcomes / total outcomes (jab sab equally likely hon). Conditional probability matlab "ye pata hai to ab chance kya hai". Bayes isi ko ulta karta hai: effect dekh kar cause ki chance.

Key points

  • Event: outcome ka set. P(A) 0 se 1 ke beech. P(not A) = 1 - P(A).
  • OR rule: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B).
  • Conditional probability: P(A|B) = P(A and B) / P(B).
  • Independence: A aur B independent agar P(A and B) = P(A) * P(B), yani B jaanne se A nahi badalta.
  • Dependent example: deck se bina wapas rakhe 2 cards. P(2 aces) = 4/52 * 3/51 = 1/221, approx 0.45%.
  • Bayes theorem: P(A|B) = P(B|A) * P(A) / P(B).
  • Prior / base rate: P(A), evidence se pehle ki chance. Isko ignore karna sabse badi galti.
  • Total probability: P(B) = P(B|A)*P(A) + P(B|not A)*P(not A).

Example

Fraud detector: 1% accounts fraud hain. Detector 95% fraud pakadta hai (sensitivity). 5% normal accounts ko galti se flag karta hai.

text
P(fraud) = 0.01
P(flag | fraud)     = 0.95  -> 0.01 * 0.95 = 0.0095
P(flag | not fraud) = 0.05  -> 0.99 * 0.05 = 0.0495
P(flag) = 0.0095 + 0.0495 = 0.0590
P(fraud | flag) = 0.0095 / 0.0590 = 0.161  (16.1%)

Flag hone par bhi fraud hone ki chance sirf 16%. Kyunki fraud rare hai, galat flags sahi flags se kaafi zyada hain.

Common mistakes

  • P(A|B) aur P(B|A) ko same samajhna.
  • Base rate ignore karna.
  • Har cheez ko independent maan lena (consecutive hands, same user ke events).
  • P(A and B) ko P(A) * P(B) bina independence check kiye likhna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Independent aur mutually exclusive me fark?
    A. Mutually exclusive: dono saath ho hi nahi sakte. Independent: ek ka hona doosre ki chance nahi badalta. Dono alag concepts hain.
  • Q. Bayes theorem ek line me?
    A. Naya evidence aane par prior belief ko update karke posterior nikalna.
  • Q. 95% accurate test ka positive result 95% sahi kyun nahi?
    A. Base rate low ho to false positives true positives se zyada hote hain.

Yaad rakho

Evidence aane par bhi base rate mat bhoolo.

ST-08Sampling methodsIntermediateMust Know

Poori population nahi ho sakti to sample lete hain. Kaise lete ho wahi decide karta hai ki result bharosemand hai ya biased.

Simple me samjho

Daal ka ek chamach pakane par poori degchi ka swad pata chalta hai, par pehle hilana padta hai. Sample bhi "hilaya hua" (representative) hona chahiye.

Key points

  • Simple random: har unit ko barabar chance. Gold standard, par list (sampling frame) chahiye.
  • Stratified: population ko groups (strata) me baanto, har group se random lo. Chhote important groups (high-value players) ka representation pakka.
  • Cluster: pura group (jaise ek club ya table) randomly chuno aur uske sab members lo. Sasta hai par error zyada.
  • Sampling bias: sample population jaisa nahi (sirf app users se survey, jabki web users bhi hain).
  • Survivorship bias: sirf bache hue ko dekhna (sirf active players ka analysis, churn hue players gayab).
  • Non-response bias: jo jawab dete hain wo alag hote hain.
  • Sample size (proportion): n = z^2 * p(1-p) / e^2. 95% confidence, e = 5%, p = 0.5 par n = 1.96^2 * 0.25 / 0.0025 = 384.16, yani 385.
  • Zyada data != kam bias: bada biased sample bhi galat hai.

Example

10,000 players: 9,000 casual, 1,000 high-value. 500 ka sample chahiye.

text
Simple random: high-value ~ 50 aayenge, par kabhi 30, kabhi 70 (random).
Stratified proportional:
  casual     = 500 * 9000/10000 = 450
  high-value = 500 * 1000/10000 =  50  (guaranteed)

Stratified me har run me high-value ke exactly 50 aate hain, isliye estimate stable hota hai.

python
import numpy as np
n = int(np.ceil(1.96**2 * 0.5 * 0.5 / 0.05**2))   # 385

Common mistakes

  • Convenience sample (jo aasani se mile) ko random sample bolna.
  • Sirf current active users ko dekh kar retention ka conclusion nikalna (survivorship).
  • Strata ke weights lagaye bina results combine karna.
  • Sample size bina margin of error aur confidence decide kiye rakhna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Stratified vs cluster?
    A. Stratified me har group se sample lete hain (precision badhti hai). Cluster me poore groups chunte hain (cost kam hoti hai).
  • Q. Survivorship bias example?
    A. Sirf profitable players ki habits dekh kar "winning strategy" batana, jo haare aur chhod gaye unhe ignore karna.
  • Q. Sample size kis par depend karta hai?
    A. Margin of error, confidence level aur variability (p ya SD).

Yaad rakho

Sample ka size nahi, uska representative hona zyada important hai.

ST-09Central Limit Theorem and LLNIntermediateMust Know

LLN: zyada data to sample average true mean ke paas. CLT: sample means ka distribution normal ban jata hai, chahe data kaisa bhi ho.

Simple me samjho

Ek sikka 10 baar uchhalo to heads 70% aa sakte hain. 10,000 baar uchhalo to 50% ke bahut paas. Ye LLN hai. CLT kehta hai: bahut saare samples ke averages ko plot karo to bell curve banta hai, original data skewed ho tab bhi.

Key points

  • LLN (Law of Large Numbers): n badhne par sample mean true mean ke paas aata hai. Averages stabilise hote hain.
  • CLT: n bada ho to sample mean ka distribution approx normal hota hai, mean = mu aur SD = sigma / sqrt(n).
  • Standard error (SE): SE = sigma / sqrt(n). Sample mean ki uncertainty.
  • Sqrt law: precision double karni ho to n 4 guna chahiye.
  • Thumb rule: n >= 30 aksar kaafi. Bahut skewed data (spend) me zyada n chahiye.
  • Kyun important: isi wajah se t-test, z-test aur confidence intervals non-normal data par bhi (bade n par) chalte hain.
  • CLT individual values ke liye nahi: data khud normal nahi banta, sirf averages ka distribution.
  • Limit: heavy-tail data jaha variance infinite jaisa ho wahan CLT dheere kaam karta hai.
  • LLN vs CLT: LLN batata hai mean kahan jata hai, CLT batata hai uske around kitna noise aur kis shape ka.

Example

Spend ka SD sigma = 100 chips.

text
n = 25   -> SE = 100 / sqrt(25)  = 100 / 5  = 20
n = 400  -> SE = 100 / sqrt(400) = 100 / 20 =  5

n 16 guna hua (25 se 400), SE 4 guna kam hua (20 se 5).

python
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
pop = rng.exponential(scale=100, size=100_000)       # skewed spend
means = [rng.choice(pop, 50).mean() for _ in range(5000)]
print(np.mean(means), np.std(means))   # ~100 and ~14 (=100/sqrt(50))

Population skewed hai par 5000 sample means ka histogram bell-shaped aata hai, mean ~ 100 aur SD ~ sigma/sqrt(50) = 14.1.

Common mistakes

  • CLT ko "data normal ho jata hai" samajhna.
  • Chhote n par heavily skewed data me normal approximation maan lena.
  • SE aur SD ko confuse karna.
  • Kuch hi din ka average dekh kar "trend" bolna (LLN ke bina).

Interview Q&A

  • Q. CLT ek line me?
    A. Independent samples ke mean ka distribution n bada hone par normal hota hai, chahe population ka shape kuch bhi ho.
  • Q. LLN aur CLT ka fark?
    A. LLN: sample mean true mean ki taraf jata hai. CLT: us mean ke aas-paas fluctuation ka shape normal hota hai.
  • Q. SE ko aadha karna ho to?
    A. Sample size 4 guna karo.

Yaad rakho

SE = sigma / sqrt(n): precision ke liye data 4x chahiye.

ST-10Confidence intervalsIntermediateMust Know

CI ek range deta hai jisme true value hone ki umeed hai. Width sample size aur variability se decide hoti hai.

Simple me samjho

"Conversion 20% hai" ek point guess hai. "20% +- 2.5%" zyada honest hai, kyunki sample se sirf andaza milta hai. CI isi andaze ki range batata hai.

Key points

  • Meaning: 95% CI = agar ye experiment baar-baar karein, to aise banaye gaye 95% intervals true value ko pakdenge.
  • Galat interpretation: "true value 95% chance se is range me hai" technically frequentist me galat hai. Interview me "method 95% baar sahi hoti hai" bolo.
  • CI for mean: mean +- t * SE, SE = s / sqrt(n). Bade n par t approx 1.96.
  • CI for proportion: p +- 1.96 * sqrt(p(1-p)/n).
  • Width vs n: width ~ 1/sqrt(n). n 4 guna to width aadhi.
  • Width vs variability: zyada SD to chaudi CI. Confidence 99% karo to bhi chaudi.
  • Do groups compare: agar dono CI overlap na karein to difference clear hai. Overlap ho to bhi difference ho sakta hai, direct difference ka CI nikalo.
  • Zero check: difference ke CI me 0 aaye to difference significant nahi.

Example

1000 players me 200 ne convert kiya.

text
p  = 200/1000 = 0.20
SE = sqrt(0.2 * 0.8 / 1000) = sqrt(0.00016) = 0.01265
CI = 0.20 +- 1.96 * 0.01265 = 0.20 +- 0.0248 = (17.5%, 22.5%)
n = 4000 -> SE = 0.00632, CI = 20% +- 1.24% (width aadhi)

Mean ke liye: mean 50, SD 20, n 100. SE = 2, t(99) = 1.984, CI = 50 +- 3.97 = (46.03, 53.97).

python
from statsmodels.stats.proportion import proportion_confint
from scipy import stats
print(proportion_confint(200, 1000, alpha=0.05, method="normal"))  # (0.1752, 0.2248)
print(stats.t.interval(0.95, 99, loc=50, scale=2))                 # (46.03, 53.97)

Common mistakes

  • 95% CI ko "95% data is range me hai" samajhna. Ye mean ki range hai, individual values ki nahi.
  • Chhote n ya p ke 0/1 ke paas normal-approx CI use karna (Wilson method behtar).
  • Dono CI ke overlap se hi significance decide karna.
  • CI report kiye bina sirf point estimate dena.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. 95% CI ka matlab?
    A. Agar sampling baar-baar karein to 95% intervals true parameter ko cover karenge.
  • Q. CI chhoti kaise karein?
    A. Sample size badhao, variability kam karo, ya confidence level ghatao.
  • Q. Proportion ka CI formula?
    A. p +- z * sqrt(p(1-p)/n).

Yaad rakho

Hamesha estimate ke saath CI do, aur width ~ 1/sqrt(n) yaad rakho.

ST-11Hypothesis testingIntermediateMust Know

Hypothesis test batata hai ki dikhne wala difference sirf random noise ho sakta hai ya nahi. p-value aur errors iske core hain.

Simple me samjho

Adalat ki tarah: pehle maan lo "kuch farak nahi" (null). Phir dekho data itna ajeeb hai ki ye maan-na mushkil ho jaye. Agar bahut ajeeb hai to null reject.

Key points

  • Null (H0): koi effect/difference nahi. Alternative (H1): effect hai (two-sided ya one-sided).
  • p-value: agar H0 sahi ho, to itna ya usse zyada extreme data milne ki probability.
  • p-value kya nahi hai: H0 sahi hone ki probability nahi hai, aur effect ke bade hone ka measure nahi hai.
  • Alpha: pehle se tay threshold (aam 0.05). p < alpha to H0 reject.
  • Type I error: H0 sahi tha par reject kiya (false positive). Probability = alpha.
  • Type II error (beta): asli effect tha par pakad nahi paye (false negative).
  • Power: 1 - beta, asli effect pakadne ki probability. Aam target 80%.
  • Power ko kya badhata hai: bada n, bada effect, kam variability, bada alpha.
  • Rule of thumb: 80% power, alpha 0.05 par n per group approx 16 * p(1-p) / delta^2 (delta = detect karna wala difference).
  • Fail to reject != H0 sahi: sirf itna ki evidence kam hai.

Example

Promo A: 100/1000 conversion. Promo B: 130/1000.

text
H0: pA = pB      H1: pA != pB
pooled p = 230/2000 = 0.115
SE = sqrt(0.115 * 0.885 * (1/1000 + 1/1000)) = 0.014267
z  = (0.13 - 0.10) / 0.014267 = 2.10
p-value (two-sided) = 0.0355

0.0355 < 0.05, to H0 reject. Isse B better dikhta hai. Par agar 10% se 11% (delta 0.01) detect karna ho to n approx 16 * 0.09 / 0.0001 = 14,400 per group chahiye.

python
from statsmodels.stats.proportion import proportions_ztest
print(proportions_ztest([130, 100], [1000, 1000]))  # z ~ 2.10, p ~ 0.035

Common mistakes

  • p = 0.04 ko "96% sure ki effect hai" samajhna.
  • Test ke baad alpha ya hypothesis badalna.
  • "Not significant" ko "no effect" bolna jab power kam thi.
  • Pehle se sample size (power analysis) tay na karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. p-value ko simple me samjhao.
    A. H0 sahi ho to itna extreme result aane ki chance.
  • Q. Type I vs Type II?
    A. Type I false alarm (alpha). Type II missed effect (beta). Power = 1 - beta.
  • Q. Sample size badhane se kya hota hai?
    A. Power badhti hai aur chhote effects bhi detect hote hain. Alpha wahi rehta hai.

Yaad rakho

p-value data ke baare me hai, hypothesis ke baare me nahi.

ST-12t-tests and z-testsIntermediateMust Know

Means (ya proportions) compare karne ke tests. z bade n ya known sigma par, t chhote n par jab sigma unknown ho.

Simple me samjho

Sawal hota hai: "ye mean kisi number se alag hai?" ya "do groups ke mean alag hain?". Difference ko uske noise (SE) se divide karte hain. Ratio bada to difference real lagta hai.

Key points

  • z-test: sigma known ya n bada. Proportions ke test me bhi common.
  • t-test: sigma unknown, sample SD use hota hai. t distribution ki tails moti hoti hain, n badhne par normal ke paas.
  • One-sample t: sample mean vs fixed value. t = (mean - mu0) / (s / sqrt(n)).
  • Two-sample (independent) t: do alag groups. Welch version equal-variance assume nahi karta, aksar default rakho.
  • Paired t: same users ke before/after. Differences par one-sample t lagta hai.
  • Assumptions: independent observations, roughly normal means (bade n par CLT), (Student t me) equal variance.
  • Paired vs independent: paired variability kam karta hai, to power zyada.
  • Non-normal ya chhote n: non-parametric test (Mann-Whitney) dekho.

Example

8 players ka spend, groups A aur B (alag alag players).

python
from scipy import stats
a = [52, 48, 55, 60, 45, 58, 50, 53]   # mean 52.625
b = [58, 54, 61, 66, 52, 59, 57, 60]   # mean 58.375
print(stats.ttest_1samp(a, 50))                 # t=1.48, p=0.18
print(stats.ttest_ind(b, a, equal_var=False))   # Welch: t=2.46, df~13.7, p=0.028
print(stats.ttest_rel(b, a))                    # paired: t=8.21, p~0.0001

Welch: B ka mean 5.75 zyada, p = 0.028 to significant. Agar a aur b same 8 players ke before/after hote to paired test lagta: differences [6,6,6,6,7,1,7,7], mean 5.75, p ~ 0.0001. Paired me player-to-player variation hat jati hai.

Common mistakes

  • Same users ke before/after par independent t-test lagana.
  • Equal variance blindly maan lena (Welch use karo).
  • Ek hi user ki multiple rows ko independent samples maan lena.
  • Multiple groups par bar-bar t-test lagana (ANOVA ya correction chahiye).

Interview Q&A

  • Q. t-test vs z-test?
    A. z me sigma known/bada n, t me sigma unknown aur chhota n. Bade n par dono lagbhag same.
  • Q. Paired test kab?
    A. Jab observations jode hue hon (same user before/after).
  • Q. Welch t-test kyun?
    A. Variances barabar hone ki assumption nahi chahiye, safe default hai.

Yaad rakho

Test ka chunaav data ki structure se: ek group, do group, ya paired.

ST-13Chi-square testsIntermediateGood to Have

Categorical data ke liye test. Independence check karta hai ya observed counts ko expected se compare karta hai.

Simple me samjho

Counts dekhte hain. Agar do cheezein independent hoti to kitni counts aati (expected)? Asli counts usse kitni door hain? Door ho to relation hai.

Key points

  • Statistic: chi2 = sum((Observed - Expected)^2 / Expected).
  • Test of independence: contingency table me do categorical variables ka relation (device vs converted).
  • Expected count: (row total * column total) / grand total.
  • Goodness of fit: ek variable ka observed distribution kisi expected distribution se match karta hai ya nahi (jaise cards/dice fair hain).
  • Degrees of freedom: independence: (rows - 1) * (cols - 1). Fit: categories - 1.
  • Categorical comparisons: conversion rate ko groups me compare karna, 2x2 me ye two-proportion z-test ke equal hai.
  • Assumptions: independent observations, raw counts (percent nahi), expected count >= 5 har cell me. Chhote counts me Fisher exact.
  • Sirf "kuch farak hai" batata hai, kaunsa group alag hai wo residuals se dekho.

Example

Android: 50 converted, 150 not. iOS: 80 converted, 120 not.

text
Total converted = 130, not = 270, n = 400. Expected (har group 200 users):
Android converted = 200*130/400 = 65, not = 135   (iOS same)
chi2 = (50-65)^2/65 + (150-135)^2/135 + (80-65)^2/65 + (120-135)^2/135
     = 3.46 + 1.67 + 3.46 + 1.67 = 10.26,  df = 1,  p = 0.0014

Device aur conversion independent nahi hain (p < 0.05).

python
from scipy import stats
obs = [[50, 150], [80, 120]]
chi2, p, df, exp = stats.chi2_contingency(obs, correction=False)  # 10.26, 0.0014, 1
print(stats.chisquare([18, 22, 20, 40], [25]*4))  # fit: chi2=12.32, p=0.0064

Fit example: 100 hands ke 4 suits observed [18,22,20,40] vs expected 25 each, chi2 = 12.32, df 3, p = 0.006, to suits uniform nahi.

Common mistakes

  • Percentages par chi-square lagana (raw counts chahiye).
  • Expected < 5 wale cells ignore karna.
  • Same users ko multiple rows me count karke independence tod dena.
  • Chi-square ke significance ko effect size samajhna (bade n par chhota farak bhi significant).

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Chi-square independence test kab?
    A. Do categorical variables ke beech relation dekhna ho (device vs conversion).
  • Q. Goodness of fit kya?
    A. Observed counts kisi expected distribution se match karte hain ya nahi.
  • Q. Degrees of freedom?
    A. Independence me (r-1)(c-1), fit me k-1.

Yaad rakho

Chi-square = (Observed - Expected)^2 / Expected ka sum, sirf counts par.

ST-14ANOVAAdvancedGood to Have

3 ya zyada groups ke means ek saath compare karne ka test. Significant aaye to post-hoc se pata karte hain kaun alag hai.

Simple me samjho

Teen tables ka average pot size compare karna hai. Har pair par t-test lagayenge to false positives badhenge. ANOVA ek hi test me puchta hai: "kya koi bhi group alag hai?"

Key points

  • Idea: group ke beech ka variance vs group ke andar ka variance. F = MS_between / MS_within.
  • H0: sab group means barabar. H1: kam se kam ek alag.
  • F bada to groups ke beech ka farak noise se zyada hai.
  • Kyun not multiple t-tests: 3 groups me 3 pairs, 10 groups me 45 pairs. Type I error inflate hota hai.
  • Assumptions: independent observations, residuals roughly normal, groups me similar variance.
  • ANOVA sirf "kuch alag hai" batata hai, kaunsa alag hai nahi.
  • Post-hoc tests: Tukey HSD (sab pairs, error control ke saath), Bonferroni-corrected t-tests.
  • Violation: normality na ho to Kruskal-Wallis (non-parametric). Variance alag ho to Welch ANOVA.

Example

Teen tables ke pot sizes (5-5 observations): means 12, 15, 21.

text
Grand mean = 16
SS_between = 5 * ((12-16)^2 + (15-16)^2 + (21-16)^2) = 5 * 42 = 210, df = 2 -> MS = 105
SS_within  = 10 + 10 + 10 = 30, df = 12 -> MS = 2.5
F = 105 / 2.5 = 42,  p ~ 0.000004

Bahut chhota p, to kam se kam ek table alag hai.

python
from scipy import stats
g1 = [10,12,11,13,14]; g2 = [14,15,16,13,17]; g3 = [20,22,19,21,23]
print(stats.f_oneway(g1, g2, g3))      # F=42.0, p=3.8e-06
print(stats.tukey_hsd(g1, g2, g3))     # 1 vs 2: p=0.028, 3rd vs others: p<0.001

Tukey batata hai ki teeno pairs alag hain (g1 vs g2 ka p = 0.028, baaki bahut chhote).

Common mistakes

  • ANOVA ke baad seedha conclusion "A best hai" bolna bina post-hoc ke.
  • Post-hoc me correction na lagana.
  • Unequal variance/sample size ko ignore karna.
  • Same users ko multiple groups me repeat karna (repeated-measures ANOVA chahiye).

Interview Q&A

  • Q. ANOVA kyun, multiple t-tests kyun nahi?
    A. Multiple t-tests overall false positive rate badha dete hain. ANOVA ek hi test me control karta hai.
  • Q. F-statistic kya hai?
    A. Between-group variance / within-group variance.
  • Q. Significant ANOVA ke baad kya karein?
    A. Tukey HSD jaisa post-hoc test.

Yaad rakho

ANOVA batata hai "farak hai", post-hoc batata hai "kahan".

ST-15Non-parametric testsAdvancedGood to Have

Jab data normal na ho, chhota ho ya ordinal ho, tab distribution ki assumption ke bina chalne wale tests.

Simple me samjho

Parametric tests mean aur normal shape par tike hain. Non-parametric tests values ki jagah unke ranks dekhte hain. Isliye outliers aur skew se kam hilte hain.

Key points

  • Mann-Whitney U: do independent groups (t-test ka non-parametric option). Kaun sa group stochastically bada hai.
  • Wilcoxon signed-rank: paired data (paired t-test ka option). Differences ke ranks par.
  • Kruskal-Wallis: 3+ groups (ANOVA ka option).
  • KS test: do samples ya sample vs theoretical distribution ka shape compare karta hai (ks_2samp, kstest).
  • Kab use karein: data skewed (spend, latency), n chhota, ordinal data, outliers heavy.
  • Trade-off: normal data par thoda kam power. Normal na ho to aksar zyada power.
  • Kya test hota hai: mean ka farak nahi, ranks ya poore distribution ka farak.
  • Ties aur n bada hone par software approximate p-value deta hai.

Example

Do tables ka session length (minutes), 6-6 observations.

python
from scipy import stats
x = [12, 15, 14, 10, 18, 25]
y = [20, 22, 19, 30, 28, 35]
print(stats.mannwhitneyu(x, y, alternative="two-sided"))  # U=3.0, p=0.0152
print(stats.ttest_ind(x, y))                              # t=-2.96, p=0.0143

# paired: before vs after
# stats.wilcoxon(before, after)
# distribution shape: stats.ks_2samp(x, y)

U = 3 ka matlab x ki sirf 3 pairs hi y se bade nikle (25 ne 20, 22, 19 ko beat kiya) out of 36. p = 0.015 to y ke session lambe hain. Yahan dono tests agree karte hain.

Common mistakes

  • Mann-Whitney ko "medians ka test" bol dena (sirf same shape ke case me).
  • Chhote n par normality check kiye bina t-test chalana.
  • KS test ko normality ka perfect test maan lena (bade n par chhote farak bhi reject).
  • Paired data par Mann-Whitney lagana (Wilcoxon chahiye).

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Non-parametric test kab?
    A. Data normal na ho, n chhota ho, ordinal ho ya outliers heavy hon.
  • Q. Mann-Whitney vs t-test?
    A. t-test means compare karta hai (normality chahiye), Mann-Whitney ranks compare karta hai.
  • Q. KS test kya karta hai?
    A. Do distributions ke CDF ka maximum gap napta hai.

Yaad rakho

Skewed ya chhota data: ranks wale tests.

ST-16Multiple testing and peekingAdvancedGood to Have

Jitne zyada tests ya jitni baar results dekhoge, utne zyada false positives milenge. Correction lagana zaroori hai.

Simple me samjho

20 baar dice phenko to ek baar 6 aana normal hai. 20 metrics test karoge to ek "significant" milna bhi normal hai, chahe koi effect na ho. Roz result jhaankna bhi ek tarah ka multiple test hai.

Key points

  • Problem: m independent tests par kam se kam ek false positive ki chance = 1 - (1 - alpha)^m. m = 20 par 64%.
  • Bonferroni: alpha / m par test karo. Simple par conservative (power kam).
  • FDR (Benjamini-Hochberg): false discoveries ka expected share control karta hai. Bahut tests ho to behtar.
  • BH steps: p-values sort karo, p(i) <= (i/m) * alpha wala sabse bada i dhundo, wahan tak sab reject.
  • Bonferroni vs FDR: Bonferroni = FWER (ek bhi galat nahi), FDR = galat discoveries ka fraction. FDR zyada power deta hai.
  • Peeking: A/B test me roz p-value check karke jaise hi < 0.05 ho jaye, rok dena. Isse false positive rate bahut badhta hai.
  • Peeking ka asar: 5 baar dekhne par ~14%, 10 baar par ~19% (nominal 5% ki jagah, simulation).
  • Fixes: pehle se sample size tay karo, fixed horizon par hi decide karo, ya sequential testing / alpha spending use karo.
  • Pehle se metrics tay karo: ek primary metric, baaki secondary.

Example

10 metrics ke p-values (sorted): 0.001, 0.008, 0.039, 0.041, 0.042, 0.06, 0.074, 0.205, 0.212, 0.216.

text
Bonferroni: 0.05/10 = 0.005 -> sirf 0.001 reject (1 discovery)
BH: i=1 threshold 0.005 -> 0.001 ok; i=2 threshold 0.010 -> 0.008 ok
    i=3 threshold 0.015 -> 0.039 fail; baaki bhi fail -> 2 discoveries
Bina correction (alpha 0.05): 5 metrics "significant" dikhte, jinme se kai sirf noise ho sakte hain.
python
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests
p = [0.001,0.008,0.039,0.041,0.042,0.06,0.074,0.205,0.212,0.216]
print(multipletests(p, alpha=0.05, method="bonferroni")[0])  # sirf pehla True
print(multipletests(p, alpha=0.05, method="fdr_bh")[0])      # pehle do True

Common mistakes

  • 20 segments cut karke jo significant mila use report karna (p-hacking).
  • A/B test ko roz check karke pehli baar significant par rok dena.
  • Correction lagana par family of tests galat define karna.
  • Bonferroni ko hamesha best maan lena (bahut metrics par power gir jati hai).

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Peeking problem kya hai?
    A. Baar-baar results dekh kar rokne se Type I error alpha se kaafi upar chala jata hai.
  • Q. Bonferroni vs FDR?
    A. Bonferroni ek bhi false positive se bachata hai (strict). FDR false discoveries ka ratio control karta hai (zyada power).
  • Q. 20 tests par alpha 0.05 ho to chance?
    A. 1 - 0.95^20 = 64% ki kam se kam ek false positive.

Yaad rakho

Zyada tests ya zyada peeks = zyada false positives. Plan pehle, correction baad me.

ST-17Effect size and practical significanceIntermediateMust Know

Statistically significant ka matlab business ke liye important nahi. Effect ka size aur lift dekhna zaroori hai.

Simple me samjho

Bahut bade sample me 0.1 chip ka farak bhi "significant" aa jata hai. Par kya wo paisa ya mehnat ke laayak hai? p-value batata hai "farak real hai ya nahi", effect size batata hai "kitna bada hai".

Key points

  • Statistical significance: p < alpha. Sample size par bahut depend karta hai.
  • Practical significance: effect itna bada hai ki business decision badle (cost, revenue ke hisab se).
  • Absolute lift: B - A (percentage points). Conversion 10% se 11.5% = +1.5 pp.
  • Relative lift: (B - A) / A. 10% se 11.5% = +15%.
  • Cohen's d: (mean1 - mean2) / pooled SD. Mean difference ko SD ki unit me napta hai.
  • Cohen's d ke rough labels: 0.2 small, 0.5 medium, 0.8 large (sirf thumb rule).
  • Pooled SD: sqrt((s1^2 + s2^2) / 2) barabar n ke liye.
  • CI ke saath report: effect aur uski CI dikhao, sirf p-value nahi.
  • MDE (minimum detectable effect): experiment se pehle tay karo ki kitna lift worth hai.
  • Decision: significant + practical = ship. Significant + tiny = shayad nahi. Not significant + CI wide = aur data chahiye.

Example

Average spend: A = 50, B = 51, SD = 20, n = 1,000,000 per group.

text
Cohen's d = (51 - 50) / 20 = 0.05  (bahut chhota)
SE of difference = 20 * sqrt(2 / 1,000,000) = 0.0283
z = 1 / 0.0283 = 35.4  -> p lagbhag 0

Bahut significant, par effect sirf 1 chip (2% relative). Agar ek feature build karne ki cost zyada hai to ship karna worth nahi.

python
import numpy as np
def cohens_d(a, b):
    na, nb = len(a), len(b)
    sp = np.sqrt(((na-1)*np.var(a, ddof=1) + (nb-1)*np.var(b, ddof=1)) / (na+nb-2))
    return (np.mean(b) - np.mean(a)) / sp

Pichle t-test wale 8-8 data par ye d ~ 1.23 deta hai, yani bada effect.

Common mistakes

  • "p < 0.05, to jeet gaye" bolna bina lift dekhe.
  • Relative lift batana aur base rate chhupana (1% se 2% = +100% par sirf +1 pp).
  • Cohen's d ke labels ko business rule maan lena.
  • Bade n par har chhoti cheez ko important bolna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Significant par useless result kaise ho sakta hai?
    A. Bahut bade n par chhota sa farak bhi p < 0.05 deta hai, par effect business ke liye negligible hota hai.
  • Q. Cohen's d kya hai?
    A. Do means ke farak ko pooled SD se divide karna, SD-units me effect.
  • Q. Absolute vs relative lift?
    A. Absolute = pp me farak, relative = base ke percent me. Dono batao.

Yaad rakho

p-value ke saath hamesha effect size aur CI dikhao.

ST-18Linear regressionIntermediateMust Know

Ek outcome ko ek ya zyada features se seedhi line se explain karna. Coefficients batate hain feature badhne par outcome kitna badalta hai.

Simple me samjho

Aisi line dhundo jo points ke sabse paas ho. Slope batata hai x ek unit badhne par y kitna badhta hai. Residual wo doori hai jo line se bacha hua error hai.

Key points

  • Model: y = b0 + b1*x1 + ... + error. OLS (least squares) squared residuals ka sum minimum karta hai.
  • Simple regression: slope b1 = Sxy / Sxx, intercept b0 = mean(y) - b1 * mean(x).
  • Coefficient interpretation: baaki features fixed rakh kar x ek unit badhe to y average b1 badhta hai. Ye association hai, causation nahi.
  • Intercept: x = 0 par predicted y (aksar meaningful nahi).
  • R squared: 1 - SSE/SST. Model variance ka kitna fraction explain karta hai.
  • Adjusted R squared: features badhane ki penalty ke saath.
  • Residual: actual - predicted. Sum ~ 0.
  • Assumptions (LINE): Linearity, Independence of errors, Normality of residuals, Equal variance (homoscedasticity).
  • Residual plots: patterns (curve, funnel shape) assumption tootna batate hain.
  • p-value of coefficient: kya true slope 0 hai? Effect size aur CI bhi dekho.

Example

x = hands played (hundreds): [1,2,3,4,5]. y = revenue: [2,4,5,4,5].

text
mean x = 3, mean y = 4
Sxy = 6, Sxx = 10  -> slope = 0.6, intercept = 4 - 0.6*3 = 2.2
Predicted: 2.8, 3.4, 4.0, 4.6, 5.2
Residuals: -0.8, 0.6, 1.0, -0.6, -0.2  (sum = 0)
SSE = 2.4, SST = 6  -> R2 = 1 - 2.4/6 = 0.6

Matlab 100 extra hands par revenue average 0.6 unit badhta hai. Model 60% variation explain karta hai.

python
import statsmodels.api as sm
X = sm.add_constant([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
res = sm.OLS([2, 4, 5, 4, 5], X).fit()
print(res.params, res.rsquared)   # [2.2 0.6] 0.6

Common mistakes

  • Residual plot dekhe bina model maan lena.
  • Extrapolate karna (data range ke bahar predict).
  • Zyada R squared ko "accha model" samajhna (overfit ho sakta hai).
  • Coefficient ko causal bolna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. R squared 0.6 ka matlab?
    A. Outcome ke variance ka 60% model explain karta hai.
  • Q. Linear regression ki assumptions?
    A. Linearity, independence, normal residuals, constant variance (aur multiple regression me no multicollinearity).
  • Q. Coefficient ka interpretation?
    A. Baaki variables constant, x ek unit badhne par y me average change.

Yaad rakho

Fit ke baad residuals dekho, R squared akela kaafi nahi.

ST-19Logistic regressionIntermediateGood to Have

Yes/no outcome (churn, convert) ki probability predict karne ka model. Coefficient log-odds me hota hai.

Simple me samjho

Linear regression 0-1 se bahar probability de sakta hai. Logistic regression line ko S-shaped curve me mod deta hai, jisse output hamesha 0 se 1 ke beech rehta hai.

Key points

  • Probability p 0 se 1. Odds = p / (1 - p). p = 0.2 to odds = 0.25 (1 ke against 4).
  • Log-odds (logit) = ln(p / (1 - p)). Model me linear hota hai: logit = b0 + b1*x1 + ...
  • Probability wapas: p = 1 / (1 + e^-logit).
  • Coefficient: x ek unit badhe to log-odds b1 badhte hain.
  • Odds ratio: e^b1. e^0.7 = 2.01, yani odds lagbhag double.
  • Probability change constant nahi hota: odds ratio constant hai, p ka change x ke level par depend karta hai.
  • Classification threshold: p >= 0.5 par class 1, par threshold business se tay karo (fraud me kam rakho, to recall badhta hai).
  • Threshold trade-off: kam threshold = zyada recall, kam precision.
  • Fitting: maximum likelihood se, OLS se nahi.
  • Evaluation: accuracy imbalanced data me dhokha deti hai; precision, recall, AUC dekho.

Example

Churn model: logit = -2 + 0.7 * days_inactive_weeks.

text
x = 3 weeks inactive:
logit = -2 + 0.7*3 = 0.1
odds  = e^0.1 = 1.105
p     = 1 / (1 + e^-0.1) = 0.525  (52.5% churn chance)
Odds ratio per extra week = e^0.7 = 2.01
python
import statsmodels.api as sm
# y: 0/1 churn, X: features
model = sm.Logit(y, sm.add_constant(X)).fit()
print(model.params)                 # log-odds
print(np.exp(model.params))         # odds ratios
pred = (model.predict(sm.add_constant(X)) >= 0.5).astype(int)

Har extra inactive week par churn ke odds lagbhag 2 guna (probability nahi).

Common mistakes

  • Coefficient ko seedhe probability change samajhna.
  • Odds ratio ko "2 guna probability" bolna.
  • Imbalanced data par accuracy se evaluate karna aur threshold 0.5 hi rakhna.
  • Perfect separation / bahut kam events par model fit karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Odds aur probability me fark?
    A. Probability = p, odds = p/(1-p). p = 0.5 par odds = 1.
  • Q. Coefficient 0.7 ka matlab?
    A. x ek unit badhe to log-odds 0.7 badhte hain, odds e^0.7 = 2.01 guna.
  • Q. Threshold kaise chunte hain?
    A. Cost of false positive vs false negative aur precision-recall curve dekh kar.

Yaad rakho

Logit linear hai, probability nahi. Odds ratio = e^coefficient.

ST-20Multicollinearity and interactionsAdvancedGood to Have

Jab features aapas me bahut correlated hon, coefficients unstable ho jate hain. Interaction batata hai ek feature ka asar doosre par depend karta hai.

Simple me samjho

Do features lagbhag ek hi cheez napte hon (hands_played aur sessions) to model nahi jaan pata credit kise de. Coefficient idhar-udhar hilte hain. Interaction: promo ka asar VIP aur non-VIP par alag ho sakta hai.

Key points

  • Multicollinearity: ek feature ko baaki features se predict kiya ja sake.
  • Symptoms: coefficient ke sign ulte, bade SE, features individually insignificant par model ka R squared high.
  • VIF: VIF = 1 / (1 - R2_j), jahan R2_j feature j ko baaki features se predict karne ka R squared hai.
  • VIF reading: 1 = koi issue nahi, > 5 dhyan do, > 10 serious (thumb rule).
  • Fix: correlated feature drop karo, combine karo (ratio ya average), PCA, ya ridge regularization.
  • Prediction vs interpretation: sirf prediction chahiye to multicollinearity itni badi problem nahi. Interpretation me problem hai.
  • Correlated features dekhna: correlation matrix aur VIF dono.
  • Interaction term: x1 * x2 ko model me add karna: y = b0 + b1*x1 + b2*x2 + b3*(x1*x2).
  • Interaction ka matlab: x1 ka effect x2 ke level par depend karta hai. b3 wahi change batata hai.
  • Interaction ke saath main effects bhi rakho.

Example

VIF: agar hands_played ko baaki features se predict karne par R2 = 0.9, VIF = 1/(1-0.9) = 10. R2 = 0.8 par VIF = 5.

Interaction: spend ~ promo + is_vip + promo*is_vip, maan lo coefficients promo = 5, promo*is_vip = 15.

text
Non-VIP par promo ka asar = 5
VIP par promo ka asar    = 5 + 15 = 20
python
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from statsmodels.stats.outliers_influence import variance_inflation_factor
import statsmodels.api as sm

m = smf.ols("spend ~ promo * is_vip", data=df).fit()   # promo + is_vip + promo:is_vip
X = sm.add_constant(df[["hands", "sessions", "tenure"]])
vif = [variance_inflation_factor(X.values, i) for i in range(1, X.shape[1])]

Common mistakes

  • Dummy variable trap (saari dummy columns + intercept) ko multicollinearity ka source na samajhna.
  • High correlation wale feature ke coefficient ko alag alag interpret karna.
  • Interaction add karke main effects hata dena.
  • VIF me constant column ko include kar lena aur galat reading lena.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. VIF kya batata hai?
    A. Ek feature kitna baaki features se explain ho jata hai. VIF > 10 serious multicollinearity.
  • Q. Multicollinearity se kya bigadta hai?
    A. Coefficients ka estimate unstable aur interpretation mushkil, prediction aksar theek.
  • Q. Interaction term kab?
    A. Jab ek variable ka effect doosre ke level par depend kare (promo ka asar VIP par alag).

Yaad rakho

Correlated features ke coefficients par bharosa mat karo; VIF dekho.

ST-21Time series basicsIntermediateMust Know

Time series me data time order me hota hai, isliye trend, seasonality aur stationarity samajhna zaroori hai.

Simple me samjho

Daily active players ka graph dekho: lambi avadhi me upar ja raha hai (trend), har weekend spike aata hai (seasonality), baaki random noise. Time series me aaj ka value kal se jura hota hai, isliye normal independent assumptions nahi lagte.

Key points

  • Trend: lambi avadhi ki upar ya neeche ki direction.
  • Seasonality: fixed period par repeat hone wala pattern (weekly, monthly, tournament calendar).
  • Noise (residual): jo trend aur seasonality ke baad bacha.
  • Stationarity: mean, variance aur autocorrelation time ke saath na badle. Kai models (ARIMA) iski maang karte hain.
  • Stationary banana: differencing (y_t - y_(t-1)), log transform.
  • ADF test: H0 = non-stationary. p < 0.05 to stationary.
  • Moving average: pichle k points ka average. Noise smooth karta hai, trend dikhata hai.
  • Decomposition: series = trend + seasonality + residual (additive) ya multiply (multiplicative). Seasonality amplitude level ke saath badhe to multiplicative.
  • Autocorrelation: series ka khud se lag par correlation.
  • Random shuffle mat karo: train/test split time ke hisaab se karo.

Example

Daily logins (thousands): [100, 120, 90, 110, 130, 95, 115]. 3-day moving average:

text
(100+120+90)/3  = 103.33
(120+90+110)/3  = 106.67
(90+110+130)/3  = 110.00
(110+130+95)/3  = 111.67
(130+95+115)/3  = 113.33

Daily values 90 se 130 ke beech jhoomti hain par MA 103 se 113 tak smoothly upar ja raha hai, yani halka uptrend.

python
from statsmodels.tsa.seasonal import seasonal_decompose
from statsmodels.tsa.stattools import adfuller
res = seasonal_decompose(series, model="additive", period=7)
print(res.trend.head(), res.seasonal.head())
print(adfuller(series)[1])      # p-value; < 0.05 -> stationary

Common mistakes

  • Time series ko random shuffle karke train/test split karna.
  • Trend wale series par seedha correlation ya regression lagana (spurious).
  • Seasonality period galat dena (daily data me weekly = 7).
  • Moving average ka window itna bada rakhna ki asli changes chhup jayein.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Stationary series kya hoti hai?
    A. Jisme mean, variance aur autocorrelation time ke saath constant ho.
  • Q. Trend aur seasonality me fark?
    A. Trend lambi directional movement hai, seasonality fixed period par repeat hone wala pattern hai.
  • Q. Non-stationary ko stationary kaise banate hain?
    A. Differencing ya log transform, phir ADF se check.

Yaad rakho

Pehle decompose karo: trend + seasonality + noise.

ST-22Forecasting methodsAdvancedGood to Have

Future values predict karne ke tareeke, simple baseline se ARIMA/Prophet tak, aur error MAPE/RMSE se napna.

Simple me samjho

Pehle sabse simple tareeka try karo (kal jitna hi hoga). Naya complex model tabhi worth hai jab wo is baseline ko beat kare.

Key points

  • Naive: agla value = last value. Seasonal naive: pichle hafte ka same din. Hamesha baseline rakho.
  • Moving average forecast: pichle k values ka average.
  • Exponential smoothing: recent values ko zyada weight. SES: level_t = alpha * y_t + (1 - alpha) * level_(t-1). Holt-Winters trend aur seasonality jodta hai.
  • ARIMA(p, d, q): p = autoregressive lags, d = differencing, q = moving average lags. Stationary data par.
  • Prophet: trend + seasonality + holidays ka additive model, ds aur y columns chahiye. Missing data aur holidays me aasan.
  • MAPE: mean(|actual - forecast| / |actual|) * 100. Percent me, par actual 0 ke paas phat jata hai.
  • RMSE: sqrt(mean(error^2)). Bade errors ko zyada punish karta hai.
  • MAE: mean(|error|). Same unit, outlier se kam sensitive.
  • Validation: time order me (rolling / walk-forward), random split nahi.
  • Method chunav: data kam aur simple pattern = naive/ETS. Holidays aur multiple seasonality = Prophet.

Example

Actual [100, 120, 80, 110], forecast [90, 130, 85, 100].

text
Errors (actual - forecast): 10, -10, -5, 10
APE: 10%, 8.33%, 6.25%, 9.09%  -> MAPE = 8.42%
RMSE = sqrt((100 + 100 + 25 + 100) / 4) = sqrt(81.25) = 9.01

SES alpha = 0.5 on [100, 120, 80, 110]: levels = 100, 110, 95, 102.5. Agla forecast = 102.5.

python
from statsmodels.tsa.arima.model import ARIMA
from prophet import Prophet
fc = ARIMA(y, order=(1, 1, 1)).fit().forecast(7)

m = Prophet()
m.fit(df)                                        # df columns: ds, y
future = m.make_future_dataframe(periods=30)
pred = m.predict(future)[["ds", "yhat"]]

Common mistakes

  • Naive baseline se compare kiye bina complex model deploy karna.
  • MAPE ko zero ya bahut chhote actuals par use karna.
  • Random split se model validate karna.
  • Sirf point forecast dena, uncertainty interval nahi.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. MAPE vs RMSE?
    A. MAPE percent error deta hai (scale-free), RMSE bade errors ko zyada penalty deta hai aur same unit me hota hai.
  • Q. ARIMA ke p, d, q?
    A. p = AR lags, d = differencing order, q = MA lags.
  • Q. Prophet kab?
    A. Strong seasonality, holidays aur missing data ho, aur quick reliable baseline chahiye.

Yaad rakho

Naive baseline se shuru karo, time-ordered validation se judge karo.

ST-23Simpson's paradox and fallaciesIntermediateMust Know

Groups me trend ek taraf, combine karne par ulta. Saath me base-rate fallacy aur selection bias jaise common dimaagi jaal.

Simple me samjho

Ek promo har segment me jeet raha hai, par overall number me haar raha hai. Wajah: segments ke size alag hain. Isliye aggregate number par seedha bharosa mat karo, segments me todke dekho.

Key points

  • Simpson's paradox: har sub-group me trend ek direction me, aggregate me ulta. Wajah: groups ka size/mix alag aur ek confounder.
  • Kaise pakdein: segment (device, VIP level, country, new vs old) ke hisaab se break-down karo.
  • Kaun sa sahi: depends. Agar confounder (case ki mushkil) real hai to segment-level result zyada sahi.
  • Base-rate fallacy: rare event ke prior ko ignore karna (ST-07 wala fraud 16% example).
  • Selection bias: jo log sample me aate hain wo random nahi (opt-in survey, sirf active players).
  • Survivorship bias: selection bias ka ek roop, sirf bache hue dikhte hain.
  • Ecological fallacy: group level ke pattern ko individual par laagu karna.
  • Rule: aggregation se pehle mix check karo (kisko kitna traffic mila).

Example

Do promos A aur B, player segments casual aur high-roller ke hisaab se conversions.

text
              Promo A            Promo B
Casual        81/87   = 93%      234/270 = 87%
High-roller   192/263 = 73%      55/80   = 69%
Overall       273/350 = 78%      289/350 = 82.6%

Har segment me A jeet raha hai (93 vs 87, 73 vs 69), par overall B jeet raha hai (82.6 vs 78). Wajah: A ko zyada high-roller (263) mile jo convert kam hote hain, B ko zyada casual (270) mile.

python
import pandas as pd
print(df.groupby("promo")["converted"].mean())                  # aggregate
print(df.groupby(["segment", "promo"])["converted"].mean())     # segment-wise

Common mistakes

  • Sirf overall conversion dekh kar decision lena.
  • Segment mix ko control kiye bina A/B groups compare karna (randomization toot gaya ho to).
  • Opt-in ya sirf-active users ko poori population maan lena.
  • Paradox dekh kar hamesha segment wala sahi maan lena bina causal soch ke.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Simpson's paradox kya hai?
    A. Sub-groups me ek trend, combine karne par ulta, groups ke unequal size/mix ki wajah se.
  • Q. Kaise bachein?
    A. Segments ke hisaab se break-down karo, confounder pehchano, randomization check karo.
  • Q. Base rate fallacy ka example?
    A. 95% accurate fraud flag ko 95% sahi maanna jabki fraud sirf 1% hai (asli precision ~16%).

Yaad rakho

Aggregate ke saath segment cut dekhna mat bhoolo.

ST-24Bayesian thinkingAdvancedBonus

Pehle ki belief (prior) + naya data = updated belief (posterior). A/B test me seedha "B ke better hone ki probability" milti hai.

Simple me samjho

Aap pehle se kuch maante ho (prior). Data aata hai, belief update hota hai (posterior). Jitna zyada data, utna prior ka asar kam. Frequentist me p-value, Bayesian me seedha probability statement.

Key points

  • Prior: data se pehle ki belief ya distribution (ek parameter ke liye).
  • Likelihood: data parameter ke is value par kitna likely hai.
  • Posterior: prior * likelihood ka normalized result. Final updated belief.
  • Bayes rule: posterior proportional to likelihood * prior.
  • Beta-Binomial: conversion rate ke liye prior Beta(a, b). Data me s successes aur f failures par posterior Beta(a + s, b + f).
  • Weak/uniform prior: Beta(1, 1) lagbhag "kuch pata nahi". Strong prior me purana data ya domain knowledge lagta hai.
  • Bayesian A/B: P(B > A), expected loss, credible interval nikalte hain.
  • Credible interval: "parameter 95% probability se is range me hai", seedha interpretation (CI se alag).
  • Fayde: chhote data par stable, business ke liye interpretable, prior information use.
  • Dhyan: prior ka chunav subjective hai, sensitivity check karo. Peeking ka asar kam par bilkul khatam nahi.

Example

Coin: prior Beta(2, 2), 10 flips me 7 heads, 3 tails.

text
Posterior = Beta(2 + 7, 2 + 3) = Beta(9, 5)
Posterior mean = 9 / 14 = 0.643

A/B: prior Beta(1, 1). A = 100/1000, B = 130/1000.

text
A posterior = Beta(101, 901)  mean = 101/1002 = 0.1008
B posterior = Beta(131, 871)  mean = 131/1002 = 0.1307
python
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
A = rng.beta(101, 901, 1_000_000)
B = rng.beta(131, 871, 1_000_000)
print((B > A).mean())                          # ~0.98
print(np.percentile(B - A, [2.5, 97.5]))       # ~[0.002, 0.058]

Simulation se B ke A se better hone ki probability ~98% aur lift ka 95% credible interval lagbhag 0.2 pp se 5.8 pp.

Common mistakes

  • Credible interval ko confidence interval ki tarah interpret karna ya ulta.
  • Prior bahut strong chun lena aur data ke asar ko dab dena.
  • "P(B > A) = 98%" ko "B 98% better hai" samajhna.
  • Prior ka kaaran na batana, sensitivity check na karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Frequentist vs Bayesian?
    A. Frequentist parameter ko fixed maan kar data ki variability dekhta hai (p-value, CI). Bayesian parameter par probability distribution banata hai (posterior).
  • Q. Bayesian A/B ka fayda?
    A. Seedha "B ke better hone ki probability" aur expected loss, jo business ko samajhna aasan hai.
  • Q. Prior kaise chunte hain?
    A. Purana data ya domain knowledge se, ya weak prior (Beta(1,1)) aur sensitivity check.

Yaad rakho

Posterior = prior + data. Jitna zyada data, utna prior ka asar kam.

Data Cleaning & EDA 16 topics

EDA-01Understanding source and grainBasicMust Know

Data use karne se pehle samjho: ek row kya represent karti hai, key kya hai, time range aur owner kaun hai.

Simple me samjho

Grain matlab "ek row = kya?". Jaise bill book me ek page = ek bill. Agar grain galat samjha, to har number galat aayega. Pehle table ko jaano, phir query likho.

Key points

  • Grain: ek row kis cheez ki hai. Example: ek hand, ek player-hand, ek transaction, ya ek user-day.
  • Primary key: wo column(s) jo row ko unique banate hain. Verify karo, assume mat karo.
  • Granularity: level of detail. Hand-level data ko daily level me aggregate kar sakte ho, reverse nahi.
  • Time range: data kab se kab tak hai. Missing months ya late start date check karo.
  • Refresh frequency: real-time, hourly ya daily batch. Dashboard "today" ka number kab stale hota hai, ye isse pata chalta hai.
  • Owner: table kaun maintain karta hai (team/person). Doubt hone par unse poocho.
  • Time zone: timestamp UTC hai ya IST, ye bhi source ka part hai.
  • Fan-out risk: grain alag wale tables join karoge to rows multiply ho jaati hain.
  • Source of record: transaction DB, event stream ya warehouse copy. Kaun sa original hai, note karo.

Example

sql
-- Kya (user_id, game_date) unique hai?
SELECT user_id, game_date, COUNT(*) AS c
FROM player_daily
GROUP BY user_id, game_date
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

SELECT MIN(game_date), MAX(game_date), COUNT(*) FROM player_daily;
python
df.duplicated(["user_id", "game_date"]).sum()   # 0 hona chahiye
df["game_date"].agg(["min", "max"])

Agar HAVING ki query rows deti hai, to grain "ek user-day" nahi hai. Pehle isse solve karo.

Common mistakes

  • Column name se grain guess karna (amount per hand hai ya per session?).
  • Hand-level aur user-level table join karke SUM karna, jisse double counting hoti hai.
  • Time range check na karna aur partial month ko full month samajhna.
  • Owner ko na poochna aur galat interpretation pe report bhej dena.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Naye table pe sabse pehle kya check karte ho?
    A. Grain, primary key uniqueness, time range, refresh schedule aur owner. Phir row count aur nulls.
  • Q. Grain mismatch se kya problem hoti hai?
    A. Join pe fan-out hota hai, to SUM/COUNT inflate ho jaate hain. Pehle same grain pe aggregate karo, phir join.

Yaad rakho

Query likhne se pehle bolo: "ek row = ?" aur key ko verify karo.

EDA-02Data profilingBasicMust Know

Data ka quick health check: row counts, distinct values, null %, min/max aur value frequencies.

Simple me samjho

Doctor jaise pehle BP, pulse check karta hai, waise hi analysis se pehle data ka profile dekhte hain. Isse 80% surprises pehle hi pakad me aa jaate hain.

Key points

  • Row counts: total rows aur expected se compare karo. Kal ke mukable achanak drop to nahi?
  • Distinct counts: COUNT(DISTINCT col). ID column me distinct = rows hona chahiye.
  • Null %: har column me kitne null hain. 40% null wala column risky hai.
  • Min/Max: impossible values pakadne ke liye (negative amount, 1970 date, future date).
  • Value frequencies: top values dekho. Ek default value (like 0 ya 'NA') dominate to nahi kar rahi?
  • Data types: number string me stored to nahi hai?
  • Distribution quick look: mean, median, percentiles.
  • Cardinality: kam distinct = category, zyada distinct = ID ya free text.

Example

sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_,
       COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS users,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN email IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS email_null_pct,
       MIN(amount) AS min_amt, MAX(amount) AS max_amt
FROM transactions;

SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM transactions GROUP BY status ORDER BY 2 DESC;
python
df.describe(include="all")
df.isna().mean().mul(100).round(1)
df["status"].value_counts(dropna=False)

Agar min_amt negative aur status me 'sucess' jaise typo dikhe, to cleaning ki list ready hai.

Common mistakes

  • COUNT(col) aur COUNT(*) ka farak bhoolna. COUNT(col) nulls ignore karta hai.
  • value_counts() me dropna=False na lagana, nulls dikhte hi nahi.
  • Sirf average dekhna, min/max aur percentiles ignore karna.
  • Profile ek baar karke chhod dena, jabki data roz badalta hai.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Profiling me kya kya dekhte ho?
    A. Row count, distinct count, null %, min/max, top value frequencies, types aur date range.
  • Q. COUNT(*) vs COUNT(col)?
    A. COUNT(*) saari rows, COUNT(col) sirf non-null values.

Yaad rakho

Cleaning se pehle profile: counts, nulls, min/max, frequencies.

EDA-03Missing dataIntermediateMust Know

Missing values ka reason samjho (MCAR/MAR/MNAR), phir drop ya impute karo, aur missingness ko flag zaroor karo.

Simple me samjho

Missing data ek clue hai. Kabhi wo random hota hai, kabhi kisi wajah se. Bina wajah jaane mean bhar dena galat conclusion de sakta hai.

Key points

  • MCAR: Missing Completely At Random. Koi pattern nahi, jaise network glitch se kuch rows gir gayi.
  • MAR: Missing At Random. Missing hona kisi doosre observed column pe depend karta hai, jaise old Android app version me device field khaali.
  • MNAR: Missing Not At Random. Missing hona us value pe hi depend karta hai, jaise high earners income nahi batate.
  • Drop: rows ya column hata do. Tab theek jab missing kam ho aur MCAR ho.
  • Mean impute: symmetric numeric data me. Outliers se bigad jaata hai.
  • Median impute: skewed data (deposit amount) me better.
  • Mode impute: categorical column me sabse common value.
  • Forward fill: time series me pichli value. Jaise daily balance snapshot.
  • Flag missingness: is_missing column banao, taaki imputed aur real values alag dikhen.

Example

python
df["age_missing"] = df["age"].isna().astype(int)
df["age"] = df["age"].fillna(df["age"].median())
df = df.sort_values("date")
df["balance"] = df.groupby("user_id")["balance"].ffill()
sql
SELECT COALESCE(city, 'Unknown') AS city,
       (city IS NULL) AS city_missing
FROM users;

Flag column se baad me dekh sakte ho ki missing users ka behaviour alag hai ya nahi.

Common mistakes

  • Missing ko 0 se bhar dena. 0 aur "pata nahi" alag cheezein hain.
  • Mean se fill karke variance kam kar dena.
  • Reason jaane bina rows drop karna, jisse bias aata hai.
  • ffill ko user ya sort order ke bina chalana, jisse doosre user ki value aa jaati hai.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. MCAR, MAR, MNAR me farak?
    A. MCAR purely random, MAR doosre columns pe depend, MNAR khud us value pe depend karta hai. MNAR sabse risky hai.
  • Q. Mean ya median kab?
    A. Skewed ya outliers ho to median, roughly symmetric ho to mean.

Yaad rakho

Pehle wajah dhundo, phir drop/impute, aur hamesha missing flag rakho.

EDA-04DuplicatesBasicMust Know

Duplicate rows pehchano (exact ya near), sahi dedupe key chuno, aur latest record rakho.

Simple me samjho

Ek hi customer ka form do baar bhar diya gaya. Count double ho jaata hai. Dedupe ka matlab: ek entity ki ek hi row rakhna, sahi wali.

Key points

  • Exact duplicate: saare columns same. DISTINCT ya drop_duplicates() se hat jaate hain.
  • Near duplicate: thoda alag. Jaise Rahul@Gmail.com aur rahul@gmail.com, ya same user alag signup time ke saath.
  • Dedupe key: business ke hisaab se chuno (user_id, ya email lower+trim, ya txn_id).
  • Keeping latest: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY key ORDER BY updated_at DESC) aur rn = 1.
  • Kaaran: retries, double webhook delivery, ETL rerun, join fan-out.
  • Pehle count karo: kitne duplicate hain aur kaun se keys pe.
  • Cleaning ke baad verify: key ab unique hai ya nahi.

Example

sql
SELECT user_id, updated_at, plan
FROM (
  SELECT *,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY LOWER(TRIM(email))
                            ORDER BY updated_at DESC) AS rn
  FROM users
) t
WHERE rn = 1;
python
df["email_key"] = df["email"].str.strip().str.lower()
df = (df.sort_values("updated_at")
        .drop_duplicates("email_key", keep="last"))

Dono code har email ka sabse naya record rakhte hain. Email ko pehle normalise kiya, warna near duplicates bach jaate.

Common mistakes

  • DISTINCT * lagana jabki rows me timestamp alag hai, duplicate hataata hi nahi.
  • Galat key se dedupe karna aur real alag customers ko merge kar dena.
  • Sort order bina keep="last" use karna.
  • Duplicates ka root cause (ETL retry) fix na karna, sirf upar se saaf karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Latest record kaise rakhoge?
    A. ROW_NUMBER() partition by key, order by updated_at DESC, phir rn = 1.
  • Q. Near duplicate kaise handle?
    A. Pehle trim/lower se normalise karo, phir key pe dedupe. Zaroorat ho to fuzzy match.

Yaad rakho

Key socho, normalise karo, latest rakho, aur uniqueness verify karo.

EDA-05Type and format fixesBasicMust Know

Dates, currency, units, encoding, whitespace aur casing ko ek consistent format me laao.

Simple me samjho

Alag sources alag format me data dete hain. "01/02/2026" 1 Feb hai ya 2 Jan? Analysis se pehle sab ko ek hi standard me laana padta hai.

Key points

  • Dates: mixed formats (2026-02-01, 01/02/26, 1 Feb 2026). Format explicitly parse karo, guess mat karo.
  • Time zone: UTC me store, reporting me IST convert karo.
  • Currencies: INR, USD, ek hi currency me convert ya currency column rakho. Rate date ka dhyan rakho.
  • Units: paise vs rupees, chips vs real money, ms vs seconds.
  • Encoding: UTF-8 vs Latin-1. Galat encoding se Ã© jaise garbage characters aate hain.
  • Whitespace: leading/trailing spaces, non-breaking space. TRIM use karo.
  • Casing: LOWER/UPPER se normalise, join aur group by se pehle.
  • Numbers as text: "1,200" ya "Rs. 500" ko numeric me cast karo.

Example

python
df["created_at"] = pd.to_datetime(df["created_at"], format="%d/%m/%Y", errors="coerce")
df["amount"] = (df["amount"].astype(str)
                .str.replace(r"[^\d.]", "", regex=True).astype(float))
df["city"] = df["city"].str.strip().str.title()
sql
SELECT CAST(REPLACE(amount_txt, ',', '') AS NUMERIC) AS amount,
       TRIM(LOWER(email)) AS email
FROM raw_deposits;

errors="coerce" bad dates ko NaT bana deta hai. Unhe baad me count karke check karo.

Common mistakes

  • dd/mm aur mm/dd confuse karna. Format string explicitly do.
  • Time zone ignore karke "daily" numbers galat din me daalna.
  • Paise ko rupees samajhna (100x error).
  • errors="coerce" ke baad NaT count na dekhna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Mixed date formats kaise handle karte ho?
