OLTP live transactions chalata hai, OLAP analysis ke liye hota hai. Production DB se direct reporting karna risky hai.

Simple me samjho

OLTP ek bank counter jaisa hai: chhote chhote kaam, fast, ek-ek customer ka. OLAP ek audit room jaisa hai: saara record ek saath padhke summary nikalna. Dono ka kaam alag hai, isliye design bhi alag hota hai.

Key points

  • OLTP: Online Transaction Processing. Example: poker app ka bets, wallets, users table jo har second update hota hai.
  • OLAP: Online Analytical Processing. Example: "pichle 90 din ka stake-wise rake" jaisi query.
  • Workload: OLTP me bahut saare small read/write (insert, update by primary key). OLAP me kam queries but badi scans aur aggregations.
  • Schema: OLTP normalised (3NF) hota hai. OLAP denormalised star schema hota hai.
  • Storage: OLTP usually row-store (PostgreSQL, MySQL). OLAP usually column-store (BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift).
  • Data freshness: OLTP current state rakhta hai. OLAP history rakhta hai (saalon ka data).
  • Users: OLTP ke users app aur players hain. OLAP ke users analyst, BI tool, data scientist hain.
  • Why not report from production: heavy query locks aur CPU khaati hai, app slow ho jaata hai, players ko lag dikhta hai.
  • Other reasons: production me history overwrite ho jaati hai, multiple systems ka data join nahi hota, aur analyst galti se live data badal sakta hai.
  • Practical options: read replica (quick fix), ya proper warehouse me ETL/ELT se data copy karna (best).

Example

sql
-- OLTP query: ek player ka balance (fast, index se)
SELECT balance FROM wallets WHERE user_id = 1042;

-- OLAP query: sab players ka monthly rake (badi scan)
SELECT date_trunc('month', created_at) AS month, SUM(rake) AS total_rake
FROM bets
GROUP BY 1;

Pehli query milliseconds me 1 row deti hai. Dusri query crores rows scan karti hai aur agar production par chali to app ko slow kar sakti hai.

Common mistakes

  • Production primary DB par peak hours me heavy query chalana.
  • Read replica ko hi "warehouse" samajh lena. Replica me history aur joins ka design nahi hota.
  • Analytics tables me OLTP ki tarah har chhoti cheez normalise karna, phir 10 joins lagana.
  • Warehouse me data ko real-time maan lena jabki load delay hota hai.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. OLTP aur OLAP me main difference?
    A. OLTP chhote fast read/write transactions ke liye normalised row-store hai. OLAP badi aggregations ke liye denormalised, usually column-store hai.
  • Q. Production DB se report kyun nahi nikalte?
    A. Performance impact, locking, history missing, aur multiple source data join nahi hota. Warehouse ya replica use karte hain.

Yaad rakho

OLTP = operate the business, OLAP = analyse the business. Dono ko alag rakho.

DW-02Normalisation and denormalisationIntermediateMust Know

Normalisation duplicate data hataata hai (OLTP ke liye). Denormalisation joins kam karke queries fast aur simple banata hai (warehouse ke liye).

Simple me samjho

Normalisation matlab har fact ek hi jagah store karo, jaise contact list me ek number ek hi baar. Denormalisation matlab padhne me aasani ke liye data ki copy rakh dena. Write-heavy system ko normal chahiye, read-heavy system ko denormal.

Key points

  • 1NF: har cell me ek hi value (atomic), repeating groups nahi. tags = 'a,b,c' jaisa column 1NF tod'ta hai.
  • 2NF: 1NF + koi non-key column composite key ke sirf ek hisse par depend na kare (partial dependency nahi).
  • 3NF: 2NF + non-key column dusre non-key column par depend na kare (transitive dependency nahi). Example: city se state nikal raha ho to alag table.
  • Why normalise: update anomaly, insert anomaly, delete anomaly se bachna aur storage kam rakhna.
  • Cost of normalisation: reports me bahut joins, slow aur complex queries.
  • Why warehouses denormalise: scan fast, joins kam, BI tools ke liye simple, aur storage sasta hai.
  • Denormalised dim: dim_player me country_name seedha rakhte hain, alag countries table nahi.
  • Trade-off: denormalised data me redundancy hoti hai, isliye update ek controlled ETL se hi hota hai.
  • Wide table (OBT): kabhi kabhi ek hi badi flat table banate hain. Fast hai but maintain karna mushkil.

Example

text
Not 1NF:   orders(order_id, items)         -> items = 'chips,vip_pass'
1NF:       order_items(order_id, item)     -> 2 rows

Not 3NF:   users(user_id, city, state)     -> state depends on city
3NF:       users(user_id, city_id)
           cities(city_id, city, state)

Warehouse: dim_player(player_key, user_id, city, state, country)  -- flat

OLTP me city/state alag table me hai taaki ek jagah change ho. Warehouse me dim_player flat hai taaki analyst ko join na karna pade.

Common mistakes

  • Warehouse me bhi strict 3NF rakhna aur BI queries slow kar dena.
  • Denormalise karke source of truth bhool jana. Fix hamesha upstream me karo.
  • Comma-separated values ek column me store karna (1NF violation) aur phir LIKE se search karna.
  • 2NF/3NF definitions ko ratta marna bina example ke.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. 3NF kya hai?
    A. Table 2NF me ho aur koi non-key column kisi dusre non-key column par depend na kare, sab sirf key par depend karein.
  • Q. Warehouse me denormalise kyun?
    A. Reads aur aggregations fast hote hain, joins kam, query simple. Storage sasta hai aur writes ETL se control hote hain.

Yaad rakho

OLTP me normalise (write safe), warehouse me denormalise (read fast).

DW-03Star and snowflake schemaIntermediateMust Know

Star schema me beech me fact table aur charo taraf dimension tables hote hain. Snowflake me dimensions aur aage normalise hote hain.

Simple me samjho

Fact table ek bill book jaisi hai: kya hua, kitna hua. Dimension table ek directory jaisi hai: kisne, kahan, kab. Star me directory flat hai. Snowflake me directory ke andar sub-directories hoti hain.

Key points

  • Fact table: events/measurements store karta hai, jaise bet_amount, rake. Numeric aur additive columns plus foreign keys.
  • Dimension table: descriptive attributes, jaise player ka country, game ka type. Filters aur group by yahin se aate hain.
  • Grain: fact table ki ek row kya represent karti hai. Pehle grain decide karo, jaise "one row per bet".
  • Join path: fact se dimension tak foreign key join. Dimensions ke beech seedha join nahi hota.
  • Star schema: dimensions denormalised, ek hi join level. Simple aur fast.
  • Snowflake schema: dimension ke andar sub-dimension, jaise dim_game -> dim_game_category. Storage kam, joins zyada.
  • Conformed dimension: ek hi dim_date ya dim_player kai fact tables share karte hain.
  • Additive measures: SUM kar sakte ho (bet_amount). Non-additive: ratios, averages, unko sum nahi karte.
  • Which to prefer: zyada tar BI me star schema prefer hota hai.

Example

sql
CREATE TABLE dim_player (
  player_key  BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
  player_id   VARCHAR(40),
  country     VARCHAR(40),
  vip_tier    VARCHAR(20)
);
CREATE TABLE dim_date (date_key INT PRIMARY KEY, full_date DATE, month INT, year INT);
CREATE TABLE fact_bets (   -- grain: one row per bet
  bet_id      BIGINT,
  player_key  BIGINT REFERENCES dim_player(player_key),
  date_key    INT    REFERENCES dim_date(date_key),
  bet_amount  NUMERIC(12,2),
  rake        NUMERIC(12,2)
);

SELECT d.year, p.country, SUM(f.rake) AS rake
FROM fact_bets f
JOIN dim_player p ON p.player_key = f.player_key
JOIN dim_date   d ON d.date_key   = f.date_key
GROUP BY d.year, p.country;

Fact ek baar me dono dimensions se join hota hai. Ye classic star-schema query hai.

Common mistakes

  • Grain define kiye bina fact table banana, phir duplicate counts aana.
  • Fact table me text descriptions bhar dena. Wo dimension me jaane chahiye.
  • Fact aur dimension ke beech many-to-many join se rows explode ho jaana.
  • Har cheez ko snowflake karke joins badha dena bina need ke.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Star aur snowflake me fark?
    A. Star me dimensions denormalised (ek level join). Snowflake me dimensions normalised multiple tables me, storage kam but joins zyada.
  • Q. Grain kya hai?
    A. Fact table ki ek row kis level ki hai, jaise per bet ya per player per day. Sab measures us grain ke hone chahiye.

Yaad rakho

Pehle grain, phir facts, phir dimensions. Star se shuru karo.

DW-04Fact table typesAdvancedGood to Have

Teen types: transaction (ek event = ek row), periodic snapshot (fixed interval ka status), accumulating snapshot (process ke milestones ek row me).

Simple me samjho

Transaction fact CCTV recording jaisa hai: har event record. Periodic snapshot roz subah ka photo hai: aaj balance kitna. Accumulating snapshot ek parcel tracking jaisa hai: ek row, milestones update hote rehte hain.

Key points

  • Transaction fact: ek event ek row, jaise har bet ya har deposit. Sabse detailed grain, sabse zyada rows.
  • Periodic snapshot: fixed interval par state, jaise fact_wallet_daily (player, date, closing_balance). Row tab bhi banti hai jab koi activity nahi hui.
  • Accumulating snapshot: ek business process ki ek row, jaise withdrawal request: requested, approved, paid dates. Row update hoti hai jab milestone aata hai.
  • Semi-additive: balance jaise measures time par sum nahi hote (aaj aur kal ka balance add nahi karte), player par sum ho sakte hain.
  • Date columns: accumulating snapshot me multiple date keys hote hain (requested_date, approved_date, paid_date).
  • Lag columns: accumulating me hours_to_approve jaise duration measures useful hote hain.
  • Choice: events analysis ke liye transaction, trend of state ke liye snapshot, pipeline/funnel timing ke liye accumulating.
  • Factless fact: ek aur type hai jisme measure nahi hota, sirf event ka hona record hota hai (jaise login hua). Interview me naam se bas aana chahiye.

Example

sql
-- Periodic snapshot: roz ka closing balance
CREATE TABLE fact_wallet_daily (
  date_key        INT,
  player_key      BIGINT,
  closing_balance NUMERIC(14,2)
);

-- Accumulating snapshot: withdrawal lifecycle
CREATE TABLE fact_withdrawal (
  withdrawal_id      BIGINT,
  player_key         BIGINT,
  requested_date_key INT,
  approved_date_key  INT,   -- NULL jab tak approve na ho
  paid_date_key      INT,
  amount             NUMERIC(12,2),
  hours_to_approve   NUMERIC(8,2)
);

Snapshot me ek player-day = ek row. Withdrawal me ek request = ek row jo stage badalne par UPDATE hoti hai.

Common mistakes

  • Balance jaise semi-additive measure ko date par SUM kar dena.
  • Accumulating snapshot ko append-only samajhna. Isme row update hoti hai.
  • Sab kuch ke liye sirf transaction fact rakhna, phir daily balance nikalna slow ho jaana.
  • Periodic snapshot me inactive days ki rows miss kar dena.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Periodic snapshot kab use karte ho?
    A. Jab regular interval par state track karni ho, jaise daily balance ya inventory. Trend analysis aasaan hota hai.
  • Q. Accumulating snapshot kya hai?
    A. Ek process instance ki ek row jo milestones ke saath update hoti hai, jaise order ya withdrawal lifecycle.

Yaad rakho

Event = transaction, status over time = periodic, lifecycle = accumulating.

DW-05Slowly changing dimensionsAdvancedGood to Have

SCD batata hai ki dimension ke attributes badalne par history kaise handle karein: overwrite (Type 1), nayi row (Type 2), nayi column (Type 3).

Simple me samjho

Player ka VIP tier Silver se Gold ho gaya. Purane bets ka report Silver ke saath dikhana hai ya Gold ke saath? Ye decision SCD type tay karta hai.

Key points

  • Type 1: purani value overwrite. History nahi. Typo fix ke liye theek.
  • Type 2: nayi row add, purani row expire. Poori history milti hai. Sabse common.
  • Type 3: nayi column previous_tier. Sirf ek pichli value rakhta hai. Kam use hota hai.
  • Effective dates: valid_from aur valid_to columns batate hain ki row kab se kab tak valid thi.
  • Current flag: is_current (true/false) se latest row jaldi mil jaati hai. Current row ka valid_to aksar 9999-12-31 ya NULL.
  • Surrogate key: Type 2 me har version ka naya player_key hota hai, natural key (player_id) same rehti hai.
  • Fact join: fact me us version ka player_key store hota hai jo event ke time valid tha. Isse point-in-time correct report milti hai.
  • Detecting change: ETL me source rows ko current dim row se compare karte hain (ya hash).
  • dbt: snapshots feature Type 2 jaisa kaam karta hai.

Example

SCD2 dim_player table, player P7 ka tier badla:

player_keyplayer_idvip_tiervalid_fromvalid_tois_current
101P7Silver2026-01-012026-06-30false
245P7Gold2026-07-019999-12-31true
sql
-- Step 1: purani row expire
UPDATE dim_player SET valid_to = DATE '2026-06-30', is_current = false
WHERE player_id = 'P7' AND is_current = true;
-- Step 2: nayi row insert
INSERT INTO dim_player (player_key, player_id, vip_tier, valid_from, valid_to, is_current)
VALUES (245, 'P7', 'Gold', '2026-07-01', '9999-12-31', true);

June ke bets key 101 (Silver) se jude rahenge, July ke bets key 245 (Gold) se.

Common mistakes

  • Type 2 me natural key ko primary key bana dena. Duplicate aa jayenge.
  • Fact load me current row se join karna jabki historical row chahiye.
  • Dates overlap ho jaana (gap ya overlap in valid_from/valid_to).
  • Har column par Type 2 laga dena. Sirf wahi jinki history chahiye.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. SCD Type 1 vs 2?
    A. Type 1 overwrite karta hai, history jaati hai. Type 2 nayi row banata hai, history safe rehti hai.
  • Q. Type 2 me fact kaise sahi version se jude?
    A. Fact load ke time event date ke hisaab se valid dim row ka surrogate key fact me store karte hain.

Yaad rakho

History chahiye to Type 2: nayi row, naya surrogate key, valid_from/valid_to.

DW-06KeysIntermediateGood to Have

Surrogate key warehouse ka apna system-generated id hai, natural key business ka id. Stable keys joins aur history safe rakhti hain.

Simple me samjho

Natural key aapka Aadhaar jaisa hai, business ne diya. Surrogate key hostel ka room number jaisa hai, hamare system ne diya, aur wo sirf hamare liye matlab rakhta hai.

Key points

  • Natural key: source ka business id, jaise player_id, email, order_no. Meaning rakhta hai.
  • Surrogate key: warehouse ka generated integer ya hash, jaise player_key. Business meaning nahi.
  • Why surrogate: source id reuse ya format change ho sakta hai, multiple source systems ke ids clash kar sakte hain, aur SCD2 me ek player ke multiple versions chahiye.
  • Composite key: do ya zyada columns milke unique, jaise (player_id, table_id, hand_id). Join me sab columns lagte hain.
  • Key stability: key kabhi change nahi honi chahiye. Email natural key ke liye bura choice hai kyunki badal sakti hai.
  • Primary key: row ko uniquely identify karta hai. Foreign key: dusre table ki primary key ko refer karta hai.
  • Warehouse constraints: BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift me PK/FK declare hote hain par usually enforce nahi hote. Uniqueness ko tests se check karo.
  • Hash keys: surrogate key ko natural key columns ke hash se bhi bana sakte hain (dbt me common pattern).
  • Unknown member: missing dimension ke liye ek default row (player_key = -1) rakhte hain taaki fact join na tute.

Example

sql
CREATE TABLE dim_player (
  player_key  BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, -- surrogate (PostgreSQL)
  player_id   VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,                            -- natural key
  vip_tier    VARCHAR(20),
  valid_from  DATE,
  valid_to    DATE
);
-- composite natural key example
CREATE TABLE fact_hand_player (
  hand_id BIGINT, player_key BIGINT, pot_won NUMERIC(12,2),
  PRIMARY KEY (hand_id, player_key)
);

player_id same rahegi, SCD2 me player_key har version ke saath badlegi.

Common mistakes

  • Email ya phone ko primary key banana.
  • Surrogate key bana ke natural key ko drop kar dena. Natural key reconcile ke liye chahiye.
  • Warehouse me PK declare karke maan lena ki duplicates nahi aayenge.
  • Composite key ke ek hi column par join karke rows duplicate kar dena.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Surrogate key kyun?
    A. Source change se independent, multiple systems merge kar sakte hain, aur SCD2 me versions ko unique identify karti hai.
  • Q. Key stability ka matlab?
    A. Ek baar assign hone ke baad key ki value kabhi nahi badalni chahiye, warna joins aur history toot jaati hai.

Yaad rakho

Natural key rakho reconcile ke liye, surrogate key use karo joins ke liye.

DW-07Warehouse vs lake vs lakehouseIntermediateGood to Have

Warehouse structured cleaned data rakhta hai, lake raw files, lakehouse dono ka mix. Schema on write vs schema on read ka fark yaad rakho.

Simple me samjho

Warehouse ek organised library hai: har book shelf par label ke saath. Lake ek godown hai: sab kuch daal do, baad me dekhenge. Lakehouse godown me hi library ke rules laga deta hai.

Key points

  • Data warehouse: structured tables, cleaned data, SQL se fast analytics. Examples: BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift.
  • Data lake: raw files (JSON, CSV, Parquet, logs, images) cheap object storage me (S3, GCS, ADLS).
  • Lakehouse: lake storage ke upar table format aur transactions, jaise Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, Apache Hudi. Databricks isi concept se jaana jaata hai.
  • Schema on write: data likhte waqt schema fix aur validate. Warehouse ka style. Padhna fast, load strict.
  • Schema on read: data jaisa hai waisa store, padhte waqt structure lagate hain. Lake ka style. Load flexible, quality ki zimmedari baad me.
  • Data types: warehouse structured data ke liye. Lake structured, semi-structured aur unstructured sab ke liye.
  • Cost: lake storage sasta hai. Warehouse compute aur managed performance ke liye paise leta hai.
  • Users: warehouse analyst/BI ke liye. Lake data engineers aur data scientists ke liye.
  • Risk: bina governance ke lake "data swamp" ban jaata hai.

Example

text
Raw poker events (JSON) -> S3 bucket       = data lake (schema on read)
Cleaned tables fact_bets, dim_player       = warehouse (schema on write)
Parquet + Delta/Iceberg table on S3        = lakehouse (files + ACID + SQL)

Same data ko ek hi storage par rakhke BI aur ML dono chalana lakehouse ka maqsad hai.

Common mistakes

  • Lake me dump karke maan lena ki data analysis-ready hai.
  • Lake aur warehouse ko competitors samajhna. Aksar dono saath use hote hain.
  • Schema on read me bad data ko pakadne ke tests na lagana.
  • Lakehouse ko "magic" samajhna. Governance aur modelling phir bhi chahiye.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Schema on read vs write?
    A. Write me load ke time schema enforce hota hai (warehouse). Read me raw store hota hai aur query ke time schema lagta hai (lake).
  • Q. Lakehouse kyun?
    A. Lake ki cheap flexible storage ke saath warehouse jaisa ACID, schema aur SQL performance milta hai.

Yaad rakho

Warehouse = structured aur fast. Lake = raw aur cheap. Lakehouse = dono ka compromise.

DW-08Cloud warehousesIntermediateMust Know

BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Synapse sab cloud warehouses hain. Main idea: storage aur compute alag, aur cost query ke scan ya compute time par.

Simple me samjho

Cloud warehouse ek rented godown plus rented workers jaisa hai. Samaan rakhne ka kiraya alag, aur workers ka kiraya sirf jab kaam karte hain. Isliye "kitna data scan kiya" seedha bill se juda hai.

Key points

  • Storage vs compute: modern warehouses me data storage alag aur query compute alag scale hota hai. Compute band karke bhi data safe rehta hai.
  • BigQuery (Google): serverless. On-demand pricing me bill scanned bytes par. Flat-rate/capacity pricing bhi hai.
  • Snowflake: virtual warehouses (compute clusters) alag size ke hote hain. Bill credits me, running time ke hisaab se (per second, minimum ke saath).
  • Redshift (AWS): traditional me cluster of nodes, node-hours ka bill. Redshift Serverless bhi hai. Distribution key aur sort key important hote hain.
  • Synapse (Azure): dedicated SQL pool (DWU capacity ke hisaab se) aur serverless SQL pool (data processed ke hisaab se).
  • Cost per query: scan kam karo to cost kam. SELECT * avoid karo, partition filter lagao.
  • Concurrency: kai users ek saath queries chalayein to compute alag warehouse/pool me isolate kar sakte hain.
  • Column store: sirf required columns padhe jaate hain, isliye column count ka cost par seedha asar hota hai.
  • Pricing details: rates aur plans badalte rehte hain, isliye provider ka current pricing page dekho. Yahan sirf model samjho.

Example

sql
-- BigQuery: bad (poori table ke saare columns scan)
SELECT * FROM analytics.fact_bets;

-- BigQuery: better (sirf 2 columns, aur partition filter)
SELECT player_key, SUM(rake) AS rake
FROM analytics.fact_bets
WHERE bet_date BETWEEN '2026-11-01' AND '2026-11-07'
GROUP BY player_key;

Doosri query kam bytes scan karti hai, isliye BigQuery on-demand me sasti. Snowflake me same query sasti isliye hai ki kam time chalti hai aur chhota warehouse kaafi hota hai.

Common mistakes

  • SELECT * ya bina date filter ke badi table par query chalana.
  • Snowflake warehouse ko chalta chhod dena. Auto-suspend set karo.
  • Sab providers ko same mehsoos karna. Pricing aur tuning ka tareeka alag hai.
  • Dev queries bhi production size compute par chalana.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Storage aur compute separation ka fayda?
    A. Dono alag scale hote hain, compute sirf zarurat par chalta hai, aur multiple teams ek hi data par alag compute se kaam kar sakti hain.
  • Q. BigQuery me cost kaise kam karoge?
    A. Partition filter, sirf zaroori columns, clustering, aur repeated heavy queries ko materialised table me daalna.

Yaad rakho

Cloud warehouse me bill = data scan ya compute time. Dono ko control karo.

DW-09Data layersIntermediateMust Know

Data ko layers me rakhte hain: raw, cleaned, curated. Isse debugging, reuse aur trust badhta hai. Bronze/silver/gold isi ka naam hai.

Simple me samjho

Ye ek kitchen jaisa hai: pehle sabzi aati hai (raw), phir dhoke kaati jaati hai (cleaned), phir dish ban ke plate me jaati hai (curated). Har step alag rakhne se galti kahan hui, pata chal jaata hai.

Key points

  • Raw / staging: source jaisa data, bina badle. Sirf load time, source name, batch id jaise metadata. Re-run ke liye source of truth.
  • Cleaned: duplicates hata, types cast, nulls handle, names standard, timezone UTC. Business logic kam.
  • Curated: business logic lagi hui star schema, facts, dimensions, metrics. Analyst yahin se kaam karta hai.
  • Bronze / silver / gold: Databricks/lakehouse terminology. Bronze = raw, silver = cleaned, gold = curated.
  • Data marts: ek team ya function ke liye chhota subset, jaise mart_finance, mart_marketing. Curated layer ke upar bante hain.
  • Naming: schemas/prefixes se layer clear karo, jaise stg_, int_, fct_, dim_ (dbt convention).
  • Access: analysts ko curated/marts access, raw sirf engineers ko.
  • Reprocessing: raw safe hai to upar ki layers dobara bana sakte hain.
  • Over-layering: har dataset ko 6 layers me mat todo. Zaroorat jitne hi layers.

Example

text
raw.app_bets_json          (as loaded, append-only)
   |
silver.bets_clean          (dedupe, cast, UTC time)
   |
gold.fact_bets + gold.dim_player   (star schema)
   |
mart_finance.daily_rake    (finance team ka summary)

Agar daily_rake galat dikhe to ek ek layer peeche jaake dekhte hain ki kahan bigda.

Common mistakes

  • Raw layer ko edit ya overwrite kar dena, phir reprocess impossible.
  • Business rules cleaned layer me chhupa dena, phir har team ko alag number milna.
  • Analysts ko raw tables par dashboards banane dena.
  • Marts me logic duplicate karna jo curated me hona chahiye.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Bronze, silver, gold kya hain?
    A. Bronze raw data, silver cleaned aur conformed data, gold business-ready aggregated ya modelled data.
  • Q. Data mart kya hai?
    A. Ek business function ke liye focused subset of curated data, jaise marketing ya finance.

Yaad rakho

Raw ko chhedo mat, clean me safai karo, curated me business logic lagao.

DW-10Partitioning and clusteringAdvancedGood to Have

Partition table ko hisson me baant'ta hai (aksar date se), clustering ek partition ke andar data ko sort karta hai. Dono scan cost kam karte hain.

Simple me samjho

Partition ek almirari ke date-wise drawers hain. Aapko 5 November chahiye to sirf wohi drawer kholte ho. Clustering us drawer ke andar files ko player_id ke order me lagana hai.

Key points

  • Partition: table ko physical parts me todna, usually date/timestamp column se. BigQuery, Redshift Spectrum, Hive-style lake tables me common. Snowflake automatically micro-partitions banata hai.
  • Partition pruning: query me partition column par filter ho to engine baaki partitions skip kar deta hai.
  • Clustering / cluster keys: data ko chune hue columns ke order me co-locate karna. BigQuery me CLUSTER BY, Snowflake me clustering key.
  • Scan cost: kam partitions aur blocks scan = kam bytes = kam cost aur fast query. BigQuery on-demand me bytes par bill.
  • Good partition column: wo jo filters me roz aata ho aur low-cardinality chunks de, jaise event date.
  • Good cluster column: filters aur joins me aane wale high-cardinality columns, jaise player_id.
  • Function trap: filter me partition column par function lagane se pruning toot sakti hai (engine par depend karta hai). Seedha range filter lagao.
  • Too many partitions: bahut chhote partitions overhead badhate hain.
  • Dialect: Redshift me partition ki jagah sort key aur distribution key use hote hain.

Example

sql
-- BigQuery
CREATE TABLE analytics.fact_bets (
  bet_id BIGINT, player_id STRING, bet_ts TIMESTAMP, rake NUMERIC
)
PARTITION BY DATE(bet_ts)
CLUSTER BY player_id;

SELECT SUM(rake)
FROM analytics.fact_bets
WHERE DATE(bet_ts) = '2026-11-05' AND player_id = 'P7';

Sirf 5 Nov ka partition scan hota hai, aur uske andar P7 ke blocks. Baaki table skip hoti hai.

Common mistakes

  • Partition column par filter na lagana, phir poori table scan.
  • Low-value column par partition karna (jaise sirf 2 values wala flag).
  • Bahut zyada chhote partitions banana (per hour per player).
  • Cluster key ko aise badalna ki queries ke filters se match hi na kare.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Partition pruning kya hai?
    A. Query ke filter ke basis par engine un partitions ko padhta hi nahi jo result me aa nahi sakte, isse scan aur cost kam hoti hai.
  • Q. Partition aur cluster me fark?
    A. Partition table ko alag parts me baant'ta hai, cluster ek part ke andar rows ko sort karke group karta hai.

Yaad rakho

Date par partition, filter columns par cluster, aur hamesha partition filter lagao.

DW-11Data lineage and catalogIntermediateGood to Have

Lineage batati hai ki number kahan se aaya aur change ka asar kahan padega. Catalog data assets ki searchable list hai.

Simple me samjho

Lineage ek family tree jaisa hai: ye dashboard kis table se bana, wo table kin tables se. Catalog us tree aur data ki Google search jaisa hai.

Key points

  • Data lineage: source se report tak data ka path (table -> model -> dashboard).
  • Where a number comes from: dashboard ka Total Rake kis query, table aur raw source se aaya, ye lineage se pata chalta hai.
  • Upstream: jahan se data aata hai (sources, parent models).
  • Downstream: jo data use karte hain (child models, dashboards, ML jobs).
  • Impact analysis: column rename ya table drop karne se pehle downstream check karo ki kya tootega.
  • Root cause analysis: number galat ho to upstream trace karke bug dhoondho.
  • Column-level lineage: table ki jagah column tak lineage. Zyada detailed hai, har tool me nahi hoti.
  • Data catalog: datasets, columns, owners, descriptions ki searchable inventory. Tools: DataHub, Collibra, Alation, Atlan, aur cloud native (Google Dataplex, AWS Glue Data Catalog).
  • dbt: ref() aur source() se dbt docs me lineage graph khud banta hai.
  • Catalog hygiene: owner aur description bina update ke catalog bekaar ho jaata hai.

Example

text
raw.app_bets -> stg_bets -> fct_bets -> mart_daily_rake -> "Rake Dashboard"

Question: stg_bets.stake_amt ka naam badalna hai.
Downstream check: fct_bets, mart_daily_rake, dashboard
Action: pehle teeno update karo ya owners ko inform karo.

Lineage ke bina rename silently dashboard tod sakta tha.

Common mistakes

  • Table change karne se pehle downstream consumers check na karna.
  • Lineage ko sirf tool ka kaam samajhna. Manual SQL scripts lineage me nahi aate.
  • Catalog me descriptions aur owners khali chhodna.
  • Dashboard ke andar hidden calculations ko lineage me na dikhana.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Lineage kyun zaroori?
    A. Galat number ka source trace karne aur change ke impact (upstream/downstream) samajhne ke liye.
  • Q. Catalog aur dictionary me fark?
    A. Catalog poora searchable inventory tool hai (owners, lineage, usage). Dictionary columns ke meaning ka document hai, aksar catalog ke andar hota hai.

Yaad rakho

Change se pehle downstream dekho, bug me upstream dekho.

DW-12Data dictionaryBasicMust Know

Data dictionary har table/column ka meaning, owner, allowed values aur update process likhti hai taaki sab ek hi matlab samjhein.

Simple me samjho

Ye ek shabdkosh hai data ka. "rake" ka matlab finance aur product team dono ke liye same likha ho. Naya analyst bina poochhe samajh jaye, ye iska maqsad hai.

Key points

  • Column meanings: har column ki simple definition, jaise rake = house commission per hand in INR.
  • Data type and unit: type, unit aur timezone likho (bet_ts UTC, amount INR paise me ya rupees me).
  • Owners: har table/column ka owner (team ya person) jisse sawaal puchh sakein.
  • Allowed values: enum ya range, jaise status in (pending, approved, rejected).
  • Nullability and defaults: NULL kab aata hai aur uska matlab kya hai.
  • Source and logic: column kahan se aaya, formula kya hai (net_revenue = bets - wins - bonus).
  • Update process: schema change par dictionary update karna pull request ya release checklist ka hissa ho.
  • Where to keep: dbt schema.yml descriptions, catalog tool ya shared sheet. Ek hi source of truth.
  • Metric definitions: sirf columns nahi, Active Player jaise business terms bhi likho.

Example

ColumnMeaningTypeAllowed valuesOwner
statusWithdrawal request ki stateVARCHARpending, approved, rejected, paidPayments team
rakeHouse commission per hand, INRNUMERIC(12,2)>= 0Finance
bet_tsBet time, UTCTIMESTAMPnot nullGame engineering

Naya analyst rake ko galti se player ka profit nahi samjhega, kyunki unit aur meaning likha hai.

Common mistakes

  • Dictionary ek baar likhke bhool jana, schema change par update na karna.
  • Vague definitions jaise "amount of the bet" bina unit ke.
  • Do alag documents rakhna jinme alag alag definitions hon.
  • Owner ka naam na likhna, phir sawaal kisse poochein pata nahi.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Data dictionary me kya hota hai?
    A. Column meaning, type, unit, allowed values, owner, source logic aur update history.
  • Q. Isko updated kaise rakhoge?
    A. Schema change ke PR me dictionary update mandatory karo, aur dbt descriptions ya catalog se automate karo.

Yaad rakho

Jo column likha nahi, uska matlab har banda apna alag nikalega. Likho, owner do, update karo.

DW-13Calendar and date dimensionIntermediateGood to Have

dim_date ek pre-built calendar table hai jisme har date ke attributes hote hain: month, week, fiscal period, holiday, weekend flags.

Simple me samjho

Har query me date se month ya quarter nikalna bar bar mushkil hai. Ek calendar table bana lo jisme sab pehle se ready ho. Fact table sirf date_key rakhe.

Key points

  • Why dim_date: ek jagah par date logic, sab reports me consistent. Holiday ya fiscal quarter jaise attributes SQL function se nahi nikalte.
  • Date key: integer jaise 20261105 (YYYYMMDD), simple aur sortable.
  • Fiscal calendar: company ka financial year (India me aksar April se March). fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter columns alag rakho.
  • Holidays: is_holiday aur holiday_name. Country specific ho sakta hai, jaise Diwali, IPL final.
  • Week start: kuch jagah Monday, kuch jagah Sunday. Ye ek baar dim_date me decide karo, taaki week reports match karein. (ISO week Monday se shuru hoti hai.)
  • Day flags: is_weekend, is_month_end, is_payday. Weekend vs weekday analysis easy.
  • Gap-free dates: har date row ho, taaki "no activity" wale days bhi report me aayein (LEFT JOIN se zero dikhe).
  • Time of day: alag dim_time ya hour column; date dimension me time nahi rakhte.
  • Timezone: date kis timezone ki hai, ye clear rakho (UTC vs IST).

Example

sql
-- PostgreSQL: dim_date generate karo
CREATE TABLE dim_date AS
SELECT
  TO_CHAR(d, 'YYYYMMDD')::INT                         AS date_key,
  d::DATE                                             AS full_date,
  EXTRACT(ISODOW FROM d) IN (6, 7)                    AS is_weekend,
  DATE_TRUNC('week', d)::DATE                         AS week_start_monday,
  CASE WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM d) >= 4
       THEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM d) + 1
       ELSE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM d) END                  AS fiscal_year  -- Apr-Mar FY
FROM generate_series('2026-01-01'::DATE, '2030-12-31'::DATE, '1 day') AS d;

Ek hi table se weekend, fiscal year aur week start sab reports me same milte hain. fiscal_year yahan us saal ko dikhata hai jisme FY khatam hota hai.

Common mistakes

  • Har report me alag fiscal year logic likhna.
  • Date range limited rakhna, phir future dates ka join fail hona.
  • Week start ka agreement na hona (Monday vs Sunday), numbers mismatch.
  • Timezone ignore karna, jisse late-night bets galat din me aana.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Date dimension kyun banate hain?
    A. Date attributes (fiscal, holiday, week, flags) ek jagah consistent rakhne ke liye aur gap-free reporting ke liye.
  • Q. Fiscal calendar kaise handle karoge?
    A. dim_date me fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter columns, jo company ke FY start month se nikalte hain.

Yaad rakho

Date logic ek baar dim_date me, har query me nahi.

DW-14Event tracking schemaIntermediateMust Know

Event tracking me app ke user actions ko event name, properties, user id aur session id ke saath ek fixed plan me log karte hain.

Simple me samjho

Event ek CCTV note jaisa hai: "kaun ne, kab, kya kiya, kis context me." Agar naming aur fields har developer ki marzi se hon, to analysis impossible ho jaata hai. Isliye tracking plan banta hai.

Key points

  • Event name: action jo hua, jaise table_joined, deposit_completed. Past tense aur clear.
  • Properties: event ka context, jaise table_id, stake, amount, payment_method.
  • User id: logged-in player ka stable id. Anonymous user ke liye anonymous_id, aur login ke baad dono ko link karte hain.
  • Session id: ek visit/session ke events group karne ke liye. Session ka rule (jaise 30 min inactivity) pehle tay karo.
  • Timestamp: client time aur server time dono bhej sakte ho. Warehouse me UTC rakho.
  • Naming conventions: ek style choose karo, jaise snake_case, object_action (deposit_completed). Mix mat karo.
  • Tracking plan: document jisme har event, uski properties, types, kab fire hota hai aur owner likha ho.
  • Versioning: schema badle to event version ya naya property add karo, purane events mat todo.
  • Validation: bad events ko ingest par reject ya quarantine karo.

Example

json
{
  "event_name": "deposit_completed",
  "event_ts": "2026-11-05T14:22:10Z",
  "user_id": "P7",
  "anonymous_id": "a1f9",
  "session_id": "s-889",
  "properties": { "amount": 500, "currency": "INR", "payment_method": "upi" }
}
sql
SELECT DATE(event_ts) AS d, COUNT(*) AS deposits
FROM events
WHERE event_name = 'deposit_completed'
GROUP BY 1;

Ek hi event_name par saari deposit counting hoti hai. Agar kisi ne Deposit Done naam se bheja hota to ye miss ho jaata.

Common mistakes

  • Same action ke liye alag naam (deposit_ok, DepositCompleted).
  • Properties ke type badalna (amount kabhi string, kabhi number).
  • Session id ya user id bhejna bhool jaana.
  • Tracking plan na rakhna ya release ke baad update na karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Tracking plan kya hota hai?
    A. Ek document jisme har event ka naam, properties, types, trigger aur owner likha hota hai taaki data consistent rahe.
  • Q. Event me kaunse ids zaroori hain?
    A. User id (aur anonymous id), session id, aur timestamp. Inke bina funnel aur retention nahi nikal sakte.

Yaad rakho

Naming aur properties ka plan pehle, tracking baad me. Warna analysis me dard.

ETL & Automation 12 topics

ETL-01ETL vs ELTBasicMust Know

ETL me data warehouse me jaane se pehle transform hota hai, ELT me pehle load hota hai aur transform warehouse ke andar hota hai.

Simple me samjho

ETL: sabzi ghar bhejne se pehle dukaan par kaat do. ELT: sabzi seedha ghar bhej do, kitchen me kaato. Cloud warehouse ka kitchen bada aur powerful hai, isliye ELT popular hai.

Key points

  • ETL: Extract, Transform, Load. Transformation alag server ya tool me hoti hai, phir clean data warehouse me jaata hai.
  • ELT: Extract, Load, Transform. Raw data pehle warehouse me, phir SQL se warehouse ke andar transform.
  • Where transformation happens: ETL me ETL tool/server par. ELT me warehouse ke compute par (SQL, dbt).
  • Why ELT in modern stacks: cloud warehouses scalable aur sasti storage deti hain, raw data safe rehta hai, aur SQL se analysts khud transform kar sakte hain.
  • Reprocess: ELT me raw data warehouse me hai, to logic badalke dobara build karna aasan hai.
  • ETL ke fayde: sensitive data (PII) load se pehle mask ho sakta hai, aur warehouse me sirf clean data jaata hai.
  • Tools: ELT ke liye Fivetran/Airbyte (load) + dbt (transform). ETL ke liye Informatica, SSIS, Talend ya custom scripts.
  • Compliance: PII ya regulation ho to kuch columns load se pehle hatana padta hai, ye ETL jaisa step hota hai.
  • Hybrid: practice me dono mix hote hain.

Example

text
ETL:  app DB -> Python script (clean, join) -> warehouse.fact_bets
ELT:  app DB -> loader -> warehouse.raw.bets -> dbt SQL -> warehouse.fact_bets
sql
-- ELT ka T: warehouse ke andar SQL
CREATE TABLE gold.daily_rake AS
SELECT DATE(bet_ts) AS d, SUM(rake) AS rake
FROM raw.bets
GROUP BY 1;

Raw table warehouse me hai, isliye agar rake ka formula badle to bas SQL change karke rebuild karo.

Common mistakes

  • ELT me raw PII ko bina access control ke warehouse me chhod dena.
  • ETL script me business logic hide karke documentation na likhna.
  • "ELT = no cleaning" samajhna. Transform ab bhi karna padta hai, bas baad me.
  • Warehouse compute cost ignore karna jab saari transformations wahin chalti hain.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. ETL vs ELT?
    A. ETL transform load se pehle karta hai, ELT raw load karke warehouse me transform karta hai.
  • Q. ELT kyun prefer hota hai?
    A. Cloud warehouse ka scalable compute aur sasta storage, raw data reprocess ho sakta hai, aur SQL based transformations analysts bhi kar sakte hain.

Yaad rakho

Cloud warehouse hai to Load pehle, Transform baad me (ELT).

ETL-02Batch vs streamingIntermediateGood to Have

Batch data ko fixed intervals par bulk me process karta hai, streaming har event ko aate hi. Fark latency aur cost ka hai.

Simple me samjho

Batch ek bus jaisa hai jo har ghante chalti hai. Streaming ek auto jaisa hai jo jab sawari aaye tab chal padta hai. Auto fast hai par mehnga, bus sasti hai par wait karna padta hai.

Key points

  • Batch: data ko jama karke schedule par chalana, jaise roz raat 2 baje ya har ghante.
  • Streaming: events ko continuous process karna, seconds ya milliseconds me.
  • Latency: batch me minutes se ghante/din. Streaming me seconds ya kam.
  • Cost and complexity: batch simple aur sasta. Streaming complex (ordering, late events, state, always-on infra).
  • Batch use cases: daily revenue report, finance reconciliation, monthly KPIs, ML training.
  • Streaming use cases: fraud/collusion alerts, live leaderboard, real-time bonus abuse detection, live dashboards.
  • Micro-batch: beech ka raasta, har 1-5 minute me chhote batches (jaise Spark Structured Streaming ka default model).
  • Tools: batch me Airflow, dbt, scheduled SQL. Streaming me Kafka, Flink, Spark Streaming, Kinesis, Pub/Sub.
  • Late data: streaming me late events ko handle karne ke liye watermark jaise concepts hote hain.
  • Rule: business ko real-time kyun chahiye, ye pehle poochho.

Example

text
Use case                          Choice      Reason
Daily rake report for finance     Batch       Roz ek baar kaafi hai
"Player ne 5 min me 20 withdrawals
 kiye" fraud alert                Streaming   Turant action chahiye
Live tournament leaderboard       Streaming   Seconds me update

Agar decision sirf subah ek baar lena hai to streaming pipeline par paise kharch karna waste hai.

Common mistakes

  • Bina zarurat ke streaming banana kyunki "real-time cool hai".
  • Batch ke liye late-arriving data ka plan na rakhna.
  • Streaming aur batch numbers me mismatch ko samjhaye bina dashboards dikhana.
  • Streaming job ke monitoring aur replay ka plan na hona.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Batch vs streaming kab?
    A. Latency requirement dekho. Daily/hourly reports batch se, alerts aur live features streaming se.
  • Q. Micro-batch kya hai?
    A. Bahut chhote batches jo har kuch seconds ya minutes me chalte hain, near real-time deta hai kam complexity me.

Yaad rakho

Sirf utna real-time banao jitna business ko sach me chahiye.

ETL-03Orchestration with AirflowIntermediateGood to Have

Airflow pipelines ko DAG ke roop me schedule, retry, monitor aur backfill karta hai. Tasks ke dependencies yahin define hote hain.

Simple me samjho

Airflow ek manager hai jo bolta hai: pehle ye kaam, phir wo kaam, fail ho to dobara try karo, aur time par chalao. Kaam khud nahi karta, kaam ka order aur timing sambhalta hai.

Key points

  • DAG: Directed Acyclic Graph. Tasks aur unke dependencies ka graph, bina loop ke.
  • Task: DAG ka ek kaam, jaise SQL chalana ya script. Operators (jaise BashOperator, PythonOperator) tasks banate hain.
  • Schedule: cron jaisa expression ya preset (@daily). Naye Airflow versions me parameter schedule hai, purane me schedule_interval.
  • Retries: retries aur retry_delay se fail hone par auto retry.
  • Backfill: past dates ke liye DAG runs chalana. catchup=True se missed intervals chalte hain. Command line se airflow dags backfill.
  • Sensors: wait karne wale tasks, jaise file S3 me aane ka intezaar (S3KeySensor) ya upstream data ready hone ka.
  • Logical date: run ka data interval dikhata hai. Daily DAG ka run interval ke end par chalta hai, ye confusing hota hai.
  • XCom: tasks ke beech chhota data pass karne ke liye. Badi data pass mat karo.
  • UI: runs, logs, failed tasks dekhne aur rerun karne ke liye.

Example

python
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from airflow import DAG
from airflow.operators.bash import BashOperator

with DAG(
    dag_id="daily_rake_pipeline",
    start_date=datetime(2026, 1, 1),
    schedule="@daily",
    catchup=False,
    default_args={"retries": 2, "retry_delay": timedelta(minutes=5)},
) as dag:
    extract = BashOperator(task_id="extract", bash_command="python extract.py {{ ds }}")
    transform = BashOperator(task_id="transform", bash_command="dbt run --select daily_rake")
    test = BashOperator(task_id="test", bash_command="dbt test --select daily_rake")

    extract >> transform >> test

Roz chalega: extract, phir dbt run, phir dbt test. Fail hone par 2 baar 5-5 minute baad retry. {{ ds }} run ki date deta hai.

Common mistakes

  • Tasks idempotent na banana, retry/backfill par duplicates aana.
  • catchup ka default samjhe bina DAG deploy karna, aur achanak purane saare runs chal jaana.
  • Badi dataframes XCom me bhejna.
  • Heavy processing Airflow worker me karna jabki warehouse ko karni chahiye.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. DAG kya hai?
    A. Tasks ka directed graph bina cycle ke, jo batata hai kaunsa task kiske baad chalega.
  • Q. Sensor kab?
    A. Jab kisi external cheez ka intezaar karna ho, jaise file ya upstream table ready hone ka, bina fail kiye.

Yaad rakho

Airflow orchestrate karta hai, process nahi. Tasks ko idempotent rakho.

ETL-04dbt basicsIntermediateGood to Have

dbt warehouse ke andar SQL models se transformation karta hai, tests, docs aur lineage ke saath. Ye ELT ka T hai.

Simple me samjho

dbt me aap sirf SELECT likhte ho, dbt use table ya view bana deta hai. Tests aur documentation saath me aate hain. Ye SQL ko software project ki tarah treat karta hai.

Key points

  • Model: ek .sql file jisme SELECT hota hai. dbt use table/view banata hai.
  • Source: raw tables ko declare karna (source() function). Isse freshness check aur lineage milti hai.
  • ref(): ek model dusre model ko {{ ref('model') }} se refer karta hai. Dependency order dbt khud nikalta hai.
  • Tests: schema tests jaise unique, not_null, accepted_values, relationships. Custom SQL tests bhi.
  • Docs: YAML descriptions se dbt docs generate documentation aur lineage graph banata hai.
  • Materializations: view, table, incremental, ephemeral.
  • Incremental models: sirf naya data process karo, is_incremental() block se.
  • Jinja: SQL me templating, {{ }} expressions aur {% %} logic ke liye. Loops, macros aur variables me use.
  • Commands: dbt run, dbt test, dbt build (run + test), dbt docs generate.

Example

sql
-- models/fct_bets.sql
{{ config(materialized='incremental', unique_key='bet_id') }}

SELECT bet_id, player_id, bet_ts, rake
FROM {{ source('app', 'bets') }}
{% if is_incremental() %}
WHERE bet_ts > (SELECT MAX(bet_ts) FROM {{ this }})
{% endif %}
yaml
# models/schema.yml
version: 2
models:
  - name: fct_bets
    description: One row per bet
    columns:
      - name: bet_id
        tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: player_id
        tests:
          - relationships: {to: ref('dim_player'), field: player_id}

Pehli baar poori table banti hai, baad me sirf naye bets aate hain. Tests bet_id ki uniqueness aur player_id ka dimension me hona check karte hain.

Common mistakes

  • Source tables ko ref() ki jagah hardcode karna, lineage toot jaati hai.
  • Incremental model me unique_key na dena, duplicates ban jaate hain.
  • Tests na likhna kyunki "SQL chal gayi".
  • Jinja ko over-use karke SQL ko unreadable bana dena.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. dbt kya karta hai?
    A. Warehouse me SQL models se T karta hai, dependency order, tests, docs aur lineage ke saath.
  • Q. Incremental model kya hai?
    A. Jo sirf naye ya badle rows process karta hai, full rebuild ki jagah. is_incremental() se logic lagti hai.

Yaad rakho

dbt = SELECT likho, ref() se jodo, tests lagao.

ETL-05Incremental loads and idempotencyAdvancedGood to Have

Incremental load sirf naya data laata hai. Idempotent pipeline ko kitni bhi baar rerun karo, result same rehta hai aur duplicates nahi aate.

Simple me samjho

Roz poora data dobara load karna ghar ki poori safai roz karne jaisa hai. Incremental matlab sirf aaj ka kachra uthana. Idempotent matlab ek hi kaam do baar karne par bhi ghar ek jaisa saaf rahe.

Key points

  • Full load: poori table har baar. Simple but badi tables par slow aur mehngi.
  • Incremental load: sirf naye ya badle rows, usually updated_at ya auto-increment id ke watermark se.
  • Watermark: last successful load ki max timestamp/id. Agla run usse aage se padhta hai.
  • Idempotency: rerun karne par duplicates nahi, result same.
  • MERGE / UPSERT: key ke basis par existing rows update, nayi insert. Duplicates se bachata hai.
  • Delete + insert by partition: ek date partition ko hata ke dobara likhna. Simple idempotent pattern.
  • Late data: data late aaye to watermark ke peeche chhut sakta hai. Overlap window (jaise last 2 din re-read) rakho.
  • Hard deletes: source me delete hui rows incremental me nahi dikhti. Soft delete flag ya CDC chahiye.
  • Dedupe: ROW_NUMBER() se latest row choose karo.

Example

sql
-- Idempotent upsert (PostgreSQL syntax)
INSERT INTO fact_bets (bet_id, player_key, bet_ts, rake)
SELECT bet_id, player_key, bet_ts, rake
FROM stg_bets
WHERE bet_ts >= DATE '2026-11-05' - INTERVAL '2 days'
ON CONFLICT (bet_id) DO UPDATE
SET rake = EXCLUDED.rake, bet_ts = EXCLUDED.bet_ts;

2 din ka overlap late data pakadta hai. ON CONFLICT ki wajah se rerun par duplicate nahi banta, sirf update hota hai. Dusre warehouses me MERGE use hota hai.

Common mistakes

  • Plain INSERT se rerun karna, aur duplicates aana.
  • Watermark ko strict > rakhna jisse same timestamp wali rows miss hoti hain.
  • Pipeline fail hone par watermark pehle hi aage badha dena.
  • Source ke deletes ko ignore karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Idempotency kya hai?
    A. Operation ko ek ya zyada baar chalane par same final result. Pipelines me rerun safe hona.
  • Q. Duplicates kaise rokoge?
    A. MERGE/upsert on unique key, ya partition ko delete karke dobara insert, aur unique tests.

Yaad rakho

Naya laao, key se merge karo, rerun safe rakho.

ETL-06Ingestion toolsIntermediateBonus

Ingestion tools source se warehouse tak data laate hain. Fivetran aur Airbyte managed connectors dete hain, Kafka event streams ke liye, CDC DB changes ke liye.

Simple me samjho

Har source ke liye apni script likhna thaka dene wala hai. Ingestion tools readymade connectors dete hain: source chuno, destination chuno, sync chalu.

Key points

  • Fivetran: managed, paid SaaS connectors. Setup aasan, maintenance kam.
  • Airbyte: open-source (aur cloud) connectors, zyada flexibility, self-host ka option.
  • Connector: kisi source (Postgres, Mongo, Stripe) se data padhne wala module.
  • Sync modes: full refresh aur incremental. Incremental sync cursor column par chalta hai.
  • Schema drift: source me naya column aaye to tool use sambhalta hai ya fail hota hai, ye tool par depend karta hai.
  • Kafka: distributed event log. Events publish aur consume hote hain. Streaming ingestion ka common base.
  • CDC (Change Data Capture): database ke transaction log (jaise PostgreSQL WAL, MySQL binlog) se insert/update/delete changes pakadna. Debezium ek popular open-source CDC tool hai.
  • CDC ka fayda: low load aur deletes bhi capture hote hain.
  • Build vs buy: custom script sasti lagti hai par maintenance bhari padti hai.

Example

text
Postgres (app DB)
   --CDC (Debezium)--> Kafka topic "app.public.bets"
   --consumer/sink---> warehouse.raw.bets

Stripe API --Fivetran/Airbyte--> warehouse.raw.stripe_charges

DB se CDC deletes aur updates bhi deta hai. API sources ke liye managed connector hota hai, apni script nahi likhni padti.

Common mistakes

  • Connector chalu karke row counts source se match na karna.
  • Raw data me PII aa jaana aur masking ya access control na lagana.
  • Schema change par pipeline silent toot jaana.
  • CDC chalu karke DB logs ke disk usage ko monitor na karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. CDC kya hai?
    A. Source DB ke transaction log se row-level changes (insert/update/delete) pakadke downstream bhejna, bina poori table query kiye.
  • Q. Fivetran vs Airbyte?
    A. Fivetran managed paid service hai. Airbyte open-source/self-host option deta hai aur zyada customisable hai.

Yaad rakho

Connectors reuse karo, DB changes ke liye CDC, events ke liye Kafka.

ETL-07File formatsIntermediateGood to Have

CSV aur JSON human-friendly row formats hain. Parquet aur ORC columnar analytics formats hain, Avro row-based streaming/schema formats ke liye.

Simple me samjho

CSV ek simple Excel-jaisa text file hai. Parquet ek smart packed box hai jisme columns alag alag compress hote hain, isliye analytics me bahut fast aur chhota.

Key points

  • CSV: plain text, easy, par types nahi, quoting/delimiter issues, schema nahi.
  • JSON: nested data support, flexible, par verbose aur slow analytics ke liye.
  • Parquet: columnar, compressed, schema ke saath, analytics ke liye best. Spark, BigQuery, Snowflake, Athena sab support karte hain.
  • ORC: columnar format, Hive/Hadoop ecosystem me common. Parquet jaisa idea.
  • Avro: row-based binary format jisme schema saath rehta hai. Kafka ke saath common.
  • Row vs column: row format me poori row saath, writes aasan. Columnar me ek column ke saare values saath, selective reads fast.
  • Compression: gzip, snappy, zstd. Snappy fast, gzip zyada compress. Kaunsa best, data aur use par depend.
  • Schema evolution: naye columns add karna ya types badalna. Avro aur Parquet iska kuch support dete hain (add column aasan, type change risky).
  • Splittable: Parquet files parallel read ho sakte hain. Compressed CSV (gzip) aksar nahi hote.

Example

text
Format    Layout    Schema        Best use
CSV       row       none          small exports, Excel
JSON      row       flexible      API payloads, logs
Avro      row       embedded      Kafka messages
Parquet   column    embedded      lake / warehouse analytics
ORC       column    embedded      Hive-style lakes
sql
-- PostgreSQL: CSV export; Parquet ke liye Spark ya warehouse ke export commands lagte hain
COPY (SELECT * FROM bets WHERE bet_ts >= '2026-11-01') TO '/tmp/bets.csv' CSV HEADER;

Agar analytics query sirf rake column padhti hai, Parquet baaki columns skip kar deta hai. CSV poori file padhta hai.

Common mistakes

  • Badi analytics data CSV me store karna.
  • CSV me commas, newlines aur encoding ka dhyan na rakhna.
  • Schema evolution me column type badalna aur readers ka tootna.
  • Chhoti-chhoti hazaaron Parquet files banana (small files problem).

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Parquet kyun?
    A. Columnar aur compressed hai, schema saath hai, aur sirf zaroori columns padhe jaate hain, isliye analytics fast aur sasta.
  • Q. Avro vs Parquet?
    A. Avro row-based hai, streaming aur schema evolution ke liye. Parquet columnar hai, analytics ke liye.

Yaad rakho

Exchange ke liye CSV/JSON, analytics storage ke liye Parquet.

ETL-08SchedulingBasicMust Know

Scheduling pipelines ko time ya dependency par chalata hai. cron simple hai, cloud schedulers aur Airflow dependencies aur retries bhi sambhalte hain.

Simple me samjho

Scheduling alarm clock jaisa hai: ye kaam is time par chalao. Par agar pehla kaam (data load) abhi khatam nahi hua, to doosra kaam (report) mat chalao. Wahi dependency hai.

Key points

  • cron: Linux scheduler. Format minute hour day month weekday. Example 0 2 * * * = roz 02:00.
  • Cloud schedulers: Cloud Scheduler (GCP), EventBridge Scheduler (AWS), BigQuery scheduled queries, Snowflake tasks. Managed, server nahi chahiye.
  • Time zones: cron server ke timezone me chalta hai. UTC me schedule karna aur code me convert karna safe hai.
  • DST: daylight saving wale timezones me 1 ghanta repeat ya skip ho sakta hai. India me DST nahi hota, par global system me hota hai.
  • Dependencies: report tab chale jab upstream load success ho. Sirf time par bharosa mat karo.
  • Fixed time vs event-driven: "2 baje chalao" vs "file aate hi chalao". Event-driven dependency ke liye better.
  • Overlap: purana run khatam hone se pehle naya na chale (concurrency limit).
  • Run date: job ko batao ki kis date ka data process karna hai, now() par depend mat karo.
  • Cron limits: cron me retries, alerts, dependencies nahi hote. Orchestrator use karo.

Example

text
# cron: roz 02:00 UTC par load, 03:00 UTC par report
0 2 * * *  /opt/etl/load_bets.sh   --date $(date -u -d yesterday +\%F)
0 3 * * *  /opt/etl/build_rake.sh  --date $(date -u -d yesterday +\%F)

Problem: agar load 03:00 tak chala to report adhoora data par chalegi. Isliye dependency chahiye, jise Airflow jaise tools handle karte hain.

Common mistakes

  • Server timezone ko pata kiye bina cron lagana.
  • Time gap rakhke dependency ka kaam chalana ("1 ghante baad to ho hi jayega").
  • Job me now() use karna, jisse rerun par alag date ka data aata hai.
  • Overlapping runs jo same table ko ek saath likhte hain.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. cron expression 0 2 * * * ka matlab?
    A. Roz subah 02:00 baje.
  • Q. Time based schedule ki problem?
    A. Upstream late ho to downstream adhoore data par chalta hai. Dependency based orchestration chahiye.

Yaad rakho

UTC me schedule karo, date parameter do, dependencies bandho.

ETL-09Pipeline monitoring and failure handlingIntermediateMust Know

Pipeline fail hoga, ye maan ke chalo. Alerts, retries, freshness checks, SLAs aur on-call ownership pehle se tay rakho.

Simple me samjho

Pipeline ek railway track jaisa hai. Train late ho sakti hai, isliye signal, announcement aur ek zimmedar stationmaster chahiye. Chup chaap fail hona sabse bada khatra hai.

Key points

  • Alerts: fail hone par Slack/email/pager. Alert actionable ho: kaunsa pipeline, kaunsa task, link logs ka.
  • Retries: temporary errors (network, API limit) ke liye auto retry with delay. Permanent bugs retry se theek nahi hote.
  • Freshness checks: table me latest data kitna purana hai. Example: MAX(event_ts) 2 ghante se purana ho to alert. dbt me source freshness check hai.
  • Volume checks: aaj ke row counts normal range me hain ya nahi.
  • Data quality tests: not_null, unique, accepted_values aur business rules (rake >= 0).
  • SLA: promise jaise "dashboard roz 8 baje tak ready". SLA miss ho to alert.
  • Who gets paged: har pipeline ka owner aur on-call rota. Alert sabko mat bhejo.
  • Alert fatigue: bahut zyada noisy alerts ignore hone lagte hain. Severity levels rakho.
  • Runbook: common failure aur fix ki short guide.
  • Silent failures: job success dikhe par data khali ho, isliye data checks, sirf job status nahi.

Example

sql
-- Freshness + volume check
SELECT
  MAX(bet_ts)                                   AS latest_bet,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE bet_ts >= CURRENT_DATE) AS rows_today
FROM fact_bets;
-- Alert: latest_bet < NOW() - INTERVAL '2 hours' OR rows_today < 1000

Ye query PostgreSQL syntax me hai. Agar pipeline chal rahi hai par data aa hi nahi raha, to freshness check isse pakad leta hai jabki job status green dikhta.

Common mistakes

  • Sirf job fail par alert, data galat hone par nahi.
  • Har chhoti warning par page karna, aur team ka alert ignore karna.
  • Owner tay na hona, to fail hone par koi dekhta hi nahi.
  • Retry ko fix samajhna aur root cause ko ignore karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Freshness check kya hai?
    A. Data kitna naya hai ye check karna, jaise latest timestamp threshold se purana ho to alert.
  • Q. Silent failure kaise pakdoge?
    A. Row count, freshness aur quality tests, kyunki job success hone ka matlab data sahi hona nahi.

Yaad rakho

Job status nahi, data ki health monitor karo, aur owner pehle se tay rakho.

ETL-10Backfills and reprocessingAdvancedGood to Have

Backfill purane dates ka data dobara build karta hai (bug fix ya naya logic ke baad). Safe backfill idempotent hota hai aur badle hue numbers ki communication zaroori hai.

Simple me samjho

Rake formula me galti mili. Ab pichhle 3 mahine ke numbers dobara banane honge. Ye backfill hai. Dhyan ye rakhna hai ki purani reports ke numbers badal jayenge, aur logon ko batana padega.

Key points

  • Backfill: past date range ke liye pipeline dobara chalana.
  • Reprocessing: existing data ko naye logic se dobara transform karna.
  • When: bug fix, naya column/metric, source late data, schema change.
  • Safe rebuilding: idempotent logic, date-partition wise delete + insert ya MERGE.
  • Test first: pehle chhote range (1 din) par chalao aur purane se compare karo.
  • Chunking: lamba range chhote chunks me (hafta/mahina) chalao taaki load na badhe.
  • Raw layer: raw data safe ho to hi reliable backfill ho sakta hai.
  • Staging copy: nayi table me build karke compare karo, phir swap karo.
  • Communicating changed numbers: kya badla, kyun, kitna fark, kab se. Stakeholders ko pehle batao, dashboards par note lagao.
  • Downstream: marts, dashboards aur exports ko bhi refresh karo.

Example

bash
# Airflow: 1 se 7 November ka backfill (idempotent DAG chahiye)
airflow dags backfill daily_rake_pipeline -s 2026-11-01 -e 2026-11-07
text
Comms template:
Metric: Net Rake (Nov 1-7)
Reason: rake formula me bonus ka double count tha
Impact: -2.3% (old 1.20 Cr -> new 1.17 Cr)
Effective: reports updated Nov 20

Bina communication ke finance purane numbers se compare karke confuse ho jayegi.

Common mistakes

  • Production table par seedha backfill chalana bina comparison ke.
  • Non-idempotent job backfill karna aur duplicates bana dena.
  • Dashboards refresh na karna, phir alag-alag numbers dikhna.
  • Stakeholders ko bataye bina historical numbers badal dena.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Safe backfill kaise karte ho?
    A. Idempotent logic, chhote chunks, pehle test range, purane numbers se comparison, aur phir swap ya merge.
  • Q. Numbers badle to kya karoge?
    A. Reason, impact aur effective date ke saath stakeholders ko inform karoge aur dashboard par note lagaoge.

Yaad rakho

Backfill idempotent rakho, compare karo, aur badle numbers ka khud ailaan karo.

ETL-11Queues and event dataIntermediateBonus

Queues (Redis, RabbitMQ, Kafka) services ke beech messages bhejti hain. Events inhi se consume hoke warehouse tak pahunchte hain.

Simple me samjho

Queue ek post office jaisa hai: sender chitthi daalta hai, receiver apni speed se uthata hai. Producer aur consumer ko ek doosre ka wait nahi karna padta.

Key points

  • Queue / message broker: producer messages bhejta hai, consumer unhe process karta hai. Decoupling aur buffering milti hai.
  • Redis: in-memory store, lists/streams/pub-sub se queue ban sakti hai. Libraries jaise BullMQ job queue ke liye Redis use karti hain.
  • RabbitMQ: message broker (AMQP protocol). Queues, exchanges, routing. Message consume hone ke baad queue se hat'ta hai.
  • Kafka: distributed log. Messages topic me partitions me rehte hain aur retention period tak rakhe jaate hain. Multiple consumers apne offset se alag alag padh sakte hain, replay possible.
  • Queue vs log: RabbitMQ aksar task delivery ke liye, Kafka event history aur streaming analytics ke liye.
  • Events to warehouse: app event emit karta hai -> broker -> consumer/sink -> object storage ya warehouse raw table -> transform.
  • Delivery: at-least-once me duplicates ho sakte hain, isliye warehouse me dedupe (event_id) chahiye.
  • Ordering and late events: events out of order ya late aa sakte hain. event_ts aur ingested_at dono rakho.
  • Dead-letter queue: bad ya failed messages alag queue me jaate hain.

Example

text
Game server --event--> Kafka topic "game.events"
   --sink connector--> S3 (Parquet) / warehouse raw.events
   --dbt--> stg_events -> fct_hands
sql
-- At-least-once delivery ke baad dedupe
SELECT * FROM (
  SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY event_id ORDER BY ingested_at DESC) AS rn
  FROM raw.events
) t WHERE rn = 1;

Kafka consumer retry ke karan same event 2 baar aa sakta hai, event_id par dedupe analysis ko safe banata hai.

Common mistakes

  • Queue ko permanent storage samajhna (RabbitMQ me consume hone par message hat'ta hai).
  • Event ids ke bina dedupe karne ki koshish.
  • Event time aur ingestion time ko mix karna.
  • Dead-letter queue ko monitor na karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. RabbitMQ vs Kafka?
    A. RabbitMQ message routing aur task queues ke liye hai. Kafka durable, replayable event log hai jo high-volume streaming ke liye use hota hai.
  • Q. Events warehouse tak kaise pahunchte hain?
    A. Broker se consumer ya sink connector raw table/files me likhta hai, phir ELT transformations chalti hain.

Yaad rakho

Queue message bhejti hai, Kafka log rakhta hai, warehouse me hamesha dedupe karo.

ETL-12APIs for pushing dataIntermediateBonus

Reverse ETL warehouse ka curated data wapas business tools (CRM, marketing, support) me bhejta hai, aksar un tools ki APIs se.

Simple me samjho

Ab tak data warehouse me aata tha. Reverse ETL me warehouse ka insight, jaise "ye players churn hone wale hain", CRM ya email tool me chala jaata hai taaki team action le sake.

Key points

  • Reverse ETL: warehouse se operational tools tak data bhejna. Example: segment list ko CRM me sync karna.
  • Use cases: VIP/churn audience marketing tool me, lead score sales tool me, support tool me player value.
  • Tools: Hightouch, Census jaise reverse ETL tools. Ya custom script jo API call kare.
  • API push: HTTP request (POST/PUT) se record create ya update.
  • Rate limits: APIs limit lagati hain, batches aur retries with backoff chahiye.
  • Idempotent updates: upsert by external id, taaki rerun par duplicate contacts na bane.
  • Incremental sync: sirf badli hui rows bhejo, har baar poora data nahi.
  • Auth and secrets: API keys secret manager me, code me nahi.
  • Privacy: sirf zaroori fields bhejo, PII aur consent rules follow karo.

Example

python
import requests

rows = [{"player_id": "P7", "segment": "high_value"}]  # warehouse query se aaya
for r in rows:
    resp = requests.put(
        f"https://crm.example.com/api/contacts/{r['player_id']}",
        json={"segment": r["segment"]},
        headers={"Authorization": "Bearer <token from secret manager>"},
        timeout=10,
    )
    resp.raise_for_status()

PUT by player id ka matlab rerun par duplicate contact nahi banta, wahi record update hota hai. URL aur fields ek hypothetical CRM ke hain.

Common mistakes

  • API ke rate limit ki wajah se pipeline fail hona, bina retry/backoff ke.
  • Har baar poora segment bhej dena aur tool ke records overwrite karna.
  • Secrets code ya repo me daal dena.
  • Consent na dekhe marketing tool me data bhejna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Reverse ETL kya hai?
    A. Warehouse ke curated data ko wapas operational business tools (CRM, ads, support) me sync karna.
  • Q. API push me duplicates kaise rokte ho?
    A. External id se upsert (PUT/merge), aur incremental sync, taaki rerun safe rahe.

Yaad rakho

Warehouse me insight bana ke chhodo mat, tools me bhejo, par safely aur idempotently.

Analytics Techniques 19 topics

AN-01Four types of analyticsBasicMust Know

Analytics ke chaar level: kya hua, kyun hua, kya hoga, aur ab kya karein. Har level pichle par bana hota hai.

Simple me samjho

Doctor ka example lo. Pehle report dekhta hai (kya hua), phir reason dhoondta hai (kyun hua), phir risk batata hai (aage kya hoga), phir dawai likhta hai (kya karein). Data analytics me bhi yehi chaar steps hote hain.

Key points

  • Descriptive: "Kya hua?" Past ka summary. Dashboard, KPIs, daily revenue, DAU. Sabse common kaam.
  • Diagnostic: "Kyun hua?" Root cause. Drill-down, segment compare, metric decomposition, funnel, cohort.
  • Predictive: "Kya hoga?" Forecast ya probability. Churn prediction, revenue forecast, CLV prediction.
  • Prescriptive: "Kya karna chahiye?" Best action suggest karna. Kis player ko kaunsa bonus, optimisation, A/B test se decision.
  • Difficulty vs value: Descriptive aasan, prescriptive mushkil. Lekin business value upar jaate hue badhti hai.
  • Dependency: Bina clean descriptive data ke diagnostic ya predictive galat niklega.
  • Analyst ka daily kaam: Zyadatar descriptive + diagnostic. Predictive me DS team ke saath kaam hota hai.
  • Tools: Descriptive me SQL/BI. Diagnostic me SQL/Python. Predictive me sklearn/statsmodels. Prescriptive me experiments/optimisation.

Example

Poker platform ka rake scenario:

TypeQuestionOutput
DescriptiveLast week rake kitna tha?Rake 12 lakh, pichle week se -10%
DiagnosticKyun gira?Weekend ke tournaments cancel hue, active players -8%
PredictiveAgle week kya hoga?Forecast 11.5 lakh agar same trend
PrescriptiveKya karein?Weekend freeroll + reload bonus lagao, expected +0.6 lakh

Dekho, har row pichli row ka answer use karti hai.

Common mistakes

  • Seedha predictive model banana jabki basic descriptive numbers hi trust nahi hote.
  • Diagnostic ke bina action lena. Reason pata nahi to fix galat hoga.
  • Prescriptive recommendation dena bina test ke. Correlation se action decide mat karo.
  • Dashboard banake kaam khatam samajhna. Insight aur next step bhi batao.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Diagnostic aur predictive me kya farak hai?
    A. Diagnostic past ka reason batata hai, predictive future ka outcome ya probability. Pehla explain karta hai, doosra forecast.
  • Q. Aapne kaunsa type zyada kiya?
    A. Honest bolo: descriptive aur diagnostic daily, predictive basic forecasts ya churn flags me. Ek real example do.

Yaad rakho

Kya hua, kyun hua, kya hoga, kya karein: har level pichle level ke trusted data par chalta hai.

AN-02Trend and period comparisonBasicMust Know

Numbers ko sahi period se compare karo: WoW, MoM, YoY, same weekday, seasonality aur adhuri period ke traps se bacho.

Simple me samjho

Akele number ka matlab nahi hota. "Revenue 5 lakh" achha hai ya bura, ye comparison se pata chalta hai. Lekin galat period se compare karoge to galat story banegi.

Key points

  • WoW (week over week): Is week vs pichla week. Short-term movement ke liye.
  • MoM (month over month): Is month vs pichla month. Mahine me alag din hote hain (28 to 31), dhyan rakho.
  • YoY (year over year): Is period vs pichle saal ka same period. Seasonality hatane ke liye best.
  • Same weekday last week: Friday ko pichle Friday se compare karo. Poker me weekend aur weekday ka behaviour bahut alag hota hai.
  • Seasonality: Festival, salary day, IPL, holidays. Peak ko trend mat samjho.
  • Partial-period trap: Chalu month ke 15 din ko poore pichle month se compare karna galat hai. Same days compare karo (MTD vs MTD).
  • Growth formula: (current - previous) / previous. Base zero ho to growth undefined.
  • Percentage vs absolute: Dono dikhao. Chhote base par +50% bada lagta hai par absolute chhota ho sakta hai.
  • Trend smooth karo: 7-day moving average se daily noise kam hota hai.

Example

sql
-- PostgreSQL: WoW growth
WITH weekly AS (
  SELECT date_trunc('week', created_at) AS wk, SUM(amount) AS revenue
  FROM transactions GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT wk, revenue,
       LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY wk) AS prev_rev,
       ROUND(100.0 * (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY wk))
             / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY wk), 1) AS wow_pct
FROM weekly ORDER BY wk;

Agar is week 540 aur pichle week 500 hai, to WoW = (540-500)/500 = +8.0%.

Partial-period trap: October (31 din) revenue 310. November ke pehle 15 din = 135. Galat compare: (135-310)/310 = -56.5%. Sahi compare: October ke pehle 15 din = 150, to (135-150)/150 = -10%.

Common mistakes

  • Incomplete current week/month ko full period se compare karna.
  • Different weekday mix wale periods compare karna (4 vs 5 Fridays).
  • Seasonality ignore karke festival peak ko growth bolna.
  • Sirf percentage dikhana, base batana bhool jana.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. MoM ki jagah YoY kab use karoge?
    A. Jab seasonality strong ho. YoY same season ko compare karta hai, to festival ya holiday effect cancel ho jata hai.
  • Q. Month ke beech me dashboard par MoM kaise dikhaoge?
    A. MTD vs previous month ke same day-count tak (MTD vs MTD), ya run-rate projection with clear label.

Yaad rakho

Hamesha like-for-like compare karo: same length, same weekday mix, same season.

AN-03Metric decompositionIntermediateMust Know

Revenue ko factors me todo (users x conversion x AOV) aur dekho kaunsa factor kitna move hua.

Simple me samjho

Revenue girne ya badhne ka ek hi reason nahi hota. Usse chhote parts me todte hain, jaise car ka total time = distance / speed. Phir har part ka contribution alag nikalte hain.

Key points

  • Basic identity: Revenue = Users x Conversion x AOV. Poker me: Rake = Active players x Hands per player x Rake per hand.
  • Goal: Dhoondna ki change kis factor se aaya. Yehi diagnostic ka core hai.
  • Sequential method: Ek ek factor ko current value par badlo, baaki ko old rakho (ya order me). Total effects sum karke exact total change dete hain.
  • Order matters: Sequential method me order badalne se effects thoda badal jaate hain. Order fix karke batao.
  • Log/percentage method: Percentage me approx: %Rev ~ %Users + %Conv + %AOV (chhote changes ke liye).
  • Additive metrics ke liye: Revenue = sum of segments, to segment-wise contribution nikalo (mix effect).
  • Tree: Revenue ke neeche users, uske neeche new + returning, etc. Branch-wise drill karo.
  • Output: Ek waterfall chart ya table: Start, factor effects, End.

Example

Pichla month: 100,000 users, 5% conversion, AOV 400. Is month: 110,000 users, 4.5%, AOV 420.

text
Old revenue = 100,000 x 0.05 x 400 = 2,000,000
New revenue = 110,000 x 0.045 x 420 = 2,079,000  (change +79,000)

Users effect = (110,000-100,000) x 0.05  x 400 = +200,000
Conv effect  = 110,000 x (0.045-0.05)   x 400 = -220,000
AOV effect   = 110,000 x 0.045 x (420-400)    =  +99,000
Total = 200,000 - 220,000 + 99,000 = +79,000  (matches)

Revenue sirf +3.95% badha, par asli story hai: traffic badhi, par conversion gir gayi. Conversion fix karo to bada upside hai.

Common mistakes

  • Effects ka sum total change se match nahi karta kyunki interaction term chhoot gaya.
  • Order mention nahi karna, phir stakeholder alag answer nikalta hai.
  • Aise factors lena jo independent nahi hain (e.g. users aur conversion aapas me linked).
  • Decomposition ko "reason" samajhna. Ye batata hai kya move hua, kyun hua ye alag investigation hai.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Revenue 10% gira, kaise investigate karoge?
    A. Pehle Users x Conversion x AOV me todunga, dekhunga kaunsa factor gira, phir us factor ko channel, device, geo se drill karunga.
  • Q. Interaction term kya hai?
    A. Jab do factors saath badalte hain, unka combined effect alag se aata hai. Sequential method use karne se wo kisi factor me absorb ho jata hai.

Yaad rakho

Metric ko factors me todo, effects sum karke total change se verify karo.

AN-04Funnel analysisIntermediateMust Know

User ke stages track karo (visit se deposit tak), har step ka conversion nikalo aur segment-wise leak pakdo.

Simple me samjho

Funnel ek paani ki pipe jaisa hai. Upar se 10,000 daalo, neeche 400 nikalte hain. Analyst ka kaam hai dhoondna ki paani kahan leak ho raha hai.

Key points

  • Stages: Ordered steps. Poker app: Install, Signup, KYC, First deposit, First game.
  • Step conversion: Is stage / pichla stage. Isse pata chalta hai kahan sabse bada drop hai.
  • Overall conversion: Last stage / first stage.
  • Segment-wise leaks: Funnel ko device, channel, geo, app version se split karo. Aksar leak ek hi segment me hota hai.
  • Strict vs loose funnel: Strict me steps order me hone chahiye. Loose me bas event hona chahiye.
  • Time window: Conversion window fix karo (e.g. signup ke 7 din ke andar deposit).
  • Unique users count karo, events nahi. COUNT(DISTINCT user_id).
  • Drop-off: 100% minus conversion. Yehi fix karne wali jagah hai.

Example

Total: Visit 10,000 -> Signup 2,000 -> Deposit 500 -> First game 400.

text
Visit -> Signup   : 2,000 / 10,000 = 20%
Signup -> Deposit :   500 /  2,000 = 25%
Deposit -> Game   :   400 /    500 = 80%
Overall           :   400 / 10,000 = 4%

Ab segment: Android signup 1,200, deposit 240 (20%). iOS signup 800, deposit 260 (32.5%). Total 2,000 aur 500 match karta hai. Android par deposit step me leak hai, to wahan payment flow check karo.

sql
SELECT platform,
       COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FILTER (WHERE event = 'signup')  AS signups,
       COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FILTER (WHERE event = 'deposit') AS deposits
FROM events GROUP BY platform;

Common mistakes

  • Events count karna, users nahi, to conversion 100% se upar bhi ja sakta hai.
  • Different time windows ke stages mix karna.
  • Sirf overall funnel dekhna. Segment ke bina leak chhup jata hai.
  • Skip karne wale users ko handle nahi karna (kuch users step 2 skip karke step 3 pahunch jaate hain).

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Funnel me sabse bada drop mila, ab kya?
    A. Us step ko segment se todta hoon (device, channel, version), phir session recordings ya error logs dekhta hoon aur fix ka test plan banata hoon.
  • Q. Strict aur loose funnel me farak?
    A. Strict me order follow hona zaroori hai, loose me sirf stage ka event hona. Strict zyada conservative hota hai.

Yaad rakho

Unique users, fixed window, segment split: ye teen cheezein funnel ko sahi banati hain.

AN-05Cohort analysisIntermediateMust Know

Users ko unke joining period se group karo aur dekho ki time ke saath unka retention aur behaviour kaise badalta hai.

Simple me samjho

School ka batch socho. 2020 ka batch aur 2021 ka batch alag track karte hain ki kitne bachche aage tak padhe. Cohort analysis me bhi same age ke users ko compare karte hain, mixed crowd ko nahi.

Key points

  • Acquisition cohort: Users jo same week/month me join hue (signup ya first deposit date).
  • Cohort age: Join ke baad kitne din/week/month hue (M0, M1, M2).
  • Retention table: Rows = cohorts, columns = age, value = active users ka percentage.
  • Retention curve: Age par retention plot. Curve flatten ho jaye to ek loyal core mil gaya.
  • Behaviour over lifetime: Sirf retention nahi, revenue per user, games per user bhi age ke hisaab se dekho.
  • Cohort compare: Naye cohort purane se behtar hai ya nahi, ye product/marketing change ka asar batata hai.
  • Triangle shape: Naye cohorts ke paas kam columns hote hain, ye normal hai.
  • Cohort type: Time-based ke alawa channel ya campaign wise cohorts bhi bante hain.

Example

CohortUsersM0M1M2M3
Jan1,000100%40% (400)30% (300)25% (250)
Feb800100%36% (288)27% (216)-
Mar1,200100%45% (540)--

March cohort ka M1 retention 45% hai, Jan 40% aur Feb 36%. Lagta hai March me kuch (onboarding ya bonus) behtar hua.

sql
SELECT date_trunc('month', u.signup_at) AS cohort,
       (date_trunc('month', e.event_at)::date - date_trunc('month', u.signup_at)::date) / 30 AS age_approx,
       COUNT(DISTINCT e.user_id) AS active_users
FROM users u JOIN events e ON e.user_id = u.id
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2;

Production me month-diff ke liye proper calendar logic use karo, ye sirf rough sketch hai.

Common mistakes

  • Naye incomplete cohort ko purane se compare karna jabki age alag hai.
  • Cohort size chhota ho to percentage noisy hota hai.
  • "Active" ki definition cohorts ke beech badalna.
  • Overall retention average karna, jo cohort-wise changes chhupa deta hai.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Cohort analysis kyun, simple retention kyun nahi?
    A. Simple retention me naye aur purane users mix ho jaate hain. Cohort same-age users compare karta hai, to improvement ya decay clearly dikhta hai.
  • Q. Flat curve ka matlab?
    A. Ek stable loyal base hai jo churn nahi ho raha. Wahi long-term value ka source hota hai.

Yaad rakho

Same-age users compare karo: cohort = join period, column = age.

AN-06Churn analysisIntermediateMust Know

Churn define karo, leading indicators dhoondo aur survival analysis ka basic idea samjho.

Simple me samjho

Churn matlab customer chhod ke chala gaya. Poker me koi "leave" button nahi dabata, bas khelna band kar deta hai. To pehle define karna padta hai ki kitne din inactive = churn.

Key points

  • Churn definition: Business ke hisaab se. Example: 30 din se koi login ya hand nahi = churned. Definition document karo.
  • Churn rate: Lost customers / customers at start. Retention = 1 - churn.
  • Active window: Jisne kabhi ek baar bhi khela wo "active ever" hai, par churn ke liye recent activity dekhte hain.
  • Leading indicators: Churn se pehle ke signals: sessions kam, deposit gap lamba, losing streak, support complaint, withdrawal request.
  • Voluntary vs involuntary: Khud chhodna vs payment fail ya account block.
  • Expected lifetime: Roughly 1 / churn rate.
  • Survival analysis intro: Time-to-event model. Kaun kitne time tak "survive" karta hai. Censoring ka dhyan: jo abhi tak churn nahi hue unka final time unknown hota hai.
  • Kaplan-Meier: Survival curve estimate karne ka basic method. Python me lifelines library ka KaplanMeierFitter.

Example

Mahine ke start me 10,000 active, mahine me 800 churn:

text
Churn = 800 / 10,000 = 8%    Retention = 92%
Expected lifetime = 1 / 0.08 = 12.5 months

Kaplan-Meier chhota example: 100 users at risk. Day 7 par 10 churn: S = 1 - 10/100 = 0.90. Phir 90 bache, day 14 par 9 churn: S = 0.90 x (1 - 9/90) = 0.90 x 0.90 = 0.81.

python
from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter
kmf = KaplanMeierFitter()
kmf.fit(durations=df["days_active"], event_observed=df["churned"])
kmf.plot_survival_function()

Common mistakes

  • Churn ki definition har report me alag use karna.
  • Churn ke baad ka data (leakage) leading indicator me daal dena.
  • Active users ko censoring ke bina "survived 30 days" maan lena.
