  • Sab players ka ek hi churn window lagana jabki casual aur high-roller ka pattern alag hota hai.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Churn define kaise karoge?
    A. Normal inter-visit gap dekhta hoon (e.g. 90th percentile of gap). Usse zyada inactive = churn. Phir business se align karta hoon.
  • Q. Survival analysis kyun?
    A. Kyunki time aur censoring dono handle karta hai. Simple churn rate "kab" churn hua ye nahi batata.

Yaad rakho

Pehle churn ki definition lock karo, phir indicators dhoondo, aur censoring na bhoolo.

AN-07RFM segmentationIntermediateGood to Have

Recency, Frequency, Monetary scores se customers ko segments me baanto aur har segment ke liye alag action lo.

Simple me samjho

Customer ko teen sawaal se parkho: kab aaya last baar? Kitni baar aata hai? Kitna kharch karta hai? Teeno ke score milke batate hain ki ye champion hai ya khone wala.

Key points

  • Recency (R): Last activity ko kitne din hue. Kam din = better score.
  • Frequency (F): Period me kitni baar active ya transaction kiya.
  • Monetary (M): Period me total spend ya deposit ya rake.
  • Scoring: Har metric ko quintiles (1 to 5) me baanto. 5 = best. Recency me ulta: kam din = 5.
  • Combined: Score jaise R5 F5 M5 ya simple segment rules.
  • Common segments: Champions, Loyal, New, At Risk, Cant Lose Them, Hibernating.
  • Actions: Champions ko VIP rewards, At Risk ko win-back offer, New ko onboarding, Hibernating ko low-cost reactivation.
  • Window: Last 90 ya 180 din ka data. Window fix karo.

Example

CustomerR daysFMR,F,M scoreSegmentAction
C124050,0005,5,5ChampionVIP reward
C2803545,0001,5,5Cant losePersonal call, big offer
C3115005,1,1NewWelcome journey
C46052,0002,2,2HibernatingCheap reactivation
sql
SELECT user_id,
  NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY recency_days DESC) AS r,
  NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY frequency)         AS f,
  NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY monetary)          AS m
FROM user_rfm;

Recency me DESC order isliye ki sabse zyada din wale ko 1 aur sabse kam din wale ko 5 mile.

Common mistakes

  • Recency ka direction ulta kar dena.
  • Outliers (whales) ki wajah se quintile cutoffs skew hona; log ya capped values try karo.
  • 125 combinations ko alag segments banana. Chhote, actionable groups banao.
  • Segment banake action ya test nahi karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. RFM ki limitation?
    A. Sirf past behaviour dekhta hai, product ya demographics nahi. Future value predict nahi karta.
  • Q. NTILE me ties ka kya?
    A. NTILE rows ko equal-size buckets me baantta hai, to same value wale users alag bucket me ja sakte hain. Rank ya cutoffs se handle kar sakte ho.

Yaad rakho

R, F, M ko 1 se 5 score do, segments ko naam do, aur har segment ko ek action do.

AN-08Customer segmentationIntermediateGood to Have

Customers ko similar groups me baanto: rule-based ya K-means se, phir segments ko naam do aur use karo.

Simple me samjho

Sab players ko ek hi offer bhejna waise hai jaise sabko ek hi size ki shirt dena. Segmentation se similar players ke group bante hain. Phir har group ko uske hisaab se treat karte hain.

Key points

  • Rule-based: Khud rules likhte ho. Example: deposit > 10,000 = High value. Simple, explainable, par subjective.
  • K-means: Algorithm data se clusters nikalta hai. Features ke basis par similar users group hote hain.
  • Features: Sessions per week, avg deposit, game mix, tenure. Sensible aur numeric rakho.
  • Scaling zaroori: K-means distance use karta hai, to StandardScaler se features same scale par laao.
  • Choosing K: Elbow method (inertia) aur silhouette score. Business sense bhi dekho.
  • Naming segments: Cluster ke averages dekh ke naam do: "Weekend grinders", "High-roller occasional".
  • Using segments: Marketing, bonus, support priority, product ideas. Segment ka koi action nahi to wo bekaar hai.
  • Stability: Segments time ke saath hilte hain. Monthly refresh karo aur migration track karo.

Example

python
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans

X = StandardScaler().fit_transform(df[["sessions_wk", "avg_deposit", "tenure_days"]])
km = KMeans(n_clusters=4, n_init=10, random_state=42).fit(X)
df["segment"] = km.labels_
print(df.groupby("segment")[["sessions_wk", "avg_deposit", "tenure_days"]].mean())

Output me har cluster ka average aata hai. Agar cluster 2 me sessions 14 aur avg_deposit 8,000 hai, to naam "Heavy regulars" de sakte ho.

Rule-based quick version:

sql
SELECT user_id,
  CASE WHEN avg_deposit >= 10000 THEN 'high'
       WHEN avg_deposit >= 2000  THEN 'mid'
       ELSE 'low' END AS value_segment
FROM user_summary;

Common mistakes

  • Scaling bhool jana, to bada-number wala feature clustering par haavi ho jata hai.
  • Bahut zyada clusters banana jo koi samajh na sake.
  • Categorical features seedha K-means me daalna (K-means numeric ke liye hai).
  • Segment bana ke use na karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Rule-based vs K-means kab?
    A. Jab business ko simple explainable groups chahiye to rules. Jab pattern unknown ho aur many features hon to K-means.
  • Q. K kaise choose karte ho?
    A. Elbow aur silhouette dekhta hoon, phir check karta hoon ki clusters interpretable aur actionable hain ya nahi.

Yaad rakho

Segment tabhi achha hai jab wo explainable ho aur uske liye alag action ho.

AN-09Customer lifetime valueIntermediateGood to Have

CLV batata hai ek customer poori life me kitna value dega. Historical ya predictive, aur acquisition spend decide karne me use hota hai.

Simple me samjho

Ek customer laane me paisa lagta hai. CLV batata hai us customer se kul kitna return milega. Agar CLV, CAC se bada hai to acquisition worth hai.

Key points

  • Historical CLV: Ab tak ka actual total revenue ya margin per customer. Simple, par future nahi batata.
  • Predictive CLV: Future value ka estimate. Simple formula ya models (BG/NBD + Gamma-Gamma, Python lifetimes library).
  • Simple formula: CLV = ARPU x margin x (1 / churn).
  • Margin use karo: Revenue nahi, gross margin ya net contribution lo. Poker me bonus cost minus karo.
  • Discount rate: Future paise ki value kam hoti hai. Long horizon me discount lagao.
  • CAC: Customer acquisition cost. LTV:CAC ratio common benchmark 3:1 (rule of thumb, business ke hisaab se badalta hai).
  • Payback period: CAC / monthly margin per customer. Kitne mahine me paisa wapas.
  • Use in acquisition spend: Channel-wise CLV nikalo aur max allowed CAC decide karo.

Example

ARPU 500 per month, margin 40%, monthly churn 8%.

text
Monthly margin = 500 x 0.40 = 200
Lifetime (months) = 1 / 0.08 = 12.5
CLV = 200 x 12.5 = 2,500        (same as 200 / 0.08)

Max CAC at 3:1  = 2,500 / 3 = ~833
If actual CAC = 1,000 -> LTV:CAC = 2.5, payback = 1,000 / 200 = 5 months

Channel jiska CAC 1,000 hai, wo 3:1 target se thoda neeche hai. Ya to CAC kam karo ya CLV badhao.

python
# historical CLV per user (pandas)
clv = df.groupby("user_id")["net_revenue"].sum()

Common mistakes

  • Revenue ko hi CLV maan lena, margin aur bonus cost ignore karna.
  • Ek hi churn rate sab customers par lagana. Segment/channel-wise nikalo.
  • Naye cohorts ka CLV bina data ke over-promise karna.
  • Historical CLV ko future decision ke liye final maan lena.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. CLV acquisition me kaise kaam aata hai?
    A. Har channel ka CLV nikalke max allowed CAC set karte hain. Jis channel me CLV/CAC achha, wahan spend badhate hain.
  • Q. Historical vs predictive CLV?
    A. Historical = kya mila. Predictive = aage kya milega. Naye customers ke liye predictive chahiye kyunki unki history chhoti hai.

Yaad rakho

CLV = margin per period x expected lifetime, aur hamesha CAC se compare karo.

AN-10Pareto and ABC analysisBasicGood to Have

80/20 rule: thode customers ya products se zyada revenue aata hai. ABC me unhe A, B, C classes me baanto.

Simple me samjho

Aksar 20% log 80% kaam ya revenue dete hain. Poker me bhi kuch high-value players rake ka bada hissa dete hain. Ye pata ho to focus sahi jagah lagta hai.

Key points

  • Pareto principle: Roughly 80% outcome 20% inputs se. Exact 80/20 hona zaroori nahi, ratio data se nikalo.
  • Steps: Revenue descending sort karo, cumulative sum nikalo, cumulative % nikalo.
  • ABC classes: A = top contributors (cumulative 0-80%), B = next (80-95%), C = baaki. Cutoffs business ke hisaab se badalte hain.
  • Top customers/products: A class ko retention aur VIP focus milta hai.
  • Long-tail: Bahut saare chhote items/players, har ek ka contribution kam, par total me kaafi ho sakta hai.
  • Risk: Agar 20% customers 80% revenue dete hain to dependency risk hai.
  • Pareto chart: Bars (value) + line (cumulative %).
  • Use: Support priority, inventory, marketing spend, VIP programs.

Example

10 customers ka revenue (total 1,000):

RankRevenueCumulativeCum %Class
140040040%A
220060060%A
312072072%A
48080080%A
56086086%B
65091091%B
74095095%B
82097097%C
92099099%C
10101,000100%C

Top 2 customers (20%) = 60% revenue. Top 4 (40%) = 80%.

sql
SELECT user_id, revenue,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC)
        / SUM(revenue) OVER (), 1) AS cum_pct
FROM user_revenue ORDER BY revenue DESC;

Common mistakes

  • Ek hi period ke data par permanent class de dena. Classes badalti rehti hain.
  • Ties ya same revenue ke rows me cumulative ordering unstable chhod dena. Tie-break column add karo.
  • Long-tail ko ignore karna jabki wo combined me bada ho sakta hai.
  • 80/20 ko law maan lena.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Pareto ka business use?
    A. Focus. Top contributors ko protect karo, aur dekho ki dependency risk to nahi hai.
  • Q. ABC analysis kya hai?
    A. Items ko cumulative contribution ke basis par A (sabse important), B, C me baantna, taaki attention aur resources sahi jagah jaaye.

Yaad rakho

Sort, cumulative %, class: top 20% ka share nikalo, par ratio data se confirm karo.

AN-11Market basket analysisIntermediateBonus

Kaunse items saath kharide jaate hain: support, confidence, lift se association rules nikalo aur cross-sell karo.

Simple me samjho

Kirana dukaan wala jaanta hai ki bread ke saath butter bikta hai. Market basket analysis ye pattern data se nikalta hai. Gaming me: jo players Rummy khelte hain, kya wo Poker bhi khelte hain?

Key points

  • Basket (transaction): Ek order ya ek user-session me items ka set.
  • Association rule: A -> B. Matlab A hone par B hone ka chance.
  • Support: baskets with both / total baskets. Rule kitna common hai.
  • Confidence: baskets with both / baskets with A. A ke baad B kitni baar.
  • Lift: confidence / support(B). Lift > 1 matlab positive association, = 1 independent, < 1 negative.
  • Cross-sell: High lift pairs ko recommendation ya bundle me use karo.
  • Algorithms: Apriori, FP-Growth. Python me mlxtend ke apriori aur association_rules.
  • Thresholds: Min support set karo warna rare pairs ka noise aata hai.

Example

100 baskets: Bread 40, Butter 30, dono 20.

text
Support(Bread,Butter)   = 20 / 100 = 0.20
Confidence(Bread->Butter) = 20 / 40 = 0.50
Lift = 0.50 / 0.30 = 1.67

Lift 1.67 matlab bread wale baskets me butter random se 1.67 guna zyada milta hai.

python
from mlxtend.frequent_patterns import apriori, association_rules
freq = apriori(basket_df, min_support=0.05, use_colnames=True)
rules = association_rules(freq, metric="lift", min_threshold=1.2)

basket_df boolean (one-hot) table hona chahiye: rows = baskets, columns = items.

Common mistakes

  • Sirf confidence dekhna. Popular item B ke saath confidence hamesha high lagta hai, lift check karo.
  • Bahut low support par rules nikalna jo statistically weak hain.
  • Correlation ko causation maan lena.
  • Pair dikhne par bina A/B test ke bundle launch kar dena.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Lift 1 ka matlab?
    A. A aur B independent hain. Association random chance jitni hi hai.
  • Q. Confidence aur lift me farak?
    A. Confidence B ki base popularity ko ignore karta hai. Lift usse normalise karta hai, isliye better measure hai.

Yaad rakho

Support = kitna common, confidence = kitni baar saath, lift = random se kitna zyada.

AN-12Pricing and promotion analysisAdvancedGood to Have

Price ya discount ka demand par asar: elasticity, cannibalisation aur incrementality se pata lagao ki promo se sach me extra kaam hua ya nahi.

Simple me samjho

Discount dene se sales badhti hain, par kya wo sales waise bhi hoti? Aur discount ka kharcha nikla ya nahi? Ye sawaal pricing analysis ka core hain.

Key points

  • Price elasticity: % change in quantity / % change in price. Negative aata hai. Magnitude > 1 = elastic.
  • Elastic vs inelastic: Elastic me price kam karne se revenue badhta hai. Inelastic me price badhane se revenue badhta hai.
  • Discount impact: Volume badha, par per-unit margin gira. Dono ka net dekho.
  • Cannibalisation: Promo se naye orders nahi bane, bas dusre product ya future ke orders khinch aaye (e.g. cash game bonus se tournament entries kam).
  • Pull-forward: Kal ki demand aaj aa gayi, to promo ke baad dip aata hai.
  • Incrementality: Promo ke bina kitna hota (control group) vs promo ke saath. Difference = incremental.
  • Measure: A/B test ya holdout group. Sirf before-after misleading hota hai.
  • Subsidy cost: Un users ko bhi discount mila jo waise bhi kharidte. Ye waste hai.

Example

Price 100 se 90 (-10%). Quantity 1,000 se 1,150 (+15%).

text
Elasticity = +15% / -10% = -1.5  (elastic)
Revenue before = 100 x 1,000 = 100,000
Revenue after  =  90 x 1,150 = 103,500   (+3.5%)

Promo test: 10,000 users promo group conv 5% = 500 orders, 10,000 control conv 4% = 400 orders. Incremental orders = 100. AOV 400 to incremental revenue = 40,000. Agar 500 orders par discount 20 mila to cost = 10,000. Margin ka dhyan rakh ke decide karo ki promo worth thi ya nahi.

Common mistakes

  • Before-after dekh ke promo ko credit dena jabki seasonality bhi thi.
  • Elasticity ko ek product se sab par generalise karna.
  • Cannibalisation aur promo ke baad dip ignore karna.
  • Revenue dekhna, margin aur discount cost nahi.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Promo successful tha ya nahi, kaise batoge?
    A. Control/holdout group se incremental orders ya revenue nikalta hoon, phir discount cost aur margin minus karke net impact dekhta hoon.
  • Q. Elasticity -0.5 ka matlab?
    A. Inelastic. Price 10% badhe to demand sirf ~5% girti hai, to price badhane se revenue badh sakta hai.

Yaad rakho

Promo ka asli asar incremental hota hai, total sales nahi.

AN-13Attribution modelsAdvancedGood to Have

Conversion ka credit kis marketing touchpoint ko mile: first, last, linear, time decay, aur MMM ki awareness.

Simple me samjho

Ek user ne pehle Google ad dekha, phir Facebook, phir email se aake deposit kiya. Credit kisko milega? Attribution model ye rule decide karta hai.

Key points

  • First touch: Poora credit pehle touchpoint ko. Awareness channels ko favour karta hai.
  • Last touch: Poora credit aakhri touchpoint ko. Sabse common aur simple, par conversion se pehle ke channels ignore.
  • Linear: Sab touchpoints ko barabar credit.
  • Time decay: Conversion ke paas wale touchpoints ko zyada credit.
  • Position-based (U-shape): Pehle aur aakhri ko zyada (e.g. 40/20/40), beech ko kam.
  • Data-driven: Platform ya model touchpoint ka actual contribution estimate karta hai.
  • MMM (Marketing Mix Modeling) awareness: Aggregate spend aur outcome par regression. User-level tracking nahi chahiye, privacy-friendly, par granular nahi.
  • Limitation: Attribution correlation hai. Incrementality test se causal impact confirm hota hai.

Example

Journey: Google Ad, Facebook, Email, phir deposit 1,000.

ModelGoogleFacebookEmail
First touch1,00000
Last touch001,000
Linear333.33333.33333.33
Time decay (0.2/0.3/0.5)200300500
Position (40/20/40)400200400

Har row ka total 1,000 hai. Model badalne se channel ROI badal jata hai, isliye model ka naam report me likho.

Common mistakes

  • Last touch ko hi sach maan ke upper-funnel channels ka budget kaat dena.
  • Model change karke trends compare karna.
  • Cross-device ya offline touchpoints ka missing hona.
  • Attribution ko causal proof samajhna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Last touch ki problem?
    A. Wo discovery wale channels ko credit nahi deta. Brand ya awareness campaigns undervalue ho jaate hain.
  • Q. MMM kab?
    A. Jab user-level tracking limited ho (privacy, offline media). Weekly spend aur outcome ka aggregate model banta hai.

Yaad rakho

Koi bhi attribution model perfect nahi: model batao, aur incrementality se verify karo.

AN-14Anomaly detectionIntermediateMust Know

Metrics me unusual spikes ya drops pakadne ke tareeke: thresholds, control charts, z-score aur seasonality-aware alerts.

Simple me samjho

Normal din me 100 signups aate hain. Aaj 85 aaye. Ye kitna unusual hai? Anomaly detection yehi decide karta hai, taaki log-jam ya bug jaldi pakda jaye.

Key points

  • Static threshold: Fixed limit, e.g. signups < 50 to alert. Simple par seasonal metrics me galat alarms.
  • Control chart: Mean aur +/- 3 standard deviations ki limits. Bahar = anomaly.
  • Z-score: (x - mean) / std. |z| > 3 aam taur par anomaly mana jata hai.
  • Seasonality-aware: Sunday ko Sunday se compare karo. Same weekday ya same hour ki history use karo.
  • Rolling baseline: Last 4 to 8 same-weekday values ka mean aur std.
  • Robust options: Median aur MAD, kyunki outliers mean ko bigaadte hain.
  • Alert fatigue: Zyada alerts = log ignore karte hain. Thresholds tune karo.
  • Investigate: Pehle data pipeline problem check karo, phir real business cause.

Example

Pichle 7 same-weekday values: 100, 104, 98, 102, 96, 101, 99.

text
Mean = 700 / 7 = 100
Deviations: 0, 4, -2, 2, -4, 1, -1  -> squares sum = 42
Sample variance = 42 / 6 = 7  -> std = 2.65
Control limits (3 sigma) = 100 +/- 7.94 = [92.06, 107.94]
Today = 85 -> z = (85-100)/2.65 = -5.67  -> anomaly
python
import numpy as np
hist = np.array([100, 104, 98, 102, 96, 101, 99])
z = (85 - hist.mean()) / hist.std(ddof=1)
print(round(z, 2))   # -5.67

Common mistakes

  • Weekend aur weekday ko ek hi baseline se compare karna.
  • Baseline me pichla anomaly rakh dena, jisse std phool jata hai.
  • Pipeline delay ko business drop samajh lena.
  • Bahut kam history par z-score lagana.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Z-score ki limitation?
    A. Normal-ish distribution aur stable baseline maanta hai. Seasonality ya trend ho to same-weekday baseline ya model use karna padta hai.
  • Q. Alert aaya, pehla step?
    A. Data freshness aur pipeline check, phir segment-wise drill (platform, geo), phir cause dhoondna.

Yaad rakho

Anomaly "normal ke seasonal baseline" se door hona hai, kisi fixed number se nahi.

AN-15Business forecastingIntermediateGood to Have

Demand, revenue ya targets ka future estimate banana, scenarios ke saath, aur forecast accuracy track karna.

Simple me samjho

Forecast crystal ball nahi hai. Ye past pattern + assumptions se ek reasonable range deta hai. Planning aur target setting isi par based hoti hai.

Key points

  • Use cases: Demand, revenue, DAU, rake, staffing, budget, targets.
  • Simple methods: Naive (last value), moving average, same-period-last-year x growth. Pehle simple baseline banao.
  • Statistical models: Exponential smoothing, ARIMA (statsmodels), Prophet. Seasonality aur trend handle karte hain.
  • Driver-based: Revenue = users x conversion x AOV ko alag forecast karo, phir multiply.
  • Scenario planning: Base, optimistic, pessimistic forecasts. Assumptions likho.
  • Accuracy metrics: MAPE mean(abs(actual - forecast) / actual), MAE, bias (systematic over ya under).
  • Tracking: Har period forecast vs actual compare karo aur model improve karo.
  • Communicate range: Ek number nahi, range do.

Example

4 hafte ka forecast vs actual:

WeekActualForecastAbs error %
11001055.00%
21101081.82%
31201254.17%
41301207.69%

MAPE = (5.00 + 1.82 + 4.17 + 7.69) / 4 = 18.68 / 4 = 4.67%, yaani roughly 4.7%. Bias: forecast minus actual = +5, -2, +5, -10 = -2. Thoda under-forecast.

python
import pandas as pd
df["fc"] = df["revenue"].rolling(3).mean().shift(1)   # naive 3-period moving average baseline
mape = ((df["revenue"] - df["fc"]).abs() / df["revenue"]).mean()

shift(1) isliye ki forecast me aaj ka actual use na ho (leakage).

Common mistakes

  • Forecast me future data leak hona.
  • Ek hi model ko bina baseline se compare kiye maan lena.
  • Single-number forecast dena, range ke bina.
  • Accuracy track na karna, to model kabhi improve nahi hota.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. MAPE ki problem?
    A. Actual zero ya bahut chhota ho to undefined ya huge ho jata hai, aur over/under ko symmetric treat nahi karta. MAE ya bias bhi dekho.
  • Q. Target set karne me forecast kaise use karoge?
    A. Base forecast + planned initiatives ka impact, scenarios ke saath. Target forecast se thoda upar rakhte hain par realistic.

Yaad rakho

Simple baseline pehle, range me bolo, aur accuracy ko lagatar track karo.

AN-16Impact and causal analysisAdvancedGood to Have

Kisi change (feature, offer) ka asli asar nikalna: pre-post, diff-in-diff, matching aur counterfactual thinking.

Simple me samjho

Feature launch ke baad revenue badha. Kya feature ki wajah se, ya waise bhi badhta? Counterfactual yaani "agar launch nahi hota to kya hota" ka estimate chahiye.

Key points

  • Counterfactual: Wo outcome jo change ke bina hota. Ye kabhi directly dikhta nahi, estimate karna padta hai.
  • Pre-post: Change se pehle vs baad. Simple, par trend, seasonality, aur dusre changes ka asar mix ho jata hai.
  • Difference-in-differences (DiD): Treated group ka change minus control group ka change. Common time effects hat jaate hain.
  • Parallel trends assumption: Change ke bina dono groups ke trends similar chalte. Pre-period me check karo.
  • Matching: Treated users jaise hi control users dhoondo (propensity score ya same features par) taaki fair compare ho.
  • Randomised experiment: Gold standard. Possible na ho to quasi-experimental methods.
  • Confounders: Wo cheezein jo treatment aur outcome dono ko affect karti hain.
  • Time-based checks: Placebo test, pre-trend plot.

Example

Region A (feature mila): revenue 100 se 130. Region B (feature nahi): 100 se 110.

text
Pre-post (A only) = +30  (overstated)
Control change    = +10  (common trend)
DiD = (130 - 100) - (110 - 100) = 30 - 10 = +20

Feature ka estimated impact +20, na ki +30.

python
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
m = smf.ols("revenue ~ treated + post + treated:post", data=df).fit()
print(m.params["treated:post"])   # DiD estimate

treated:post ka coefficient hi DiD effect hai.

Common mistakes

  • Pre-post ko causal proof maan lena.
  • Control group ka chunav aise karna jiska trend alag ho.
  • Same time par chal rahe dusre campaigns ko ignore karna.
  • Chhote sample par confident conclusion dena.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. DiD kab use karoge?
    A. Jab randomised test possible na ho, par ek comparable control group ho aur dono ka pre-period trend similar ho.
  • Q. Correlation vs causation?
    A. Correlation me saath move hona hota hai. Causation ke liye counterfactual chahiye, jaise experiment ya DiD.

Yaad rakho

Impact = actual minus counterfactual: control group ke bina pre-post par bharosa mat karo.

AN-17Scenario and sensitivity analysisIntermediateGood to Have

Best, base, worst case banao aur dekho kaunsa assumption answer ko sabse zyada hilata hai.

Simple me samjho

Future unknown hai, isliye ek nahi, kuch scenarios banate hain. Phir ek ek input ko hilake dekhte hain kaun sa input sabse bada asar daalta hai. Isse risk aur focus dono samajh aate hain.

Key points

  • Base case: Sabse likely assumptions.
  • Best / worst case: Optimistic aur pessimistic assumptions. Realistic range me rakho, impossible nahi.
  • Scenario: Kai inputs ek saath badalte hain (coherent story).
  • Sensitivity: Ek input badlo (ceteris paribus), baaki fixed. Output ka change dekho.
  • Tornado chart: Inputs ko output impact ke order me bars se dikhana.
  • What moves the answer most: Wahi inputs par research aur monitoring karo.
  • Break-even: Input ki wo value jahan result zero ya target par aata hai.
  • Document assumptions: Har input ka source likho.

Example

Model: Profit = orders x (AOV x margin) - fixed cost. Base: 5,000 orders, AOV 400, margin 25%, fixed cost 350,000.

text
Base profit = 5,000 x (400 x 0.25) - 350,000 = 500,000 - 350,000 = 150,000

Sensitivity (+10% each, others fixed):
Orders 5,500  -> 550,000 - 350,000 = 200,000  (+50,000)
AOV 440       -> 550,000 - 350,000 = 200,000  (+50,000)
Margin 27.5%  -> 550,000 - 350,000 = 200,000  (+50,000)
Fixed -10%    -> 500,000 - 315,000 = 185,000  (+35,000)

Orders, AOV, margin ka asar barabar, kyunki ye multiplicative hain. Fixed cost ka asar kam hai.

Scenario: Worst orders -10% = 4,500 x 100 - 350,000 = 100,000. Best +10% = 200,000. Range 100,000 se 200,000.

Common mistakes

  • Sirf ek case dikhana.
  • Sab inputs ko ek saath worst karna, jo unlikely hai.
  • Inputs ke beech correlation ignore karna (orders badhe to AOV girta hai).
  • Assumptions document na karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Scenario aur sensitivity me farak?
    A. Scenario me kai inputs ek saath badalte hain. Sensitivity me ek input badalte hain aur output ka response dekhte hain.
  • Q. Tornado chart kya batata hai?
    A. Kaunse inputs output ko sabse zyada move karte hain, bars ke order se dikhta hai.

Yaad rakho

Range do aur sabse sensitive input pehchano: wahin focus karo.

AN-18Benchmarking and target settingIntermediateGood to Have

Apne numbers ko internal aur external benchmarks se compare karo aur realistic, driver-based targets set karo.

Simple me samjho

"D30 retention 12%" achha hai ya bura, ye benchmark se pata chalta hai. Aur target ya to hawa me nahi hota, wo drivers se nikalna chahiye.

Key points

  • Internal benchmark: Pichla saal, best region, best cohort, top team. Apni capability dikhata hai.
  • External benchmark: Industry reports, competitors ke public numbers. Definitions alag ho sakti hain, to dhyan se.
  • Like-for-like: Metric definition, period, audience same hona chahiye.
  • Baseline pehle: Current performance aur trend samjho.
  • Driver-based target: Target ko drivers me todo (users, conversion, AOV) aur har driver ka realistic improvement lo.
  • Stretch vs commit: Commit = lagbhag pakka. Stretch = ambitious.
  • SMART: Specific, measurable, time-bound targets.
  • Track: Regular check-in, aur assumptions badle to target revisit.

Example

D30 retention 12%. Industry reference 15% (assumed). Best internal cohort 14%.

text
Plan target    : 13%   (half the gap to best internal)
Stretch target : 14%   (best internal)

Revenue +20% target ko drivers me todo: users +8%, conversion +5%, AOV +5%.

text
1.08 x 1.05 x 1.05 = 1.1907  ->  +19.07%

Target roughly 20% ke paas pahunchta hai. Agar kisi driver ka improvement unrealistic lage to target adjust karo.

Common mistakes

  • Alag definition wale external benchmark se compare karna.
  • Sirf top-down target dena, bina drivers ke.
  • Best-ever number ko hi target bana dena.
  • Target set karke assumptions track na karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Realistic target kaise set karoge?
    A. Baseline aur trend dekhta hoon, internal best aur external benchmark se range banata hoon, phir drivers par bottom-up check karta hoon.
  • Q. External benchmark kyun risky?
    A. Definitions, audience aur market alag hote hain, isliye direct compare galat ho sakta hai.

Yaad rakho

Benchmark do-teen jagah se lo, target drivers se verify karo.

AN-19Market sizing and estimationIntermediateGood to Have

Fermi estimates aur TAM / SAM / SOM se market ka size nikalo, aur assumptions ko sanity-check karo.

Simple me samjho

Exact data na ho to bhi andaaza lagana aata hai: bade sawaal ko chhote sawalon me todo, har ek ka reasonable guess lo, phir multiply karo. Isse "order of magnitude" mil jata hai.

Key points

  • Fermi estimate: Sawaal ko chhote factors me todke rough answer. Exactness nahi, logic aur range important hai.
  • TAM: Total Addressable Market. Pura demand agar 100% share ho.
  • SAM: Serviceable Available Market. TAM ka wo hissa jo aapka product aur geography actually serve kar sakta hai.
  • SOM: Serviceable Obtainable Market. SAM me se realistic share jo aap pa sakte ho.
  • Top-down: Bade market se filter karte hue neeche.
  • Bottom-up: Unit economics se upar: customers x price. Aksar zyada credible.
  • Sanity check: Do alag methods se cross-check, aur real numbers (current users, competitors) se compare.
  • Assumptions list: Har assumption likho aur uska source ya reasoning do.

Example

Online card-game app (saare numbers assumed, real data se validate karo):

text
Smartphone users           : 500M
Interested in card games 10%: 50M      -> TAM users
Eligible age and region 60% : 30M      -> SAM users
Share in 3 yrs 2%           : 600,000  -> SOM users
ARPU per year               : 1,200

TAM value = 50M x 1,200  = 60,000M  (6,000 crore)
SAM value = 30M x 1,200  = 36,000M  (3,600 crore)
SOM value = 600,000 x 1,200 = 720M  (72 crore)

Sanity check: kya 600,000 paying users realistic hain, current user base aur marketing budget ko dekhte hue?

Common mistakes

  • TAM ko hi revenue forecast bana dena.
  • Share ko bina reasoning ke "1% le lenge" bolna.
  • Sirf top-down karna aur bottom-up se cross-check na karna.
  • Units mix karna (million, crore, lakh).

Interview Q&A

  • Q. TAM, SAM, SOM me farak?
    A. TAM total demand, SAM jo hum serve kar sakte hain, SOM jo realistically capture kar sakte hain.
  • Q. Estimate galat na ho, kaise ensure karoge?
    A. Assumptions explicit rakhta hoon, do methods se cross-check karta hoon, aur range deta hoon.

Yaad rakho

Bade sawaal ko todo, assumptions likho, aur do tareeke se sanity-check karo.

A/B Testing 10 topics

AB-01Experiment designIntermediateMust Know

A/B test shuru karne se pehle hypothesis, groups, randomisation unit aur metrics clear karna. Galat design se baad me sahi analysis bhi bekaar ho jata hai.

Simple me samjho

A/B test ek fair race jaisa hai. Do groups ko random banate hain, ek ko naya feature dete hain, doosre ko purana. Race se pehle rules fix hote hain: kaun jeetega ka matlab kya hai, kitne log, kitne din. Race ke baad rules badalna cheating hai.

Key points

  • Hypothesis: Clear statement: "Quick Rebuy button dikhane se rebuy rate badhega." Isme change, metric aur direction hona chahiye.
  • Null vs alternative: H0 = koi farak nahi. H1 = farak hai. Test H0 ko reject karne ki koshish karta hai.
  • Control: Jo users current experience dekhte hain. Ye baseline hai.
  • Treatment: Jo users naya variant dekhte hain. Ek test me ek hi major change rakho, warna pata nahi chalega kis cheez se farak aaya.
  • Randomisation unit: Kis level pe random assign karna hai: user, session, device ya table/club. Analysis unit bhi wahi rakho.
  • Primary metric: Ek hi main metric, jisse decision hoga (e.g. rebuy rate per user). Pehle se likh do.
  • Secondary metrics: Samajhne ke liye, decision ke liye nahi.
  • Guardrail metrics: Jo bigadne nahi chahiye: rake revenue per user, crash rate, session length, support tickets. Primary jeete par guardrail toot jaye to ship nahi karte.
  • Eligibility / trigger: Sirf un users ko count karo jinhone actually feature dekha ya jo eligible hain. Warna signal pani me ghul jata hai.

Example

Poker app: "Quick Rebuy" button.

ItemChoice
HypothesisButton se rebuy rate 10% se 11% hoga
Unituser_id (stable, har session me same variant)
Primaryusers with rebuy / eligible users
Guardrailsrake per user, app crash rate, tickets per 1k users
Split50/50, 3 weeks

Unit user_id isliye, kyunki session level pe ek hi player dono variants dekh lega aur confuse hoga.

Common mistakes

  • Metric baad me choose karna (jo significant dikhe wahi primary bana dena).
  • Ek saath bahut saare changes test karna.
  • Randomisation unit aur analysis unit alag rakhna (session pe randomise, user pe analyse).
  • Guardrail metrics bhool jana, sirf upside dekhna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Randomisation unit kaise choose karte ho?
    A. Wo unit jo experience ko consistent rakhe aur interference kam kare. Usually user_id; agar users ek doosre ko affect karte hain (same table), to table/club level cluster.
  • Q. Guardrail metric kya hota hai?
    A. Ye wo metric hai jo test se kharab nahi hona chahiye (revenue, latency, crashes). Primary improve ho aur guardrail bigde to bhi launch rok sakte hain.

Yaad rakho

Test se pehle likho: hypothesis, unit, primary metric, guardrails, duration. Baad me kuch nahi badalna.

AB-02Sample size and powerIntermediateMust Know

Test chalane se pehle batao kitne users chahiye: baseline rate, MDE, alpha aur power se sample size aur duration nikalte hain.

Simple me samjho

Chhota sample = noisy result. Sikka 10 baar uchhal ke 6 heads aaye to coin biased nahi kehte. Sample size batata hai ki chhota sa asli farak pakadne ke liye kitne users chahiye.

Key points

  • Baseline rate: Control ka current conversion, jaise 10%. Past data se nikalo.
  • MDE (Minimum Detectable Effect): Sabse chhota farak jo business ke liye matter kare, jaise 10% se 11% (+1pp, relative +10%).
  • Alpha: False positive ka risk. Usually 0.05 (two-sided).
  • Power: Asli farak hone par use pakadne ki probability. Usually 0.8 (80%). Beta = 1 - power = false negative risk.
  • Formula (two proportions, per group): n = (z_alpha/2 + z_power)^2 * (p1(1-p1) + p2(1-p2)) / (p2-p1)^2.
  • Z values: alpha 0.05 two-sided -> 1.96; power 0.8 -> 0.84.
  • MDE chhota = sample bahut bada: Effect aadha karo to sample lagbhag 4x.
  • Test duration: n_total / daily_eligible_users, phir full weeks me round up.
  • Variance: Metric jitna noisy, utna bada sample. Revenue jaise metrics ko conversion se zyada sample chahiye.

Example

python
from statsmodels.stats.power import NormalIndPower
from statsmodels.stats.proportion import proportion_effectsize

es = proportion_effectsize(0.11, 0.10)   # Cohen's h
n = NormalIndPower().solve_power(effect_size=es, alpha=0.05,
                                 power=0.8, ratio=1, alternative='two-sided')
print(round(n))   # about 14,744 per group

Formula se: (1.96+0.84)^2 = 7.84; (0.09 + 0.0979) = 0.1879; 7.84 * 0.1879 / 0.0001 = about 14,731. Dono lagbhag 14,750 per group, matlab ~29,500 total. Agar daily 2,000 eligible users aate hain: 29,500 / 2,000 = 14.75 din. Do hafte (14 din) thoda kam, isliye 3 full weeks plan karo. 10% se 10.5% detect karna ho to ~57,760 per group chahiye.

Common mistakes

  • MDE bahut chhota rakhna aur phir kehna "test 2 din me khatam".
  • Baseline rate guess karna, data se na nikalna.
  • Sirf total traffic dekhna, eligible traffic nahi.
  • Underpowered test chala ke "no effect" bol dena. Ye sabit nahi karta ki effect nahi hai.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Power 80% ka matlab?
    A. Agar asli effect MDE jitna hai, to 100 me se 80 baar test use significant dikhayega.
  • Q. Sample size kaise badhta hai?
    A. MDE kam, power zyada, alpha kam ya variance zyada hone par.

Yaad rakho

Sample size = baseline + MDE + alpha + power. Pehle nikalo, phir duration full weeks me round up karo.

AB-03Randomisation and SRM checksAdvancedGood to Have

Randomisation sahi hai ya nahi, ye SRM (sample ratio mismatch) check se pata chalta hai. SRM aaye to result pe bharosa mat karo.

Simple me samjho

50/50 split rakha, par 51.5/48.5 aaya? Ye chance nahi, shayad bug hai. SRM ek smoke alarm hai: jab bajta hai, pehle aag dhundo, phir results padho.

Key points

  • SRM: Observed group sizes expected ratio se statistically alag hon (chi-square test, jaise 50/50 expected).
  • Threshold: Many teams strict p-value use karte hain (e.g. p < 0.001), kyunki ye har test pe chalta hai.
  • Assignment bugs: Hash/salt galat, cache, ya variant assign hone ke baad filter lagna.
  • Logging loss: Treatment me crash/slow load se events log nahi hue, to users kam dikhte hain.
  • Bot / filter asymmetry: Bot ya internal users ko ek arm me zyada hataya.
  • Redirects / triggers: Treatment redirect karta hai, to kuch users page tak pahunchte hi nahi.
  • User vs session level: Session level pe ek user dono variants dekh sakta hai. Samples independent nahi rehte. User_id hash se stable assignment better hai.
  • Stable assignment: bucket = hash(user_id + experiment_salt) % 100. Har experiment ka alag salt, warna groups correlated rahenge.
  • Action: SRM aaye to results ignore karo, root cause fix karo, test dobara chalao.

Example

20,000 users, expected 10,000 / 10,000. Observed 10,300 / 9,700.

python
from scipy.stats import chisquare

stat, p = chisquare([10300, 9700], f_exp=[10000, 10000])
print(stat, p)   # 18.0, p about 0.00002

Chi-square = 300^2/10000 + 300^2/10000 = 9 + 9 = 18. P-value bahut chhota, to SRM hai. Conversion lift analyse karne se pehle cause dhundo.

Common mistakes

  • SRM check skip karke seedha lift dekhna.
  • "Sirf 1.5% ka farak hai" bolke ignore karna. Bade sample me ye bahut significant hota hai.
  • Salt reuse karna, jisse purane experiments ka bias aa jata hai.
  • Session level pe randomise karke user level pe analyse karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. SRM kya hai aur kaise check karte ho?
    A. Observed split expected se chi-square test se compare karte hain. Chhota p-value matlab assignment ya logging me bug.
  • Q. SRM ho to kya karoge?
    A. Result use nahi karunga. Root cause (bug, filters, logging) dhundunga, fix karke test dobara chalaunga.

Yaad rakho

Har A/B readout ka pehla step SRM check. SRM = result invalid.

AB-04Running a test properlyIntermediateMust Know

Test ko sahi tarah chalane ke rules: full weekly cycles, novelty effect ka dhyan, peeking nahi, aur pehle se fixed stopping rule.

Simple me samjho

Cricket match ke beech me score dekh ke winner declare nahi karte. Pura match khelte hain. A/B test bhi planned time tak chalta hai, chahe beech me kuch bhi dikhe.

Key points

  • Full weekly cycles: Poker me weekday aur weekend ka behaviour alag hota hai. Test ko 7 ke multiple din chalao (1, 2, 3 weeks).
  • Novelty effect: Naya feature pehle din excitement se zyada use hota hai, phir effect gir jata hai.
  • Primacy / change aversion: Kabhi purane users naye UI se pehle confuse hote hain, effect baad me aata hai.
  • Check: Daily lift ka trend dekho. Agar lift dheere dheere gir raha hai to novelty ho sakti hai. New vs returning users alag dekho.
  • No peeking: Baar baar p-value dekh ke jaise hi < 0.05 aaye stop karna false positive rate bahut badha deta hai.
  • Stopping rule: Pehle se fix: sample size ya duration. Us tak chalao.
  • Sequential testing: Agar early stop chahiye to sequential methods (alpha spending, always-valid p-values) design time pe choose karo.
  • Monitoring allowed: SRM, crashes, guardrails roz dekh sakte ho. Ye peeking nahi, safety hai.
  • Mid-test changes: Traffic split ya variant badalna test invalid kar deta hai.

Example

Plan: 14,750 per arm, 3 weeks. Din 4 pe p = 0.03 dikha.

text
Day 4  : p = 0.03  -> do NOT stop
Day 10 : p = 0.12  -> do NOT worry
Day 21 : planned end -> analyse once

Early p-value noise hota hai. Agar aap har din dekh ke 0.05 pe stop karoge, to actual false positive rate 5% se kaafi upar chala jata hai.

Common mistakes

  • 2 din me significant dikha to ship kar dena.
  • Test ko weekend pe start/stop karna, jisse ek weekend zyada ya kam aa jaye.
  • Duration badhaate rehna jab tak significance na mile.
  • Test ke dauran treatment me bug fix push karke test chalate rehna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Peeking problem kya hai?
    A. Multiple baar check karne se kahin na kahin p < 0.05 aa hi jata hai, to false positives badhte hain. Fixed horizon ya sequential method use karo.
  • Q. Novelty effect kaise pehchante ho?
    A. Daily lift trend decay hota hai, ya new vs returning users me farak dikhta hai. Test lamba chalao.

Yaad rakho

Plan karo, full weeks chalao, beech me mat dekho, end pe ek baar analyse karo.

AB-05Analysing resultsIntermediateMust Know

Result analyse karne ke steps: lift, p-value, confidence interval, segments aur practical significance. Statistical aur business significance dono check karo.

Simple me samjho

P-value batata hai farak chance se aaya ya nahi. Confidence interval batata hai farak kitna ho sakta hai. Aur business batata hai ki farak itna bada hai ki ship karna worth hai ya nahi.

Key points

  • Absolute lift: Treatment rate - control rate = 11% - 10% = +1.0 percentage point.
  • Relative lift: 1.0 / 10 = +10%. Hamesha batao kaunsa lift hai.
  • P-value: Agar asli me koi farak nahi hota, to itna ya usse bada farak dekhne ki probability. Ye "effect hone ki probability" nahi hai.
  • Significance: p < alpha (0.05) to H0 reject.
  • Confidence interval (CI): Effect ki plausible range. 95% CI me 0 na ho to p < 0.05 hota hai.
  • Segment cuts: Device, country, new vs returning. Pehle se planned segments hi trust karo. Zyada cuts = false positives.
  • Practical significance: Effect itna bada ho ki cost, risk aur effort justify kare.
  • Guardrails check: Primary jeet gaya, par rake per user ya crashes bigde to nahi?
  • SRM first: Pehle SRM clear karo, phir analyse.

Example

Control 1,500 / 15,000 (10%), treatment 1,650 / 15,000 (11%).

python
import numpy as np
from statsmodels.stats.proportion import proportions_ztest

conv = np.array([1650, 1500]); n = np.array([15000, 15000])
z, p = proportions_ztest(conv, n)            # z about 2.83, p about 0.0047
rate = conv / n
diff = rate[0] - rate[1]                      # 0.01
se = np.sqrt((rate * (1 - rate) / n).sum())   # about 0.00354
print(diff - 1.96 * se, diff + 1.96 * se)     # about 0.0031 to 0.0169

Lift +1.0pp (relative +10%), p = 0.0047, 95% CI = [+0.31pp, +1.69pp]. CI 0 se door hai, to significant. Ab pucho: kam se kam +0.31pp bhi worth hai?

Common mistakes

  • Sirf p-value batana, effect size aur CI nahi.
  • "p = 0.06 means no effect" bolna. Bas itna ki evidence kam hai.
  • Bahut saare segments dekh ke ek significant chun lena.
  • Statistically significant par business me bekaar tiny effect ship karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. P-value ka sahi matlab?
    A. H0 true ho to observed ya usse extreme result aane ki probability. Ye H1 true hone ki probability nahi hai.
  • Q. Significant par tiny lift ho to?
    A. Practical significance dekho: revenue impact, cost, risk. Large sample me tiny effect bhi significant ho jata hai.

Yaad rakho

Lift + CI + p-value + guardrails + practical impact. Sirf p-value kabhi nahi.

AB-06Common A/B mistakesIntermediateMust Know

A/B testing me aam galtiyan: peeking, bahut saare metrics, chhota sample, interference aur Simpson's paradox.

Simple me samjho

Ek lottery ticket kharidoge to jeetna mushkil, 20 kharidoge to kuch milne ka chance badh jata hai. Metrics ka bhi yahi haal hai: jitne dekhoge, utna koi na koi "jeet" dikhega.

Key points

  • Peeking: Baar baar check karke jaldi stop karna. False positives badhte hain.
  • Many metrics: 20 metrics par alpha 0.05 ho to kam se kam ek false positive ki chance = 1 - 0.95^20 = 64%. 5 metrics par 22.6%.
  • Fix: Ek primary metric, baaki secondary. Multiple comparisons ke liye correction (AB-07).
  • Small sample: Underpowered test noisy effect dikhata hai ("winner's curse": jo significant dikhe, usse effect bada dikhta hai).
  • Interference / spillover: Poker me same table ke players ek doosre ko affect karte hain. Treatment ka asar control tak pahunch sakta hai. Table/club level pe cluster randomise karo.
  • Simpson's paradox: Overall trend aur segment-wise trend ulte ho sakte hain, jab group sizes imbalance hon.
  • SRM ignore karna: Assignment bug se Simpson jaisi problems aati hain.
  • HARKing: Result dekh ke hypothesis likhna.
  • Multiple tests, same users: Overlapping experiments ek doosre ko contaminate karte hain.

Example

Simpson's paradox (imbalanced split):

DeviceControlTreatment
Desktop90 / 900 = 10%11 / 100 = 11%
Mobile2 / 100 = 2%27 / 900 = 3%
Overall92 / 1000 = 9.2%38 / 1000 = 3.8%

Treatment har device pe jeet raha hai, par overall haar raha hai, kyunki treatment me mobile users zyada the (low conversion). Root cause: device mix barabar nahi. Ye randomisation bug hai.

Common mistakes

  • Desktop/mobile mix check kiye bina overall number pe bharosa karna.
  • 15 metrics dekhna aur ek significant metric ko jeet bol dena.
  • Table-level interaction wale feature ko user level pe randomise karna.
  • Chhote test ka bada effect dekh ke excited ho jana.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Simpson's paradox kya hai?
    A. Aggregate me trend ek taraf aur har sub-group me ulta. Reason hota hai groups ka alag mix/size. Segment mix check karo.
  • Q. Interference kya hai?
    A. Jab ek user ka treatment doosre user ke outcome ko affect kare. Tab cluster randomisation chahiye.

Yaad rakho

Ek primary metric, fixed plan, balanced groups, aur interference socho. Warna "winner" sirf noise hota hai.

AB-07Multi-variant and banditsAdvancedBonus

Do se zyada variants (A/B/n) me multiple comparison correction chahiye. Bandits traffic ko dheere dheere better variant ki taraf bhejte hain.

Simple me samjho

Zyada variants = zyada comparisons = zyada false positive ka chance. Bandit ek smart waiter jaisa hai: jo dish zyada bikti hai, uski taraf zyada dhyan, par naye dishes ko bhi chance.

Key points

  • A/B/n: Ek control, kai treatments (A vs B vs C vs D). Traffic split hota hai, to sample size badhta hai.
  • Multiple comparison problem: 3 treatments vs control = 3 tests. Alpha ko control karna padta hai.
  • Bonferroni: alpha / m. 3 comparisons: 0.05 / 3 = 0.0167. Simple par conservative.
  • Holm: Bonferroni se thoda powerful, sorted p-values pe step-down.
  • Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR): False discovery rate control. Jab bahut tests hon aur kuch false positives chalega.
  • Multi-armed bandit: Explore (naye variants try karo) aur exploit (jo achha hai use zyada dikhao) ka balance.
  • Epsilon-greedy: epsilon probability se random variant, baaki best variant.
  • Thompson sampling: Har variant ke posterior se sample, jiska sample bada, use dikhao. Beta-Bernoulli ke liye simple.
  • Bandit kab: Short-lived decisions (banner, promo, email subject). Kam regret chahiye.
  • Bandit kab nahi: Clean causal inference ya long-term metrics chahiye to fixed A/B better.

Example

Teen treatments ke p-values: 0.012, 0.030, 0.20.

python
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests

p = [0.012, 0.030, 0.20]
for m in ["bonferroni", "holm", "fdr_bh"]:
    reject, p_adj, _, _ = multipletests(p, alpha=0.05, method=m)
    print(m, reject, p_adj.round(3))
# bonferroni [ True False False] [0.036 0.09  0.6  ]
# holm       [ True False False] [0.036 0.06  0.2  ]
# fdr_bh     [ True  True False] [0.036 0.045 0.2  ]

Bonferroni aur Holm sirf pehla variant significant maante hain. BH (FDR) do variants, kyunki FDR kam strict hai.

Common mistakes

  • Bahut saare variants chalana jabki traffic kam hai.
  • Correction ke bina "best of 4" ko winner bolna.
  • Bandit se result ka p-value nikalna jaise fixed A/B ho.
  • Bandit ko long-term retention measure karne ke liye use karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Bonferroni vs BH?
    A. Bonferroni family-wise error control karta hai (strict). BH false discovery rate control karta hai (zyada power).
  • Q. A/B test vs bandit?
    A. A/B inference aur clean learning ke liye. Bandit kam regret aur short-term optimisation ke liye.

Yaad rakho

Zyada variants = alpha correction. Bandit earn karta hai, A/B seekhta hai.

AB-08Bayesian A/B testingAdvancedBonus

Bayesian approach me hum seedha batate hain "B ke best hone ki probability" aur "galat choose karne ka expected loss".

Simple me samjho

Frequentist bolta hai "H0 true ho to data kitna surprising". Bayesian bolta hai "data dekh ke B better hone ki kitni probability". Business ko ye second wala sawal zyada natural lagta hai.

Key points

  • Prior: Test se pehle ka belief. Conversion ke liye commonly Beta(1, 1) (flat).
  • Posterior: Data ke baad ka belief. Beta prior + binomial data = Beta(1 + conversions, 1 + non-conversions).
  • Probability of being best: P(B > A) posterior samples se nikalo.
  • Expected loss: Agar B choose karein aur A actually better ho, to average kitna nuksan: E[max(A - B, 0)].
  • Decision rule: Jaise "P(B best) > 95% aur expected loss < threshold (e.g. 0.05pp)". Threshold business decide karta hai.
  • Credible interval: Parameter ki range, jo probability statement deta hai (frequentist CI se alag interpretation).
  • Peeking: Bayesian me bhi bina rule ke bar bar dekhna risky hai; stopping rule/loss threshold fix rakho.
  • Prior ka effect: Bade sample me prior ka asar kam. Chhote sample me strong prior sambhal ke use karo.

Example

Control 1,500/15,000, treatment 1,650/15,000, prior Beta(1,1).

python
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
a = rng.beta(1 + 1500, 1 + 15000 - 1500, 200_000)   # control
b = rng.beta(1 + 1650, 1 + 15000 - 1650, 200_000)   # treatment
print((b > a).mean())                  # about 0.998
print(np.maximum(a - b, 0).mean())     # about 0.0000025

P(B best) lagbhag 99.8%. Expected loss lagbhag 0.0000025, yani 0.00025 percentage point. B ship karne ka risk bahut chhota hai.

Common mistakes

  • Posterior probability ko "guaranteed win" samajhna.
  • Prior ko justify kiye bina strong rakhna.
  • Sirf P(B best) dekhna, effect size aur loss nahi.
  • Bayesian bol ke stopping rule na rakhna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Probability of being best kya hai?
    A. Posterior ke andar kitne samples me B ka rate A se zyada hai. Wo fraction hi probability hai.
  • Q. Expected loss kyun?
    A. Ye batata hai ki galat variant choose karne par average nuksan kitna. Probability ke saath cost ka idea deta hai.

Yaad rakho

Bayesian = P(B best) + expected loss. Dono dekho, sirf probability nahi.

AB-09Experiment readout documentIntermediateMust Know

Test khatam hone ke baad ka document: recommendation, risks, next steps aur kya seekha. Stakeholder ko decision lene layak banao.

Simple me samjho

Readout ek exam result jaisa hai, par saath me advice bhi: "ship karo ya nahi, kyun, aur aage kya". Pehle line me answer, baaki details baad me.

Key points

  • Recommendation first: Top pe likho: Ship / Do not ship / Iterate. Ek line me reason.
  • Context: Hypothesis, variants, dates, traffic split, population.
  • Results table: Primary metric: control, treatment, absolute + relative lift, 95% CI, p-value.
  • Guardrails: Rake, crashes, tickets: koi bigda ya nahi.
  • Data quality: SRM check, logging issues, exclusions.
  • Risks: Novelty, segment ka kam sample, long-term effect unknown, seasonality.
  • Next steps: Rollout plan (10% -> 50% -> 100%), follow-up test, monitoring.
  • What we learned: Neutral/negative result bhi learning hai. Isse next hypothesis nikalti hai.
  • Plain language: Jargon kam, chart/table zyada. Decision maker ko 2 minute me samajh aana chahiye.

Example

Mini readout (Quick Rebuy):

SectionContent
RecommendationShip to 100%, monitor rake for 2 weeks
ResultRebuy rate 10.0% -> 11.0% (+1.0pp, +10%), CI [+0.31, +1.69]pp, p = 0.005
GuardrailsRake per user flat, crash rate unchanged
RisksNovelty effect possible; weekend traffic thoda kam tha
NextTest button position; check 4-week retention
LearnedMobile users pe effect bada, desktop pe chhota (exploratory)

Common mistakes

  • Pehle 5 pages methodology, recommendation end me.
  • Sirf winning metrics dikhana, guardrails chhupana.
  • Exploratory segment finding ko confirmed bol dena.
  • Failed test ka readout na likhna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Result flat aaya to kya karoge?
    A. Bhi readout likhunga: CI se max possible effect, power, learning, aur next hypothesis. Flat result bhi decision hai.
  • Q. Stakeholder aur significance ki bhasha?
    A. "Lift +10% hai, hum 95% sure hain ki farak +3% se +17% ke beech hai" jaisi simple bhasha.

Yaad rakho

Recommendation pehle, evidence baad me, risks aur next steps saaf.

AB-10Variance reduction (CUPED)AdvancedBonus

CUPED pre-experiment data se metric ka noise kam karta hai, to chhote sample ya kam time me significance mil jata hai.

Simple me samjho

Kuch players waise hi zyada kharch karte hain. Ye farak test ka effect nahi, purani aadat hai. CUPED us purani aadat ko hata deta hai, to sirf test ka asar bachta hai.

Key points

  • Idea: Pre-experiment metric X (jaise pichhle 28 din ka rake) outcome Y se correlated hota hai. Uska predictable hissa hata do.
  • Formula: Y_adj = Y - theta * (X - mean(X)), jahan theta = cov(X, Y) / var(X).
  • Mean unbiased: Treatment effect ka estimate same rehta hai, sirf variance kam hota hai.
  • Variance reduction: Var(Y_adj) = Var(Y) * (1 - rho^2), rho = corr(X, Y).
  • Example gain: rho = 0.7 to variance 51% bachta hai (49% kam), sample lagbhag aadha.
  • X pre-treatment hi ho: Test shuru hone se pehle ka data. Treatment se affected X use mat karo.
  • Best for: Revenue, sessions, bets jaise continuous aur persistent metrics.
  • Limitation: New users jinke paas history nahi, unpe kam kaam karta hai.
  • Same theta dono arms me: Combined data se nikalo, arms alag nahi.

Example

python
import numpy as np

# y = in-test rake per user, x = rake in 28 days before test
theta = np.cov(x, y, ddof=1)[0, 1] / np.var(x, ddof=1)
y_cuped = y - theta * (x - x.mean())

print(np.var(y_cuped, ddof=1) / np.var(y, ddof=1))   # about 1 - rho^2

Agar rho = 0.7 hai to ratio lagbhag 0.51 aayega. 14,750 per arm ki jagah lagbhag 7,500 se kaam chal sakta hai (14,748 * 0.51 = 7,521). Phir y_cuped pe normal t-test chalao.

Common mistakes

  • X me test ke baad ka data use karna (leakage).
  • Alag alag arms ke liye alag theta lena.
  • Kam correlation (rho < 0.2) me expect karna ki bada fayda milega.
  • Metric definition aur pre-period window pehle se fix na karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. CUPED kaise kaam karta hai?
    A. Pre-experiment covariate se outcome ka predictable part hata ke variance kam karta hai. Estimate unbiased rehta hai.
  • Q. Kitna fayda hoga?
    A. Variance (1 - rho^2) factor se kam hota hai. Corr jitna zyada, fayda utna bada.

Yaad rakho

Pre-period data = kam noise. Correlation 0.7 matlab lagbhag aadha sample.

Machine Learning Basics 13 topics

ML-01Supervised vs unsupervisedBasicGood to Have

Supervised learning me labelled data se prediction seekhte hain, unsupervised me bina label ke patterns dhundte hain. Business problem se type decide hota hai.

Simple me samjho

Supervised: teacher ne answers diye hain, jaise churned ya not churned. Model usse seekhta hai. Unsupervised: koi answer nahi, bas data ko khud groups ya patterns me baantna hai.

Key points

  • Supervised: Input features X aur known label y. Goal: naye data ka y predict karna.
  • Classification: Label category hai (churn yes/no, fraud yes/no).
  • Regression: Label number hai (next month revenue, LTV).
  • Unsupervised: Sirf X, koi y nahi. Clustering, anomaly detection, dimensionality reduction (PCA).
  • Business examples (supervised): Churn prediction, bot/fraud detection, deposit amount forecast.
  • Business examples (unsupervised): Player segmentation, unusual betting pattern detection, product grouping.
  • Label quality: Supervised me label ki definition sabse important hai ("churn = 30 din inactive").
  • Cost of labels: Labels kabhi mehnge hote hain (manual review). Unsupervised me ye cost nahi, par result interpret karna padta hai.
  • Others: Semi-supervised aur reinforcement learning bhi hain, par analyst ke liye mostly upar wale do kaafi hain.

Example

python
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans

# supervised: y is known (1 = churned)
clf = LogisticRegression().fit(X_train, y_train)
churn_prob = clf.predict_proba(X_new)[:, 1]

# unsupervised: no y, only features
km = KMeans(n_clusters=4, n_init=10, random_state=42).fit(X)
segments = km.labels_

Pehla model batata hai kaun churn karega. Doosra players ko 4 groups me baantta hai, par group ka naam analyst ko dena padta hai.

Common mistakes

  • Label definition vague rakhna aur model pe blame karna.
  • Clustering ko "truth" maan lena. Wo bas ek grouping hai.
  • Regression problem ko classification bana dena (thresholds se information loss).
  • Unsupervised se prediction ki ummeed karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Supervised aur unsupervised me farak?
    A. Supervised me label y hota hai aur prediction seekhte hain. Unsupervised me label nahi, structure dhundte hain.
  • Q. Churn aur segmentation kis type ke hain?
    A. Churn supervised classification hai, segmentation unsupervised clustering.

Yaad rakho

Label hai to supervised, nahi hai to unsupervised.

ML-02Train/test split and cross-validationIntermediateGood to Have

Data ko train aur test me baanto taaki model ki honest performance pata chale. Leakage se bachao, k-fold se stable estimate lo.

Simple me samjho

Exam ke questions pehle se padh ke exam doge to marks real nahi honge. Test set wo exam hai jo model ne training me kabhi nahi dekha.

Key points

  • Train/test split: Usually 80/20 ya 70/30. Model train pe seekhta hai, test pe sirf ek baar score hota hai.
  • Validation set / holdout: Hyperparameters tune karne ke liye alag hissa. Test set final check ke liye untouched.
  • Data leakage: Test ki jaankari training me aa jana. Jaise scaler poore data pe fit karna ya future data use karna.
  • Fit on train only: Scaler, imputer, encoder: pehle train pe fit, phir test pe sirf transform.
  • Stratify: Imbalanced label me stratify=y se dono splits me same class ratio rahta hai.
  • Time-based split: Time series ya player behaviour me random split galat. Past pe train, future pe test.
  • K-fold CV: Data k parts me, har baar ek part validation, baaki train. k scores ka average.
  • StratifiedKFold: Classification me class ratio fold me bhi maintain.
  • Grouped split: Same player ke multiple rows train aur test dono me na aayein (GroupKFold).

Example

python
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

X_tr, X_te, y_tr, y_te = train_test_split(
    X, y, test_size=0.2, stratify=y, random_state=42)

model = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000)
scores = cross_val_score(model, X_tr, y_tr, cv=5, scoring="roc_auc")
print(scores.mean(), scores.std())

CV sirf train data pe chalaya. 5 scores ka mean performance hai, std stability batata hai. Test set (X_te) final model ke liye reserve hai.

Common mistakes

  • Pehle pure data pe scaling/encoding, phir split (leakage).
  • Test set pe baar baar tune karna, to wo validation set ban jata hai.
  • Same player ke rows split me mix hona.
  • Temporal data me random split karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Data leakage kya hai?
    A. Jab training me aisi information aa jaye jo prediction time pe available nahi hogi, ya test data ka asar train me ho. Result jhootha achha dikhta hai.
  • Q. K-fold kyun?
    A. Ek split pe luck ka asar hota hai. K-fold me har row validation me ek baar aati hai, to estimate stable hota hai.

Yaad rakho

Split pehle, preprocessing baad me (train pe fit). Test set ek baar.

ML-03Feature engineering and encodingIntermediateGood to Have

Raw data ko model ke layak features me badalna: one-hot, scaling, imputation, aur target leakage se bachna.

Simple me samjho

Model sirf numbers samajhta hai. "Mobile" ya "Desktop" jaise text ko numbers me badalna padta hai. Achhe features aksar fancy model se zyada kaam karte hain.

Key points

  • One-hot encoding: Har category ka alag 0/1 column (device_mobile, device_desktop). Low-cardinality categorical ke liye.
  • High cardinality: 10,000 cities pe one-hot bhari ho jata hai. Frequency encoding ya grouping use karo.
  • Ordinal encoding: Jab order ho (Bronze < Silver < Gold).
  • Scaling: StandardScaler (mean 0, std 1) ya MinMaxScaler (0 se 1). Linear models, KNN, k-means ko zaroori. Tree models ko nahi.
  • Imputation: Missing values bharna: SimpleImputer(strategy="median"). Saath me missing indicator column rakho.
  • Missing meaningful ho sakta hai: "kabhi deposit nahi kiya" aur "data nahi mila" alag cheezein hain.
  • Domain features: sessions_7d, deposit_30d, days_since_last_login, ratio features.
  • Target leakage: Feature jo label ke baad ya label se banta hai. Jaise churn predict karte hue days_inactive_after_cutoff.
  • Point-in-time: Feature sirf label date se pehle ke data se bane.

Example

python
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder, StandardScaler
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline

prep = ColumnTransformer([
    ("cat", OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore"), ["device", "country"]),
    ("num", make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy="median"),
                          StandardScaler()), ["sessions_30d", "deposit_30d"]),
])
X_tr_t = prep.fit_transform(X_tr)   # fit on train
X_te_t = prep.transform(X_te)       # only transform on test

Categorical columns one-hot hue, numeric columns me median imputation aur scaling hui. handle_unknown="ignore" se test me naya category aane par error nahi aata.

Common mistakes

  • Scaler ko poore data pe fit karna.
  • Target leakage wala feature rakhna: AUC 0.99 aaye to shak karo.
  • Pehle one-hot aur phir split, jis se test ki categories ka bhi pata chal jata hai.
  • Dummy variable trap ignore karna linear models me (drop="first" use kar sakte ho).

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Target leakage ka example?
    A. Churn predict karte hue "account closed flag" feature. Wo label ke baad ya label ke saath banta hai, prediction time pe available nahi hota.
  • Q. Kab scaling zaroori hai?
    A. Distance ya gradient based models (KNN, k-means, linear/logistic with regularisation). Tree models me nahi.

Yaad rakho

Feature wahi jo prediction time pe available ho. Preprocessing train pe fit.

ML-04Regression modelsIntermediateGood to Have

Number predict karne ke models: linear regression, ridge (L2) aur lasso (L1). Regularisation se overfitting kam hota hai.

Simple me samjho

Linear regression data me best seedhi line (ya plane) fit karta hai. Ridge aur lasso us line pe "brake" lagate hain, taaki coefficients bahut bade na ho jayein.

Key points

  • Linear regression: y = b0 + b1*x1 + b2*x2 + .... Squared error minimise karta hai (OLS).
  • Coefficient meaning: x1 ek unit badhe aur baaki same rahein to y me b1 ka change.
  • Assumptions: Linear relationship, residuals ka constant variance, independence, features me bahut high correlation nahi (multicollinearity).
  • Ridge (L2): Loss me alpha * sum(b^2) jodta hai. Coefficients chhote karta hai, zero nahi.
  • Lasso (L1): Loss me alpha * sum(|b|). Kuch coefficients exact zero, to feature selection jaisa.
  • Alpha: Penalty strength. Zyada alpha = zyada simple model (underfit ka risk). CV se choose karo (RidgeCV, LassoCV).
  • Scaling zaroori: Regularisation me features same scale pe hone chahiye.
  • Correlated features: Ridge unhe saath me handle karta hai, lasso ek ko chunta hai.
  • Outliers: Linear regression outliers se bahut affect hota hai. Check karo.

Example

python
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression, Ridge, Lasso
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

ridge = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), Ridge(alpha=1.0)).fit(X_tr, y_tr)
lasso = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), Lasso(alpha=0.1)).fit(X_tr, y_tr)

print(lasso[-1].coef_)        # some entries exactly 0.0
print(ridge.score(X_te, y_te))  # R^2 on test

Lasso ke kuch coefficients 0.0 aayenge, matlab wo features hat gaye. score regression me R^2 deta hai (1 best, 0 mean prediction ke barabar).

Common mistakes

  • Bina scaling ke ridge/lasso chalana.
  • Coefficient ko causal effect samajhna.
  • Alpha ko guess karna, CV na karna.
  • Sirf train R^2 dekhna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Ridge vs lasso?
    A. Ridge L2 penalty se coefficients chhote karta hai, lasso L1 se kuch ko zero kar deta hai. Lasso feature selection me kaam aata hai.
  • Q. Regularisation kyun?
    A. Model complexity kam karke overfitting rokne ke liye.

Yaad rakho

Linear = simple baseline. Overfit ho to ridge/lasso, aur scale karo.

ML-05Classification modelsIntermediateGood to Have

Category predict karne ke models: logistic regression, decision tree, random forest aur gradient boosting. Simple se start karo.

Simple me samjho

Classification me answer yes/no ya category hota hai, jaise player churn karega ya nahi. Logistic simple aur explainable hai. Trees aur boosting complex patterns pakadte hain.

Key points

  • Logistic regression: Linear score ko sigmoid se probability (0 se 1) me badalta hai. Default threshold 0.5. Coefficients explainable.
  • Odds ratio: Logistic ka exp(coef) odds ka multiplier batata hai.
  • Decision tree: If-else splits ka tree. Easy to explain, par deep tree overfit karta hai. max_depth, min_samples_leaf se control.
  • Random forest: Bahut saare trees, har ek data aur features ke random subset pe (bagging). Votes ka average. Kam variance.
  • Gradient boosting: Trees ek ke baad ek, har naya tree pichhle ki galtiyan sudharta hai. Tabular data pe aksar best. XGBoost, LightGBM isi family ke hain.
  • Tuning: Boosting me n_estimators, learning_rate, max_depth important. Overfit ka risk zyada.
  • Class imbalance: Churn 5% ho to class_weight="balanced" ya threshold tuning. Accuracy par mat jao.
  • Probability vs label: predict_proba se probability, threshold business cost se choose karo.
  • Trade-off: Complex model = accuracy shayad zyada, par explain aur maintain mushkil.

Example

python
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier, GradientBoostingClassifier

models = {
    "logit": LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, class_weight="balanced"),
    "rf":    RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=200, min_samples_leaf=5, random_state=42),
    "gb":    GradientBoostingClassifier(random_state=42),
}
for name, m in models.items():
    m.fit(X_tr, y_tr)
    print(name, m.score(X_te, y_te))

Teen models ek hi data pe compare hue. Pehle logistic baseline lo, phir check karo ki trees se kitna fayda mila.

Common mistakes

  • Seedha complex model chala dena, baseline ke bina.
  • Imbalanced data me accuracy dekhna.
  • Bina depth limit ke decision tree.
  • Default threshold 0.5 ko hi final maan lena.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Random forest vs gradient boosting?
    A. RF parallel independent trees ka average (variance kam). Boosting sequential trees jo errors sudharte hain (bias kam), par tune karna zaroori.
  • Q. Logistic regression kab?
    A. Jab explainability aur simple baseline chahiye, ya data kam ho.

Yaad rakho

Logistic se shuru karo. Trees tabhi jab fayda dikhe.

ML-06Evaluation metricsIntermediateGood to Have

Model ki quality naapne ke metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, confusion matrix, aur regression ke liye RMSE, MAE.

Simple me samjho

Accuracy akela dhoka de sakti hai. 100 me 5 fraud hain, "sab theek" bolne wala model 95% accurate hai par bekaar. Isliye problem ke hisaab se metric chuno.

Key points

  • Confusion matrix: TP, FP, FN, TN ka table.
  • Accuracy: (TP + TN) / total. Imbalanced data me misleading.
  • Precision: TP / (TP + FP). Jitne ko positive bola, unme kitne sahi.
  • Recall: TP / (TP + FN). Jitne asli positive the, unme kitne pakde.
  • F1: Precision aur recall ka harmonic mean: 2PR / (P + R).
  • ROC-AUC: Threshold ke bina ranking quality. 0.5 = random, 1.0 = perfect. Meaning: random positive ka score random negative se zyada hone ki probability.
  • Kab kya: Fraud/bot me recall important (miss mehnga). Promo targeting me precision (waste mehnga).
  • RMSE: sqrt(mean(error^2)). Bade errors ko zyada penalise karta hai.
  • MAE: mean(|error|). Outliers se kam affect, samajhne me easy.

Example

Bot detection, 1,000 accounts: TP = 80, FP = 20, FN = 40, TN = 860.

Pred botPred human
Actual bot8040
Actual human20860
python
from sklearn.metrics import (confusion_matrix, precision_score,
                             recall_score, f1_score, roc_auc_score)
# acc = (80+860)/1000 = 0.94, precision = 80/100 = 0.80
# recall = 80/120 = 0.667, f1 = 0.727

Accuracy 94% achhi dikhti hai, par "sabko human bolo" wala model bhi 880/1000 = 88% deta hai. Recall 66.7% batata hai ki 1/3 bots miss hue. Regression errors 2, -1, 0, 5: MAE = 8/4 = 2.0, RMSE = sqrt(30/4) = 2.74. RMSE bada kyunki 5 wala error zyada penalise hua.

Common mistakes

  • Imbalanced data me sirf accuracy.
  • Threshold ke bina precision/recall compare karna.
  • ROC-AUC ko hi sab kuch samajhna jab positive class bahut rare ho (PR curve bhi dekho).
  • Regression me sirf RMSE ya sirf MAE dekhna. Outliers ka asar dekhne ke liye dono dekho.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Precision vs recall?
    A. Precision: predicted positives me sahi kitne. Recall: actual positives me se kitne pakde. Dono ka trade-off threshold se control hota hai.
  • Q. ROC-AUC kya batata hai?
    A. Model positives ko negatives se upar rank karne me kitna achha hai, sab thresholds par.

Yaad rakho

Business cost se metric chuno. Imbalance me accuracy nahi.

ML-07Overfitting and bias-varianceIntermediateGood to Have

Overfit model train data ratta maar leta hai aur naye data pe fail hota hai. Pehchano aur regularisation, simple model ya zyada data se sudharo.

Simple me samjho

Student sirf pichhle saal ke papers ratta maare to naye questions pe fail hoga. Model bhi train data ratta maar sakta hai, par naye data par kamzor rahega.

Key points

  • Overfitting: Train score bahut achha, test score kaafi kam (e.g. train 98%, test 78%).
  • Underfitting: Dono scores kharab. Model bahut simple.
  • Bias: Galat assumptions se systematic error (underfit).
  • Variance: Data me chhote badlav se model bahut badalna (overfit).
  • Trade-off: Complexity badhao to bias kam, variance zyada. Sweet spot chahiye.
  • Spot karna: Train vs validation score gap, learning curves, CV score.
  • Regularisation: Ridge/lasso penalty, tree me max_depth, min_samples_leaf.
  • More data / fewer features: Noise wale features hatao, data badhao.
  • Early stopping & ensembles: Boosting me early stopping, random forest averaging.
  • Cross-validation: Hyperparameter tuning CV se, test set se nahi.

Example

python
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier

for d in [2, 5, None]:
    t = DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=d, random_state=42).fit(X_tr, y_tr)
    print(d, round(t.score(X_tr, y_tr), 2), round(t.score(X_te, y_te), 2))
# 2    0.80  0.79   -> underfit (high bias)
# 5    0.88  0.85   -> good balance
# None 1.00  0.76   -> overfit (high variance)

Illustrative numbers: unlimited depth tree train pe 100% par test me gir gaya. Depth 5 par gap chhota aur test best.

Common mistakes

  • Sirf train accuracy dekh ke khush ho jana.
  • Test set pe baar baar tune karna (indirect overfit).
  • Bahut zyada features, kam rows.
  • Underfitting ko overfitting samajhkar aur complexity ghata dena.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Overfitting kaise pehchante ho?
    A. Train aur validation/test score me bada gap. Learning curve me validation flat ya girta hua.
  • Q. Bias-variance trade-off?
    A. Simple model me high bias, low variance. Complex me low bias, high variance. Dono ka balance chahiye.

Yaad rakho

Train bahut achha aur test kharab = overfit. Simple karo, regularise karo, data badhao.

ML-08ClusteringIntermediateGood to Have

Clustering bina label ke similar rows ke groups banata hai: k-means, hierarchical, aur silhouette score se quality check.

Simple me samjho

Players ko unke behaviour se groups me baantna: casual, regular, high-roller. Kisi ne group ka naam nahi diya, model sirf similar players ko saath rakhta hai.

Key points

  • K-means: k centroids choose karta hai, har point nearest centroid ko, phir centroid update. Repeat jab tak stable.
  • k choose karna: Elbow method (inertia vs k) aur silhouette score.
  • Scaling zaroori: Distance based hai, to StandardScaler pehle lagao.
  • Initialisation: n_init=10, random_state fix karo, kyunki result initialisation pe depend karta hai.
  • Hierarchical (agglomerative): Har point alag cluster se shuru, closest clusters merge hote jate hain. Dendrogram se structure dikhta hai.
  • Linkage: ward, average, complete. Ward commonly use hota hai.
  • Silhouette score: (b - a) / max(a, b). a = apne cluster ka average distance, b = nearest doosre cluster ka. -1 se 1; 1 ke paas achha.
  • Limitations: K-means round, similar size clusters assume karta hai. Outliers se affect.
  • Interpretation: Cluster profile banao (average sessions, buy-in) aur business naam do.

Example

python
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.metrics import silhouette_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

Xs = StandardScaler().fit_transform(X)   # sessions_per_week, avg_buyin, ...
for k in range(2, 7):
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=k, n_init=10, random_state=42).fit(Xs)
    print(k, round(silhouette_score(Xs, km.labels_), 3))

Jis k pe silhouette sabse zyada ho, wo achha candidate hai. Ek point ka a = 2 aur b = 5 ho to silhouette = (5 - 2) / 5 = 0.6, yani achha cluster fit.

Common mistakes

  • Scaling ke bina features ka alag unit hona.
  • Silhouette ke bina k guess karna.
  • Cluster ko real segment maan lena bina business check ke.
  • Categorical features pe seedha k-means lagana.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. K-means me k kaise choose karte ho?
    A. Elbow aur silhouette score dekhte hain, saath me business ke liye cluster interpretable ho.
  • Q. K-means vs hierarchical?
    A. K-means fast hai par k pehle batana padta hai. Hierarchical me k baad me dendrogram se, par bade data pe slow.

Yaad rakho

Scale karo, silhouette se k choose karo, aur clusters ko business naam do.

ML-09scikit-learn workflowIntermediateGood to Have

scikit-learn me pipelines, fit/transform/predict ka pattern aur model save karna. Preprocessing aur model ek saath, leakage se safe.

Simple me samjho

Pipeline ek assembly line hai: imputer, encoder, scaler, model sab ek chain me. Ek fit aur ek predict se poori chain chalti hai.

Key points

  • Estimator API: Har object me fit(X, y). Transformers me transform(X), models me predict(X).
  • fit_transform: Train pe fit + transform ek saath. Test pe sirf transform.
  • Pipeline: Steps ka chain: Pipeline([("prep", prep), ("model", model)]). Last step model hota hai.
  • ColumnTransformer: Alag columns pe alag preprocessing.
  • Leakage safe: Pipeline ko CV me daalo, to har fold me preprocessing sirf train fold pe fit hota hai.
  • Hyperparameter search: GridSearchCV(pipe, {"model__C": [0.1, 1, 10]}, cv=5). Step name + double underscore.
  • Save model: joblib.dump(pipe, "model.joblib") aur joblib.load.
  • Security: Joblib/pickle file sirf trusted source se load karo (code execute ho sakta hai).
  • Versioning: Save karte time scikit-learn version, feature list aur training date likho.
  • Reproducibility: random_state fix.

Example

python
import joblib
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

pipe = Pipeline([("prep", prep),
                 ("model", LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000))])
pipe.fit(X_tr, y_tr)                       # prep.fit + model.fit
print(pipe.predict_proba(X_te)[:5, 1])     # prep.transform + model

joblib.dump(pipe, "churn_model.joblib")
pipe2 = joblib.load("churn_model.joblib")  # later / in another script

prep wahi ColumnTransformer hai jo ML-03 me bana tha. Pipeline save karne se preprocessing bhi model ke saath save hota hai, to deployment me mismatch nahi hota.

Common mistakes

  • Preprocessing alag aur model alag save karna.
  • Test data pe fit_transform chalana.
  • Column order/names alag hone par predict karna.
  • Untrusted joblib/pickle file load karna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. Pipeline kyun?
    A. Preprocessing aur model ek object me, CV me leakage nahi, aur deployment simple.
  • Q. fit vs transform vs predict?
    A. fit seekhta hai, transform data badalta hai, predict model se output deta hai.

Yaad rakho

Sab kuch Pipeline me. Train pe fit, test pe transform/predict.

ML-10Model interpretationAdvancedBonus

Model ne kya seekha: feature importance aur SHAP basics se samjhao kaun se features prediction ko kitna push karte hain.

Simple me samjho

Stakeholder pucha: "Ye player churn kyun karega?" Sirf probability nahi, wajah bhi batani hoti hai. Interpretation wahi wajah dikhata hai.

Key points

  • Linear/logistic coefficients: Direction aur size batate hain (scaled features pe compare karo).
  • Tree feature importance: feature_importances_ (impurity based). Fast, par high-cardinality/numeric features ki taraf biased ho sakta hai.
  • Permutation importance: Ek feature shuffle karo aur score kitna girta hai dekho. sklearn.inspection.permutation_importance. Test/validation data pe chalao.
  • SHAP: Har prediction ke liye har feature ka contribution. Game theory (Shapley values) pe based.
  • Additive: base value + sum(SHAP values) = model ka output us row ke liye.
  • Global vs local: Poore data pe average |SHAP| = global importance. Ek row ka SHAP = local explanation.
  • Plots: Summary/beeswarm plot, bar plot, waterfall plot (ek row).
  • Correlated features: Importance unme baant jati hai, interpret carefully.
  • Causation nahi: Importance = model ne kya use kiya, ye nahi ki feature badalne se outcome badlega.

Example

python
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor
from sklearn.inspection import permutation_importance
import shap

rf = RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=200, random_state=42).fit(X_tr, y_tr)

r = permutation_importance(rf, X_te, y_te, n_repeats=10, random_state=42)
print(sorted(zip(r.importances_mean, X_te.columns), reverse=True)[:5])

explainer = shap.TreeExplainer(rf)
sv = explainer(X_te)
shap.plots.beeswarm(sv)

Pehle permutation importance se top features, phir SHAP se samjho ki high ya low value prediction ko upar ya neeche push karti hai. SHAP ke liye shap library alag install karni padti hai.

Common mistakes

  • Impurity importance ko final truth maan lena.
  • Train data pe permutation importance chalana.
  • Importance ko causal impact bolna.
  • Correlated features ka importance alag alag padhna.

Interview Q&A

  • Q. SHAP kya hai?
    A. Har prediction me har feature ka contribution batata hai, Shapley values se. Sab contributions + base value = prediction.
  • Q. Permutation vs tree importance?
    A. Permutation model-agnostic hai aur held-out data pe score girne se naapta hai. Tree importance training splits se aata hai aur biased ho sakta hai.

Yaad rakho

Importance = model ka behaviour, causation nahi. Test data pe check karo.

ML-11When not to use MLBasicGood to Have

Har problem ke liye ML nahi chahiye. Pehle rules aur baseline, kyunki model banana aasan hai par maintain karna mehnga.

Simple me samjho

Chhote kaam ke liye JCB mat bulao, kudal kaafi hai. Pehle simple rule try karo. Agar wo kaam kar jaye to ML ki zarurat nahi.

Key points

  • Rules first: "14 din se login nahi kiya = churn risk" jaise rules SQL me ban jate hain.
  • Baseline: Simple method (rule, average, last month ka number) se compare karo. ML ko isse clear jeetna chahiye.
  • Kam data: Few hundred rows ya rare events me ML unreliable hota hai.
  • Explainability: Compliance ya business ko reason chahiye to rule/logistic better.
  • Maintenance cost: Pipeline, retraining, monitoring, data drift, on-call, documentation.
  • Data drift: Player behaviour badalta hai, model purana ho jata hai.
  • Label nahi ya ganda: Label quality kharab ho to model bhi kharab.
  • Value check: Improvement ka rupaye me value > build + maintain cost?
  • Alternative: Dashboard, threshold alert, ya A/B test kabhi zyada useful.

Example

Churn targeting:

ApproachRecallPrecisionCost
Rule: 14 din inactive60%40%1 SQL query
ML model65%42%pipeline + retrain + monitoring

Sirf 5 point recall aur 2 point precision ka fayda hai (illustrative numbers). Maintenance cost dekhte hue rule se shuru karna aur baad me ML par jana better ho sakta hai.

Common mistakes

  • "ML kar do" bina business sawal ke.
